intro:
Swap USDC from Ethereum to USDT on BNB Chain. Traders who need Tether on chain 56 send Circle USDC from Ethereum and receive BSC-USD.

This page is for a BNB Chain wallet that must hold Tether. A mainnet pool is the right tool when you only want to rotate Circle dollars into Tether on Ethereum, because that book already exists. You approve 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan. You receive 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955, which BscScan lists as BSC-USD. That token uses 18 decimals. Circle USDC on Ethereum uses 6. Gas to send is ETH on chain id 1, where blocks land about every 12 seconds. Switch the receiving wallet to chain id 56 before you look for BSC-USD.
description: Swap USDC from Ethereum to USDT on BNB Chain when a chain 56 wallet needs Tether and you already hold Circle USDC on Ethereum mainnet before you approve.

sections.heading: When the Ethereum stable pool is enough
sections.body: Circle USDC and Tether already trade on Ethereum. This route is the wrong tool for that rotation. Open it when the dollars have to become BSC-USD, the Tether contract on BNB Chain. A same-chain swap never creates 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955.

sections.heading: BSC-USD uses 18 decimals
sections.body: Read 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BscScan before you size the next transfer. Wallets that assume 6 decimals, the Ethereum USDT habit, misread the balance. The source you approve is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan, Circle's USDC, and the unspent remainder stays on mainnet.

sections.heading: ETH gas, then a BNB balance
sections.body: Chain id 1 charges ETH, and a block is about 12 seconds. Chain id 56 charges BNB, and a block is about 3 seconds. This output is USDT, so it does not pay the next BNB Chain transaction. [BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) is where that gas token lives. Keep a little BNB on the receiving wallet.

sections.heading: Who spends BSC-USD
sections.body: Books on chain 56 usually quote BNB pairs against this Tether. The route fits someone funding that wallet, a payment that must arrive as USDT, or a position that settles on BNB Chain. Circle does not custody the destination token. You hold Tether's BSC-USD.

faqs.question: Why does the USDT balance look huge or tiny on BNB Chain?
faqs.answer: BSC-USD at 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 uses 18 decimals. Circle USDC on Ethereum uses 6, and Ethereum Tether uses 6. A wallet pointed at the wrong decimal count will shift the displayed amount by many zeros. Open the contract on BscScan and read the decimals field before you send it onward.

faqs.question: Can I pay the BNB Chain fee with the USDT I receive?
faqs.answer: The received token is Tether, an ERC-20. Gas on chain id 56 is BNB. If the destination wallet has no BNB, the USDT can sit there until you add gas. Fund a small BNB balance, or choose a route whose output is native BNB, before you plan a second transaction on that chain.

faqs.question: Is this the same trade as USDC to USDT on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: The tickers look alike and the job is different. On Ethereum you would swap Circle USDC for Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. This route spends the Ethereum USDC contract and delivers BSC-USD on BNB Chain. Use it when that destination contract is the balance you need.

intro:
Swap USDC from Ethereum to ETH on BNB Chain. A chain 56 wallet that wants Binance-Peg ETH spends Circle USDC on Ethereum to receive it.

The ETH in the title is an ERC-20 on BNB Chain, contract 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8, which you check on BscScan. It is Binance-Peg ETH. It does not pay gas on BNB Chain, and it is a different asset from native ETH on Ethereum. You spend Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, visible on Etherscan. Ethereum is chain id 1 and still needs a little native ETH for gas. Blocks there are about 12 seconds.
description: Swap USDC from Ethereum to ETH on BNB Chain if you want Binance-Peg ETH on chain 56 and you are spending Circle USDC you already hold on Ethereum mainnet.

sections.heading: Pegged ETH does not pay BNB gas
sections.body: After this route you hold 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. Transfers of that token still cost BNB. If the wallet has never held BNB, the pegged ETH can arrive and then sit. Native ETH on Ethereum, the 0xEeee placeholder, is what you use for mainnet gas, and this route does not leave that balance in place of the USDC you spent.

sections.heading: Match USDC on Etherscan first
sections.body: Approve only 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. That is Circle USDC on Ethereum, 6 decimals. The output uses 18 decimals, which is normal for Binance-Peg ETH on BscScan. A copy that shares the ETH ticker and a different address is a different market.

sections.heading: Skip this if you want ETH on Ethereum
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when you want native ETH, or WETH, to stay on mainnet. Selling USDC for ETH on Ethereum never mints 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. Use the bridge when a BNB Chain app asks for Binance-Peg ETH specifically. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the general mechanic. This page is only the USDC to pegged ETH pair.

sections.heading: What the pegged token is used for
sections.body: BNB Chain pools that say ETH usually mean this Binance-Peg contract. Receiving it lets you enter those books without first holding BNB as the trade asset. You still need BNB for the network fee. Chain id 56 blocks are about 3 seconds once the destination transaction is in.

faqs.question: Is the ETH I receive the same ETH that pays Ethereum gas?
faqs.answer: No. Gas on Ethereum is native ETH. The token this route delivers is Binance-Peg ETH at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on BscScan. It is an ERC-20 on chain id 56. You cannot use it to pay mainnet gas, and you cannot use it to pay BNB Chain gas either.

faqs.question: Which USDC contract do I approve?
faqs.answer: Approve Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan. Binance-Peg USDC on BNB Chain is a different address and is not the token you send. You also need a small native ETH balance on Ethereum, chain id 1, because the approval and the send charge ETH gas.

faqs.question: What if I only wanted to buy ETH with USDC?
faqs.answer: Buy it on Ethereum if the ETH should remain mainnet gas or mainnet WETH. This route is the wrong tool for that. It spends Circle USDC and delivers Binance-Peg ETH on BNB Chain. Open it when a chain 56 pool or transfer asks for that pegged contract.

intro:
Swap USDC from Ethereum to BNB on BNB Chain. People who need native gas on chain 56 spend Circle USDC on Ethereum and receive BNB.

The output address is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. On this route that placeholder means native BNB, the gas coin of chain id 56, which you can see as BNB on BscScan rather than as an ERC-20 you approve. You send Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan. Keep some ETH on Ethereum for the send. Mainnet blocks are about 12 seconds. BNB Chain blocks are about 3 seconds. Chain id 56 is the network that holds the BNB.
description: Swap USDC from Ethereum to BNB on BNB Chain when a chain 56 wallet needs native gas and you will spend Circle USDC held on Ethereum mainnet before you sign.

sections.heading: Native BNB is the 0xEeee placeholder
sections.body: You do not approve an ERC-20 on the destination side. 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE stands in for the chain's gas coin. Here that coin is BNB. The same placeholder on an Ethereum route would mean native ETH. Chain id is what tells them apart.

sections.heading: Why someone spends USDC for BNB
sections.body: A new BNB Chain wallet can hold tokens and still be stuck, because every transfer costs BNB. This route turns Circle dollars you already have on Ethereum into that gas coin. It is a poor fit when you wanted a stable balance to remain a stable balance on chain 56.

sections.heading: The USDC contract you approve
sections.body: The source contract is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, Circle USDC, 6 decimals, on Etherscan. Binance-Peg USDC at 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d is a BNB Chain token and is not what leaves your Ethereum wallet. You still pay ETH gas on chain id 1 to move the USDC.

sections.heading: When to swap on Ethereum instead
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool if you want more USDC, USDT, or ETH on mainnet. Those books are already on Ethereum. Bridging into BNB only helps when the next transaction has to be signed on chain 56. The [guide to bridging assets](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) covers the wallet steps. This pair is USDC in, native BNB out.

faqs.question: Do I approve a BNB token contract on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: You approve Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. Native BNB is not an Ethereum ERC-20. The output is marked with 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which means the gas coin of the destination chain. On BNB Chain that gas coin is BNB, and BscScan shows it as the native balance.

faqs.question: Will the BNB I receive pay for the next chain 56 transaction?
faqs.answer: Yes. Native BNB is the gas token on chain id 56. That is the reason to pick this output instead of BSC-USD or Binance-Peg ETH. Leave enough BNB unspent for the next approval or swap. The route still needs ETH on Ethereum before the USDC can move.

faqs.question: Is buying BNB on a mainnet pool the same thing?
faqs.answer: A token that merely uses the BNB ticker on Ethereum is a different contract, and it will not pay gas on chain 56. This route is the one that delivers native BNB. Skip it when your next trade is still on Ethereum. Mainnet gas remains ETH either way.

intro:
Swap USDT from Ethereum to USDC on BNB Chain. Wallets that need Binance-Peg USDC spend Ethereum Tether and receive that dollar on chain 56.

You send Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, the 6 decimal USDT on Etherscan. You receive 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d, Binance-Peg USDC on BscScan, which uses 18 decimals. It is a pegged dollar on chain 56, and it is a different contract from Circle USDC on Ethereum. Gas for the send is ETH on chain id 1. Blocks there take about 12 seconds. BNB Chain, chain id 56, then charges BNB. Open BscScan on the pegged USDC and confirm the name before you send it to an app.
description: Swap USDT from Ethereum to USDC on BNB Chain when you need Binance-Peg dollars on chain 56 and you already hold Tether on Ethereum mainnet before you sign.

sections.heading: Two dollars, two issuers, two chains
sections.body: Tether's Ethereum contract is what you spend. Circle is the name people associate with USDC, and on Ethereum that contract is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. This route does not deliver that contract. It delivers Binance-Peg USDC. If a chain 56 app has whitelisted 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d, this is the matching output.

sections.heading: Decimals jump from 6 to 18
sections.body: Ethereum USDT shows 6 decimals on Etherscan. The received pegged USDC shows 18 on BscScan. Import 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d with the explorer's decimals, or the wallet will invent a balance. The source approval is only for 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7.

sections.heading: Stay on Ethereum to flip USDT into Circle USDC
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when both legs should remain on mainnet. USDT and Circle USDC already have deep books there. Bridging is justified when the dollar you need is the BNB Chain peg. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is where the Tether starts, and where the ETH gas is paid.

sections.heading: BNB still has to be in the wallet
sections.body: Pegged USDC does not pay gas on chain id 56. After it arrives you need BNB for the next move, and blocks on BNB Chain are about 3 seconds. If the wallet is empty of BNB, add gas before you try to spend the new dollars.

faqs.question: Is Binance-Peg USDC the same token as Circle USDC on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: They share a ticker and they are different contracts. Circle USDC on Ethereum is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. This route pays 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d on BscScan. Check the app you are funding. If it wants Ethereum USDC, this route delivers the wrong chain and the wrong address.

faqs.question: Which token do I approve on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: Approve Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan. USDT on Ethereum often needs a fresh approval because the contract does not support the newer approval pattern. Keep ETH in the same wallet for gas on chain id 1. The USDT itself cannot pay that fee.

faqs.question: What if the chain 56 app wants BSC-USD instead?
faqs.answer: BSC-USD is Tether on BNB Chain, at 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955. This route pays Binance-Peg USDC. If the app's allowlist is the Tether contract, switch to a route that outputs that address. Sending the wrong stable into a pool will not credit you.

intro:
Swap USDT from Ethereum to ETH on BNB Chain. Traders seeking ETH exposure on BNB Chain spend Tether from Ethereum and receive Binance-Peg ETH.

The asset that arrives is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on BscScan, Binance-Peg ETH, an ERC-20. It is not native ETH and it will not pay gas on either chain. You spend Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan. Ethereum gas is ETH, chain id 1, with blocks around 12 seconds. Once you are on chain 56, gas is BNB and blocks are about 3 seconds. Confirm the peg on BscScan before you trade it.
description: Swap USDT from Ethereum to ETH on BNB Chain when you want Binance-Peg ETH on chain 56 and you are spending Tether you already hold on Ethereum mainnet.

sections.heading: Tether leaves, pegged ETH arrives
sections.body: Confirm the spend on Etherscan at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 before you sign the approval. Confirm the receipt on BscScan at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. Those two strings are the whole pair. A Binance-Peg ETH copy with a similar name and a different address is not this output.

sections.heading: You still need two gas coins
sections.body: USDT cannot pay Ethereum gas, so the sending wallet needs ETH. Pegged ETH cannot pay BNB Chain gas, so the receiving wallet needs BNB. This route supplies neither gas coin. If you needed BNB itself, the output address would be the 0xEeee native placeholder.

sections.heading: Buying ETH on Ethereum is a different job
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when the ETH you want is mainnet gas or mainnet WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. A Uniswap trade of Tether for ETH stays on chain id 1. Use this page when a BNB Chain pool is priced in Binance-Peg ETH. See [how cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) for the split between the two networks.

sections.heading: Where pegged ETH gets used
sections.body: Chain 56 exchanges list ETH pairs against this contract. Landing 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 lets you join those pairs from a Tether balance that started on Ethereum. You are holding a pegged ERC-20, and the price you accept is the quote you sign, which this page does not set.

faqs.question: Does Binance-Peg ETH show up as native ETH in my wallet?
faqs.answer: It shows up as an ERC-20 once the wallet is on BNB Chain and you import 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. Native ETH is the gas balance on Ethereum. If your wallet is still set to chain id 1, you will not see the pegged token in the native ETH line. Switch the network to chain id 56 and check BscScan.

faqs.question: Why does the Ethereum side ask for ETH if I am spending USDT?
faqs.answer: Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is an ERC-20. Moving it costs ETH gas on chain id 1. The approval is a separate transaction from the swap, and both need ETH. A wallet that holds only USDT cannot finish this route until a little ETH is added.

faqs.question: When should I refuse this route?
faqs.answer: Refuse it when you want native ETH on Ethereum, WETH on Ethereum, or native BNB for gas. This pair spends Ethereum Tether and delivers Binance-Peg ETH only. If the pool you care about is already on mainnet, trade there and skip the second chain.

intro:
Swap USDT from Ethereum to BNB on BNB Chain. A BNB Chain wallet short of gas spends Ethereum Tether and receives native BNB.

Native BNB is represented by 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on the destination side. That is the gas coin on chain id 56, shown on BscScan as BNB, not as a token you add by contract. The token you approve is Tether, 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, on Etherscan. You need ETH beside it for mainnet gas. Ethereum blocks are about 12 seconds. BNB Chain blocks are about 3 seconds. If the wallet is still on Ethereum you will not see native BNB in the gas line. Switch to chain id 56 and read the address on BscScan.
description: Swap USDT from Ethereum to BNB on BNB Chain when a chain 56 wallet needs native BNB gas and you will spend Tether held on Ethereum mainnet before you sign.

sections.heading: Gas on chain 56 is the point
sections.body: People open this pair because a BNB Chain wallet cannot move USDT, pegged ETH, or anything else until it holds BNB. Receiving native BNB fixes that. Receiving BSC-USD would not. The output marker 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is how the route names that native coin.

sections.heading: The Tether contract you send
sections.body: Spend 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 only. That is Ethereum USDT on Etherscan, 6 decimals. BSC-USD at 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 is already on BNB Chain and is not the input. If your Tether is already on chain 56, you want a same-chain swap into BNB, and this bridge is the wrong tool.

sections.heading: ETH pays for the departure
sections.body: Chain id 1 takes ETH for the approval and the bridge send. Tether does not substitute. Keep a little ETH after you decide the amount, or the last transaction stalls. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is the network you sign on first.

sections.heading: What to do with the BNB
sections.body: Use the received BNB for gas, or as the quote asset in a chain 56 pool. It is the native balance, so you do not import an ERC-20 to see it. Switch the wallet to BNB Chain, chain id 56, and read the BNB line on BscScan.

faqs.question: I already hold USDT on BNB Chain. Should I use this page?
faqs.answer: No. This page starts from Ethereum Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. USDT that already sits at 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 can be swapped for BNB on BNB Chain. Bridging again would send a mainnet balance you may not be trying to move. Use a same-chain swap in that case.

faqs.question: Is the 0xEeee address a real BNB contract I should import?
faqs.answer: Do not import 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE as a custom ERC-20. It is a placeholder for the native gas coin. On this route the coin is BNB. Your wallet shows it as the native balance once you are on chain id 56. BscScan shows the same balance on the address page.

faqs.question: What else must be in the Ethereum wallet?
faqs.answer: Tether plus ETH. The USDT contract cannot pay gas on chain id 1. Blocks there are about 12 seconds, and the approval may be its own transaction. If you have USDT and no ETH, buy or transfer a small ETH amount before you open this route.

intro:
Swap DAI from Ethereum to USDC on BNB Chain. Holders leaving Maker DAI for a chain 56 dollar spend DAI and receive Binance-Peg USDC.

DAI on Ethereum is Maker's collateral-backed dollar at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F, 18 decimals, on Etherscan. The dollar you receive is 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d on BscScan, Binance-Peg USDC, also 18 decimals on that chain. It is not Circle's Ethereum USDC. You pay ETH gas on chain id 1. BNB Chain then asks for BNB. Mainnet blocks are about 12 seconds, and chain 56 blocks are about 3 seconds. Read the receiving app's allowlist before you deposit. A whitelist for BSC-USD will ignore this pegged USDC, and a whitelist for Ethereum USDC is on the wrong chain entirely.
description: Swap DAI from Ethereum to USDC on BNB Chain when you are leaving Maker DAI for Binance-Peg dollars that must sit on chain 56 for a payment you must send.

sections.heading: Maker DAI is the token that leaves
sections.body: Approve 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F and nothing that merely prints the DAI ticker. Etherscan is the check. DAI is an ERC-20, so the wallet also needs ETH for gas. If your goal is still a Maker dollar on Ethereum, this route is the wrong tool.

sections.heading: The received dollar is pegged USDC
sections.body: BscScan should show 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d after the route. That is the Binance-Peg USDC apps on chain 56 usually mean. Circle USDC on Ethereum, 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, stays a mainnet contract and is not the balance you gain.

sections.heading: A DAI to USDC swap on mainnet stays home
sections.body: Ethereum already pairs Maker DAI with Circle USDC. Use that pool when both tokens should remain on chain id 1. Cross to BNB Chain only when the receiving app wants the pegged contract. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is the step outline. The pair here is specific: DAI in, pegged USDC out.

sections.heading: Gas after the dollar arrives
sections.body: Binance-Peg USDC cannot pay BNB Chain fees. Keep BNB on the destination wallet or the new dollars wait. Chain id 56 is fast, about 3 seconds a block, and that speed does not replace the gas coin.

faqs.question: Does this route give me Circle USDC on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: It spends Maker DAI and it does not pay Circle's Ethereum USDC. The output is Binance-Peg USDC at 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d on BscScan. Circle's contract, 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, is the mainnet token. If that is the balance you wanted, trade DAI for it on Ethereum.

faqs.question: Are the decimals the same on both sides?
faqs.answer: Maker DAI uses 18 decimals, and Binance-Peg USDC on BNB Chain also uses 18. That match is convenient and it is not a match of contracts. Still read both token pages, Etherscan for 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F and BscScan for the pegged USDC, before you move the funds onward.

faqs.question: Why is ETH required to send a stablecoin?
faqs.answer: DAI is an ERC-20 on Ethereum, chain id 1. Every approval and transfer of it burns a little ETH as gas. Blocks are about 12 seconds. The destination fee is separate and is paid in BNB. Holding only DAI on either chain is not enough to finish both steps.

intro:
Swap DAI from Ethereum to USDT on BNB Chain. Someone who must pay Tether on chain 56 can spend Maker DAI from Ethereum to get BSC-USD.

You approve Maker DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Etherscan. You receive Tether's BSC-USD at 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BscScan. Both use 18 decimals, which hides the fact that they are different issuers on different chains. Ethereum USDT, 6 decimals at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, is not the output. Gas to leave is ETH on chain id 1. Payees on Ethereum who asked for 6 decimal Tether will not see this balance. They need the mainnet contract, and this route never touches it at all.
description: Swap DAI from Ethereum to USDT on BNB Chain when a chain 56 wallet needs Tether and the source balance is Maker DAI sitting on Ethereum mainnet before you sign.

sections.heading: BSC-USD is the Tether you are buying
sections.body: The contract to expect is 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955. BscScan names it BSC-USD. Wallets often label it USDT. If a counterparty sent you an Ethereum USDT address instead, stop. That address lives on Etherscan and this route will not credit it.

sections.heading: DAI stays a Maker token until you sign
sections.body: 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F is the collateral dollar from Maker. Approving it lets the route spend that contract only. A same-chain swap into Ethereum Tether is the right tool when the payee is on mainnet. This bridge is the wrong tool for that payee.

sections.heading: Block times on the two networks
sections.body: Ethereum, chain id 1, adds blocks about every 12 seconds and charges ETH. BNB Chain, chain id 56, adds blocks about every 3 seconds and charges BNB. [BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) will not move the received USDT until the wallet holds BNB. The Tether you receive does not replace that gas coin.

sections.heading: Why the decimals can fool you
sections.body: Both ends show 18 decimals, so the unit count can look familiar. The issuers do not match: Maker on the way out, Tether on the way in. Read the token symbol and the full address on BscScan before you forward the funds to someone who asked for USDT.

faqs.question: Will my Ethereum USDT balance increase?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum Tether stays at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 and this route does not mint into it. The new balance is BSC-USD at 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BNB Chain. Look for it on BscScan after you switch the wallet to chain id 56 and refresh the token list.

faqs.question: What do I approve, and what pays the fee?
faqs.answer: Approve Maker DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Etherscan. Pay the Ethereum fee in ETH. DAI is 18 decimals and cannot cover gas. On the far side, keep BNB for chain id 56. The route's output is an ERC-20, so it arrives as a token balance beside the native coin.

faqs.question: Is there a reason to swap DAI for USDT without bridging?
faqs.answer: Yes. If the recipient wants Tether on Ethereum, use a mainnet pool and finish at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. This route is the wrong tool for that payment. Use it when the invoice, the pool, or the wallet is on BNB Chain and names BSC-USD.

intro:
Swap DAI from Ethereum to ETH on BNB Chain. A trader moving Maker DAI into ETH exposure on chain 56 receives Binance-Peg ETH.

The pegged token is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on BscScan. It is an ERC-20 standing in for ETH on BNB Chain. Native ETH and WETH on Ethereum are different contracts and stay behind. You spend Maker DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Etherscan. Chain id 1 gas is ETH, with blocks around 12 seconds. Chain id 56 gas is BNB, with blocks around 3 seconds. Pools that say ETH on BNB Chain almost always mean this pegged contract. Native ETH on mainnet cannot be deposited into those pools from this wallet. Check BscScan.
description: Swap DAI from Ethereum to ETH on BNB Chain when you want Binance-Peg ETH on chain 56 and you are spending Maker DAI you already hold on Ethereum mainnet.

sections.heading: This ETH is an ERC-20 on BscScan
sections.body: Search 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 and confirm the name before you treat the balance as spendable ETH. It will not pay fees on BNB Chain. It will not show up as the native ETH line on Ethereum. The wallet has to be on chain id 56.

sections.heading: DAI in, and the approval is on Etherscan
sections.body: The only DAI contract for this route is 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. Maker DAI uses 18 decimals. You need ETH in the same Ethereum account so the approval can be mined. A wallet holding DAI alone cannot start.

sections.heading: Unwrapping or buying ETH locally
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool if you want native ETH on Ethereum or WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Those are mainnet actions. Buy or unwrap there when the next signature is on chain id 1. Bridge when the book you want uses Binance-Peg ETH. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is only the starting network.

sections.heading: BNB has to be waiting
sections.body: Plan a small BNB balance on the receiving address. Pegged ETH cannot sponsor its own first transfer on chain 56. Blocks there are about 3 seconds once gas is available. Until then the token can be visible on BscScan and still be stuck.

faqs.question: Is Binance-Peg ETH the same as WETH?
faqs.answer: WETH on Ethereum is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Binance-Peg ETH is 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on BNB Chain. Both are ERC-20s that track ETH, and they are not interchangeable contracts. This route pays the BscScan address. Depositing DAI into the mainnet WETH contract is a different action and will fail.

faqs.question: What gas do I need on each chain?
faqs.answer: ETH on Ethereum to spend the DAI, because chain id 1 charges ETH and blocks take about 12 seconds. BNB on BNB Chain to move the pegged ETH afterward, because chain id 56 charges BNB. The route itself delivers neither gas coin. It delivers 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8.

faqs.question: Who is this pair for?
faqs.answer: Someone who holds Maker DAI on Ethereum and needs Binance-Peg ETH for a BNB Chain pool or transfer. It is the wrong tool for a saver who wants to remain in DAI, and for a trader who wants ETH exposure to stay on mainnet. If the pool is on Ethereum, trade there.

intro:
Swap DAI from Ethereum to BNB on BNB Chain. Wallets that need BNB for gas on chain 56 can spend Maker DAI held on Ethereum.

The output is native BNB, written as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. That placeholder is the gas coin, which BscScan shows as a native balance on chain id 56. The input is Maker DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Etherscan, an 18 decimal ERC-20. You still need ETH on chain id 1 to pay for the send. Mainnet blocks are about 12 seconds. Then switch the wallet to chain id 56.
description: Swap DAI from Ethereum to BNB on BNB Chain when a chain 56 wallet needs native BNB gas and the source balance is Maker DAI on Ethereum mainnet before you sign.

sections.heading: Why DAI holders open a BNB route
sections.body: Maker DAI on Ethereum cannot pay a BNB Chain fee. If the next signature is on chain id 56, the wallet needs native BNB first. This pair converts DAI you already hold into that gas coin. It is a clumsy way to buy a long-term BNB position if you only wanted a quote, and the quote on the screen is the number you judge.

sections.heading: The placeholder is not a token to import
sections.body: Leave 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE out of the custom token list. On this route it means BNB. On an Ethereum route the same string means native ETH. The chain id in the path, 56 versus 1, is the difference. Read the native balance on BscScan.

sections.heading: Approve DAI, pay ETH
sections.body: The contract that decreases is 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. Confirm it on Etherscan. Gas for that approval is ETH, even though the asset you want is BNB. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) explains why the source chain collects its own fee.

sections.heading: When a local swap is the better tool
sections.body: If you want ETH, USDC, or USDT on Ethereum, swap DAI on mainnet. This route is the wrong tool for those balances. If you already hold a BNB Chain stable and only need gas, swap that stable for BNB on chain 56. Bridge from Ethereum when the DAI is still on mainnet.

faqs.question: Does the received BNB show up under an ERC-20?
faqs.answer: It shows up as the native BNB balance on chain id 56. The address 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is a stand-in, not a contract you import from BscScan. If you add it as a custom token you will see a bogus row. Switch the wallet network and read the native coin line.

faqs.question: Can I start this route with only DAI in the wallet?
faqs.answer: You need Maker DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F and you also need ETH. Chain id 1 charges ETH for the approval and the send. Blocks are about 12 seconds. DAI is the asset being sold. ETH is the fee. They are different balances.

faqs.question: Is this how I unwrap DAI into ETH?
faqs.answer: DAI is not a wrapper around ETH. Selling DAI for native ETH on Ethereum is a mainnet swap. This route sells DAI for native BNB on BNB Chain. Use it when chain 56 gas is the gap. Skip it when you want ETH to remain on Ethereum.

intro:
Swap ETH from Ethereum to USDC on BNB Chain. You spend native ETH on Ethereum and a chain 56 wallet receives Binance-Peg USDC.

Native ETH is not an ERC-20 you approve. The route marks it as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and on Ethereum that placeholder is the gas coin Etherscan shows as a native balance. The dollar that arrives is 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d on BscScan, Binance-Peg USDC, 18 decimals. Circle's own USDC on Ethereum is a different contract. Because the asset you sell and the fee you pay are both ETH, leave a remainder for gas on chain id 1. Blocks there are about 12 seconds.
description: Swap ETH from Ethereum to USDC on BNB Chain when you want Binance-Peg dollars on chain 56 and you will spend native ETH from Ethereum mainnet in your wallet.

sections.heading: Leave ETH behind for the fee
sections.body: Chain id 1 charges ETH. If the swap amount is your entire native balance, the transaction cannot pay for itself. Move or keep a small ETH remainder in the same wallet before you sign. The received dollars will not refund that fee, because they land on BNB Chain as an ERC-20.

sections.heading: Pegged USDC on BscScan
sections.body: Expect 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d. It uses 18 decimals, so a wallet still set to 6 decimals will misstate the balance. Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 stays on Ethereum and is not credited. [BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) is where this pegged dollar is spent.

sections.heading: A mainnet ETH to USDC trade stays home
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when you want Circle USDC on Ethereum. That pool already exists on chain id 1, and it pays a different contract. Use the bridge when a BNB Chain app, invoice, or pool has whitelisted the Binance-Peg address. Selling ETH for dollars on mainnet never creates that BscScan balance.

sections.heading: BNB after the dollars land
sections.body: Pegged USDC does not pay gas on chain id 56. Blocks there are about 3 seconds, and each transfer still needs BNB. If the destination wallet has never held BNB, the new dollars can show on BscScan and still be unable to move. Add gas before the next signature.

faqs.question: Do I approve a contract for the ETH I send?
faqs.answer: No approval is required for native ETH. The route records it as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which is a placeholder for the gas coin, not a token you import. You sign a send on Ethereum, chain id 1. Keep enough ETH unspent to cover gas, because the amount you bridge and the fee come from the same balance.

faqs.question: Which USDC will I see on BNB Chain?
faqs.answer: Binance-Peg USDC at 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d on BscScan. It is an 18 decimal token. Circle USDC on Ethereum is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 and uses 6 decimals. If the app you are funding lists the Ethereum address, this route delivers the wrong chain and the wrong contract.

faqs.question: When is selling ETH for USDC on Ethereum enough?
faqs.answer: When the dollars should remain on chain id 1 as Circle USDC. This bridge is the wrong tool for that balance. Open it only if the next use of the money is on BNB Chain and the accepted contract is the pegged USDC. A mainnet swap never moves the wallet onto chain id 56.

intro:
Swap ETH from Ethereum to USDT on BNB Chain. A chain 56 wallet that needs Tether spends native ETH from Ethereum and receives BSC-USD.

You send native ETH, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, the gas coin Etherscan lists on chain id 1. You receive Tether's BSC-USD at 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BscScan, and that token uses 18 decimals. Ethereum Tether, 6 decimals at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, is a different contract and is not the output. Leave ETH in the wallet for the mainnet fee. Blocks on Ethereum are about 12 seconds. Switch to chain id 56 before you look for BSC-USD.
description: Swap ETH from Ethereum to USDT on BNB Chain when a chain 56 wallet needs Tether and you will spend native ETH from Ethereum mainnet for the send today.

sections.heading: Ethereum already has an ETH to USDT pool
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool if the Tether you want is the mainnet contract. Sell ETH for 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Ethereum and stop there. Bridge only when the payee or the pool wants BSC-USD on chain 56. A same-chain swap cannot mint that BscScan token.

sections.heading: Eighteen decimals on BSC-USD
sections.body: Import 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 from BscScan so the wallet reads 18 decimals. People coming from Ethereum USDT expect 6 and then misread the new balance. The source side has no ERC-20 approval because native ETH is the 0xEeee placeholder, not a contract you add.

sections.heading: How the two networks charge you
sections.body: Chain id 1 takes ETH and produces a block about every 12 seconds. Chain id 56 takes BNB and produces a block about every 3 seconds. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the general picture. On this pair the output is an ERC-20, so BNB still has to sit in the destination wallet.

sections.heading: Who receives BSC-USD on purpose
sections.body: Use this pair to fund a BNB Chain book quoted in Tether, or to pay someone who sent a chain 56 address and the BSC-USD contract. You are selling mainnet ETH, the same coin that pays gas, so the quote has to leave a fee behind. This page does not set that quote.

faqs.question: Will my Ethereum USDT balance go up?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum Tether remains 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan. This route delivers 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BscScan. The ticker can read USDT in both wallets. Switch the network to chain id 56 and match the full address before you tell someone the payment has arrived.

faqs.question: Why might the transaction fail even though I hold ETH?
faqs.answer: The ETH you sell and the ETH that pays gas are one balance. Setting the amount to the full native balance leaves nothing for the chain id 1 fee. Lower the amount until the wallet still shows ETH beside the send. Native ETH uses 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE and does not need a token approval.

faqs.question: Does BSC-USD pay the next BNB Chain fee?
faqs.answer: It does not. BSC-USD is an ERC-20. Gas on chain id 56 is BNB, and blocks there are about 3 seconds once a transaction is submitted. If the receiving wallet has no BNB, add some before you try to move or spend the Tether. The route's job ends when BSC-USD arrives.

intro:
Swap ETH from Ethereum to BNB on BNB Chain. Someone who needs BNB gas on chain 56 spends native ETH on Ethereum to receive it.

Both sides of the route use 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. On Ethereum that string means native ETH, the gas coin Etherscan shows for chain id 1. On BNB Chain the same string means native BNB, the gas coin BscScan shows for chain id 56. They are not one balance viewed twice. You are selling ETH to receive BNB. Leave extra ETH on mainnet so the send can pay its own fee. Mainnet blocks are about 12 seconds.
description: Swap ETH from Ethereum to BNB on BNB Chain when you need native gas on chain 56 and you will spend native ETH from Ethereum mainnet for the send today.

sections.heading: One placeholder, two gas coins
sections.body: Do not import 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE as a custom token on either chain. It is a stand-in. The wallet shows ETH while it is on chain id 1 and BNB while it is on chain id 56. If both lines look unchanged, you are still looking at the source network.

sections.heading: What this pair is for
sections.body: People use it to turn mainnet ETH into the coin that pays fees on BNB Chain. A new chain 56 wallet can then move tokens. It is a direct way to fund gas, and a poor way to keep a dollar balance. If you wanted USDT or USDC on chain 56, pick the route whose output is that contract.

sections.heading: Skip it when the next trade is on Ethereum
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool for buying WETH, USDC, or USDT on mainnet. Those trades stay on chain id 1 and never credit native BNB. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is only the network you sign on. Wrapping ETH into 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is also a local action and does not produce BNB.

sections.heading: After BNB arrives
sections.body: Switch the wallet to chain id 56 and read the native balance on BscScan. Blocks there are about 3 seconds. The BNB you received can pay the next approval or swap. Spend less than the full amount if you still need gas for that follow-up transaction.

faqs.question: Why do tokenIn and tokenOut look identical?
faqs.answer: Both are 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE because each chain uses that placeholder for its own gas coin. Etherscan interprets it as ETH on chain id 1. BscScan interprets it as BNB on chain id 56. The path is what changes the meaning. You are not moving one native balance from one explorer to the other.

faqs.question: How much ETH should I keep back?
faqs.answer: Enough to pay the chain id 1 fee after the amount you sell. Native ETH funds both the trade and the gas, so a max send can fail. Ethereum blocks are about 12 seconds. The BNB you receive does not pay that mainnet fee, because it exists only on chain id 56.

faqs.question: Is wrapped BNB on Ethereum the same result?
faqs.answer: A token with a BNB ticker on Ethereum is an ERC-20 on chain id 1. It will not pay gas on BNB Chain. This route delivers native BNB, which BscScan shows as the chain's gas coin. Use it when chain 56 fees are the gap. Skip it when you are still trading on Ethereum.

intro:
Swap WETH from Ethereum to USDC on BNB Chain. Holders of wrapped ETH who need Binance-Peg dollars spend WETH and receive that USDC on chain 56.

WETH and ETH are different contracts. You approve wrapped ETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Etherscan. Withdrawing from that contract unwraps to native ETH and stays on Ethereum. This route does the other job: it spends WETH and delivers Binance-Peg USDC at 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d on BscScan. Gas on the way out is still ETH, chain id 1, about 12 seconds a block. The pegged USDC uses 18 decimals. Confirm that field on BscScan before you deposit the dollars into an app.
description: Swap WETH from Ethereum to USDC on BNB Chain when you want Binance-Peg dollars on chain 56 and the source token is wrapped ETH held on Ethereum mainnet.

sections.heading: Unwrapping WETH is the wrong tool here
sections.body: If you want native ETH on Ethereum, call withdraw on 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 and stop. That action never creates a BNB Chain balance. This page is for a wallet that must hold Binance-Peg USDC. A mainnet swap of WETH into Circle USDC is also the wrong tool when the dollars have to sit on chain 56.

sections.heading: The two contracts to compare
sections.body: Source: 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Etherscan, 18 decimals. Destination: 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d on BscScan, 18 decimals, Binance-Peg USDC. Circle's Ethereum USDC is 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 and is not what you receive. Matching the USDC ticker is not matching the address.

sections.heading: ETH gas even though you spend WETH
sections.body: WETH cannot pay the Ethereum fee. The wallet needs native ETH beside the wrapped balance or the approval sits unsigned. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) walks through that source-chain signature. On chain 56 the fee changes to BNB, and pegged USDC does not cover it.

sections.heading: After the pegged dollars arrive
sections.body: Switch to chain id 56, which blocks about every 3 seconds, and read the token on BscScan before you deposit it. Apps that want BSC-USD, the Tether contract, will ignore this USDC. Apps that want Ethereum USDC are on the wrong network entirely.

faqs.question: Can I unwrap WETH and bridge the ETH instead?
faqs.answer: You can unwrap on Ethereum, and that is a different route from this one. Withdrawing WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 returns native ETH on chain id 1. This page spends the WETH contract directly and pays Binance-Peg USDC at 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d. Pick the output the wallet is supposed to hold.

faqs.question: What do I approve on Etherscan?
faqs.answer: Approve 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, the WETH contract. Do not approve Circle USDC for this pair. You still need native ETH for gas on chain id 1, because an ERC-20 approval is a transaction of its own. Blocks are about 12 seconds. WETH is the asset. ETH is the fee.

faqs.question: Is Binance-Peg USDC 6 decimals like Circle USDC?
faqs.answer: No. The token at 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d on BscScan uses 18 decimals. Circle USDC on Ethereum uses 6. If the wallet shows a balance that looks a trillion times too large or too small, the decimal field is wrong. Re-import the contract from BscScan before you send it onward.

intro:
Swap WETH from Ethereum to USDT on BNB Chain. A chain 56 wallet that needs Tether spends wrapped ETH from Ethereum and receives BSC-USD.

Approve WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Etherscan. That contract is not native ETH. The Tether you receive is 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BscScan, called BSC-USD, with 18 decimals. Ethereum USDT at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 uses 6 decimals and lives on a different explorer. Gas to start is ETH on chain id 1. Gas after arrival is BNB on chain id 56. Switch the wallet to chain id 56 before you expect the Tether to show on BscScan.
description: Swap WETH from Ethereum to USDT on BNB Chain when a chain 56 wallet needs Tether and the source token is wrapped ETH held on Ethereum mainnet right now.

sections.heading: WETH on Etherscan, BSC-USD on BscScan
sections.body: Read both addresses in full before you sign. The spend is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. The receipt is 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955. A wallet that labels both as familiar tickers can still be pointed at a copy. Etherscan and BscScan are the two checks, and they are not interchangeable pages.

sections.heading: BNB Chain gas comes second
sections.body: Ethereum blocks are about 12 seconds and the fee is ETH, even when the token moving is WETH. BNB Chain blocks are about 3 seconds and the fee is BNB. [BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) will not treat BSC-USD as gas. Keep BNB on the destination address or the Tether waits.

sections.heading: When to sell WETH on Ethereum instead
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool if you want Ethereum Tether or native ETH. Uniswap-style pools already pair WETH with USDT on mainnet, and unwrapping WETH is a local withdraw. Use the bridge when the Tether contract you were given is the BNB Chain one. Staying on chain id 1 is simpler when the pool is already there.

sections.heading: Payments that ask for BSC-USD
sections.body: Send this output only to a chain 56 address that expects 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955. An Ethereum address, even one controlled by the same person, will not show the tokens on Etherscan. Tell the payee the network as well as the amount.

faqs.question: Is spending WETH the same as spending ETH?
faqs.answer: No. WETH is the ERC-20 at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Native ETH is the gas coin, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE when a route needs it. This pair approves WETH. You still need a separate ETH balance for the chain id 1 fee. Unwrapping first is a different transaction and stays on Ethereum.

faqs.question: Which USDT contract arrives?
faqs.answer: BSC-USD at 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BscScan, 18 decimals. Ethereum Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is 6 decimals and is not credited. If your books or your payee use the Ethereum contract, this route is the wrong tool. Match the address the invoice printed.

faqs.question: What blocks the Tether from moving after it arrives?
faqs.answer: An empty BNB balance. Chain id 56 charges BNB for every token transfer, and blocks are about 3 seconds only after that fee can be paid. BSC-USD cannot sponsor itself. Put a little BNB on the receiving wallet before you plan a second transaction.

intro:
Swap WETH from Ethereum to ETH on BNB Chain. Wrapped ETH on Ethereum is the input, and Binance-Peg ETH on chain 56 is what arrives.

This is not an unwrap. Unwrapping spends 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 and returns native ETH on Ethereum, which Etherscan shows as a gas balance. This route spends that same WETH contract and delivers 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8, Binance-Peg ETH, an ERC-20 on BscScan. Pegged ETH does not pay gas on chain 56. You still need ETH on chain id 1 to start, and BNB on chain id 56 afterward. A local unwrap returns native ETH on Ethereum and never produces the pegged contract on BscScan.
description: Swap WETH from Ethereum to ETH on BNB Chain when you want Binance-Peg ETH on chain 56 and the source token is wrapped ETH held on Ethereum mainnet today.

sections.heading: Unwrap locally if you want mainnet ETH
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool for getting native ETH back. The WETH contract on Ethereum already has a withdraw function, and the ETH it returns stays on chain id 1. Open this page only when a BNB Chain pool asks for Binance-Peg ETH. Those are different receipts, on different explorers.

sections.heading: Two ETH tickers, two addresses
sections.body: You approve 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Etherscan. You watch 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on BscScan. Native ETH on either chain uses the 0xEeee placeholder and is not what arrives. If the destination balance is an ERC-20, the route did what this pair says.

sections.heading: Gas on the way out of Ethereum
sections.body: Chain id 1 charges ETH and blocks about every 12 seconds. WETH cannot pay that. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is where the approval is signed. Chain id 56 then charges BNB, about every 3 seconds, and Binance-Peg ETH cannot pay that either. Budget both coins before you start.

sections.heading: Where pegged ETH is the asset people trade
sections.body: BNB Chain books that list ETH pairs mean 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. Landing that contract from a WETH balance lets you join those books. You do not receive a claim on the Ethereum WETH contract, and you do not receive bitcoin, BNB, or a stablecoin.

faqs.question: If I want ETH, why would I not just unwrap?
faqs.answer: Unwrap when the ETH should be mainnet gas. Withdrawing from 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 stays on Ethereum. This route is for Binance-Peg ETH at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on BNB Chain. The ticker matches and the chain does not. Pick unwrap for chain id 1 and this pair for chain id 56.

faqs.question: Will the received ETH pay BNB Chain fees?
faqs.answer: No. The received asset is an ERC-20. BNB pays fees on chain id 56. Pegged ETH can sit on BscScan with no way to transfer until the wallet holds BNB. Native ETH on Ethereum is similarly useless for that fee, because it lives on chain id 1.

faqs.question: What should I approve?
faqs.answer: Only the WETH contract at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Etherscan. There is no destination approval on BNB Chain before the tokens arrive. Keep native ETH for the mainnet gas. After arrival, import the pegged contract on a wallet that is switched to chain id 56.

intro:
Swap WETH from Ethereum to BNB on BNB Chain. Wallets that need native BNB spend wrapped ETH on Ethereum and receive the chain 56 gas coin.

You approve WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Etherscan. You receive native BNB, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which BscScan shows as the gas balance of chain id 56. That placeholder is not a token to import. Unwrapping WETH would have given you native ETH on Ethereum instead, and native ETH does not pay BNB Chain fees. Mainnet blocks are about 12 seconds. Chain 56 blocks are about 3 seconds.
description: Swap WETH from Ethereum to BNB on BNB Chain when a chain 56 wallet needs native gas and the source token is wrapped ETH held on Ethereum mainnet today.

sections.heading: The output is gas, not another ERC-20
sections.body: 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on this route means BNB. Once the wallet is on chain id 56, the native line should increase. If you imported the placeholder as a custom token, delete that row and read the native balance on BscScan. The WETH you spent will not appear there.

sections.heading: Approve wrapped ETH, pay native ETH
sections.body: The contract that decreases is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. The fee on chain id 1 is ETH. A wallet with WETH and no ETH cannot start. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is why the source chain collects a fee in its own coin before the destination coin exists.

sections.heading: Unwrap is the wrong tool for BNB
sections.body: Withdrawing WETH returns ETH on Ethereum. Swapping WETH for USDC or USDT on Ethereum keeps you on chain id 1. This route is the wrong tool for both of those outcomes. Use it when the missing piece is BNB for a chain 56 signature. If you already hold a BNB Chain token, swap that token for BNB locally instead.

sections.heading: Keep some BNB unspent
sections.body: The BNB you receive is what pays the next transaction. Sending the entire balance onward can leave the wallet unable to move anything else. Chain id 56 is cheap relative to mainnet and still not free. Leave a remainder sized for an approval plus a swap.

faqs.question: Does this route unwrap my WETH into ETH first?
faqs.answer: The result you hold is native BNB on chain id 56, not native ETH on Ethereum. WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is what you approve on Etherscan. A local unwrap would credit ETH on chain id 1 and stop. If ETH on Ethereum is the goal, do not open this pair.

faqs.question: How do I confirm the BNB arrived?
faqs.answer: Set the wallet to chain id 56 and check the native balance on BscScan. The marker 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is not a contract page you need to open. Blocks on BNB Chain are about 3 seconds. If the wallet network is still Ethereum, you will keep seeing ETH and miss the BNB.

faqs.question: What if I only hold WETH and no ETH?
faqs.answer: Unwrap a small part of the WETH to native ETH first, on Ethereum, so the bridge approval can pay gas. Then spend the remaining WETH on this route. The fee and the asset are different. Chain id 1 will not accept WETH as gas.

intro:
Swap WBTC from Ethereum to USDC on BNB Chain. Holders of wrapped bitcoin who need Binance-Peg dollars spend WBTC and receive that USDC on chain 56.

WBTC is an ERC-20, not bitcoin on the Bitcoin chain. You approve 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 on Etherscan. It uses 8 decimals. A Bitcoin address cannot receive it, and this route cannot send it there. The dollars you receive are Binance-Peg USDC at 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d on BscScan, 18 decimals. Gas to leave Ethereum is ETH, chain id 1, about 12 seconds a block. Keep a little ETH beside the WBTC.
description: Swap WBTC from Ethereum to USDC on BNB Chain when you want Binance-Peg dollars on chain 56 and the source is the wrapped bitcoin ERC-20 on Ethereum today.

sections.heading: This is not a Bitcoin withdrawal
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool if the destination is a Bitcoin address or a bitcoin exchange deposit that asks for the Bitcoin network. WBTC stays an Ethereum token until this route spends it, and the output is a dollar on BNB Chain. Redeeming WBTC for bitcoin, if your custodian supports it, is a different process and does not use BscScan.

sections.heading: Eight decimals in, eighteen out
sections.body: Check 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 on Etherscan for the 8 decimal WBTC balance you are spending. Check 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d on BscScan for the 18 decimal pegged USDC you receive. Circle USDC on Ethereum is not the receipt. A wallet that mixes those decimal fields will invent the size of the trade.

sections.heading: ETH to start, BNB to finish
sections.body: WBTC does not pay Ethereum gas. Keep ETH on chain id 1 for the approval. Pegged USDC does not pay BNB Chain gas. Keep BNB on chain id 56, where blocks are about 3 seconds. [BNB Chain](/chains/bsc) is the network the dollars land on.

sections.heading: When a mainnet sale is enough
sections.body: WBTC already trades against Circle USDC and Tether on Ethereum. Use those pools when the dollars should stay on chain id 1. This bridge is for a wallet that needs the Binance-Peg contract specifically. Selling WBTC on mainnet never creates 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d.

faqs.question: Can I paste a Bitcoin address as the receiver?
faqs.answer: No. The output is an ERC-20 on BNB Chain, Binance-Peg USDC at 0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d. The input is WBTC at 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 on Etherscan, also an ERC-20. Neither side is the Bitcoin network. A Bitcoin address will not credit this route. Use an EVM address that is ready for chain 56.

faqs.question: Why does a small WBTC amount look large in dollars?
faqs.answer: WBTC uses 8 decimals, so 0.01 WBTC is a meaningful unit of wrapped bitcoin, not a dust balance. The USDC you receive is priced by the quote you sign, which this page does not fix. Read the minimum on the quote. The pegged USDC then shows 18 decimals on BscScan, which is a display detail, not a promise of size.

faqs.question: What do I need besides WBTC?
faqs.answer: ETH on Ethereum for gas, because chain id 1 will not accept WBTC as a fee. After the route, BNB on chain id 56, because pegged USDC will not pay those fees. Blocks are about 12 seconds on the way out and about 3 seconds on BNB Chain. Both gas coins are separate from the two token contracts.

intro:
Swap WBTC from Ethereum to USDT on BNB Chain. A chain 56 payment in Tether can start from wrapped bitcoin held as an ERC-20 on Ethereum.

Approve WBTC at 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 on Etherscan. Eight decimals, and it is not a Bitcoin-network coin. Receive BSC-USD at 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BscScan, Tether's 18 decimal token on chain 56. Ethereum USDT at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is not the balance that increases. You pay ETH gas on chain id 1, where a block takes about 12 seconds. The recipient must be on chain 56, watching BscScan, or they will miss the payment entirely on arrival.
description: Swap WBTC from Ethereum to USDT on BNB Chain when a chain 56 wallet needs Tether and the source is the wrapped bitcoin ERC-20 on Ethereum mainnet today.

sections.heading: Contracts before the ticker
sections.body: The pair is fully named by two strings: 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 on Etherscan and 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955 on BscScan. WBTC in, BSC-USD out. If either explorer shows a different contract under a similar name, stop. Copies reuse the first and last characters.

sections.heading: A payee on Ethereum wants a different USDT
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when the invoice says Ethereum and prints 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. Sell WBTC for that Tether on mainnet. Bridge when the invoice says BNB Chain and prints the BSC-USD address. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is the signing order. The asset pair is still this one.

sections.heading: Bitcoin chain is the wrong destination
sections.body: Sending WBTC to a Bitcoin address will not redeem it. This route also will not. You finish holding Tether on BNB Chain. If the goal is bitcoin in a Bitcoin wallet, stop and use whatever redemption path your WBTC custodian documents. BscScan will not show a bitcoin UTXO.

sections.heading: Fees around an 8 decimal token
sections.body: Keep ETH for the Ethereum approval. WBTC cannot pay it. Keep BNB for the chain 56 transfer that follows, because BSC-USD cannot pay it. Blocks on BNB Chain are about 3 seconds. Size the trade from the quote, and remember that 8 decimal units are easy to mistype.

faqs.question: Is WBTC the same as bitcoin for this payment?
faqs.answer: No. WBTC at 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 is an ERC-20 on Ethereum, 8 decimals, checked on Etherscan. This route spends it and pays BSC-USD on BNB Chain. A Bitcoin wallet cannot hold either token. Treat the position as an Ethereum asset until you deliberately redeem it somewhere else.

faqs.question: Which Tether should the recipient watch?
faqs.answer: BscScan for 0x55d398326f99059fF775485246999027B3197955, on chain id 56. Watching Etherscan for 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 will show no change from this route. Ask the recipient to switch networks before they check. The token uses 18 decimals, unlike 6 decimal Ethereum USDT, so the wallet must import the BscScan contract.

faqs.question: What if I want USDT but I am still trading on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: Stay on Ethereum. WBTC and Tether already have a mainnet market, and the output is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. This bridge is the wrong tool for that market. Use it when the Tether has to be BSC-USD because the next wallet, pool, or invoice is on chain 56.

intro:
Swap WBTC from Ethereum to ETH on BNB Chain. Traders moving wrapped bitcoin into ETH exposure on chain 56 receive Binance-Peg ETH.

You spend WBTC, the ERC-20 at 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 on Etherscan, 8 decimals. You receive Binance-Peg ETH at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on BscScan. That is also an ERC-20. It is not native ETH, not WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, and not bitcoin. Chain id 1 gas is ETH, about 12 seconds a block. Chain id 56 gas is BNB, about 3 seconds a block.
description: Swap WBTC from Ethereum to ETH on BNB Chain when you want Binance-Peg ETH on chain 56 and the source is the wrapped bitcoin ERC-20 on Ethereum mainnet.

sections.heading: A wrapped pair, not a bitcoin trade
sections.body: Both ends are tokens on EVM chains. Selling WBTC for ETH on Ethereum would leave you in mainnet ETH or WETH. This route leaves you in Binance-Peg ETH. It is the wrong tool for a Bitcoin-network withdrawal and the wrong tool for a mainnet ETH balance. Use it when the ETH book you want is on BNB Chain.

sections.heading: Check the pegged ETH address
sections.body: BscScan must show 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8. The WBTC that decreases is 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 on Etherscan. Native ETH would have been the 0xEeee placeholder, and it is not the output. If your wallet's native ETH line on Ethereum is what you wanted to grow, you opened the wrong pair.

sections.heading: Two gas coins around the trade
sections.body: WBTC will not pay the Ethereum approval. Hold ETH on chain id 1. Pegged ETH will not pay the BNB Chain transfer. Hold BNB on chain id 56. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is only the starting side. The quote you sign is the amount you accept. This article does not publish a price.

sections.heading: Who holds both wrappers on purpose
sections.body: A desk that keeps WBTC on mainnet and hedges or spends ETH exposure on BNB Chain can use this pair in one signature path. Someone who simply wants to rotate WBTC into WETH should stay on Ethereum, where both contracts already trade. The pool being on the source chain is the reason to skip the bridge.

faqs.question: Is the ETH I receive WETH?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. This route pays Binance-Peg ETH at 0x2170Ed0880ac9A755fd29B2688956BD959F933F8 on BscScan. Native ETH is the gas coin on chain id 1. Three different things use the ETH name. The contract you can spend on BNB Chain is the pegged one.

faqs.question: Can this WBTC be sent to a Bitcoin address instead?
faqs.answer: Not on this route. WBTC at 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 is an ERC-20 on Ethereum. The output is an ERC-20 on BNB Chain. Neither explorer is a Bitcoin explorer. If you need bitcoin on the Bitcoin chain, this pair is the wrong tool.

faqs.question: What fails if I have WBTC and nothing else?
faqs.answer: The Ethereum transaction. Chain id 1 charges ETH, and WBTC cannot substitute. Add ETH for gas before you approve 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599. On the far side, add BNB or the pegged ETH will be unable to move. Blocks are about 12 seconds on Ethereum and about 3 seconds on BNB Chain.

intro:
Swap WBTC from Ethereum to BNB on BNB Chain. A chain 56 wallet that needs gas can spend wrapped bitcoin on Ethereum and receive native BNB.

WBTC at 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 is an 8 decimal ERC-20 on Etherscan, not a coin on the Bitcoin chain. Native BNB is marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE and shows up as the gas balance on BscScan for chain id 56. You do not import that placeholder. You do approve the WBTC contract, and you pay the approval in ETH. Ethereum blocks are about 12 seconds.
description: Swap WBTC from Ethereum to BNB on BNB Chain when a chain 56 wallet needs native gas and the source is the wrapped bitcoin ERC-20 on Ethereum mainnet today.

sections.heading: Gas on chain 56 is the reason to open it
sections.body: Wrapped bitcoin cannot pay a BNB Chain fee. If the next signature has to happen on chain id 56, the wallet needs native BNB. This pair turns WBTC you already hold on Ethereum into that gas coin. It is the wrong shape of trade if you wanted a dollar stable to arrive instead.

sections.heading: Do not treat this as a bitcoin send
sections.body: A Bitcoin address will not accept WBTC, and it will not accept BNB. The route never leaves the two EVM chains. Etherscan is where 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 decreases. BscScan is where the native BNB balance increases. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) describes that split. It is not a Bitcoin bridge.

sections.heading: When the pool on Ethereum is enough
sections.body: If you want ETH, WETH, USDC, or USDT on mainnet, sell WBTC there. This route is the wrong tool for those balances. If you already hold BNB Chain assets and only need a little BNB, swap those assets on chain 56. Bridge from Ethereum when the wrapped bitcoin is still on mainnet.

sections.heading: Leave BNB for the next click
sections.body: Chain id 56 blocks about every 3 seconds and charges BNB. The coin you just received is that fee token, so it can pay the follow-up trade. Spending all of it in one transfer strands any other token in the same wallet. Keep a remainder.

faqs.question: Is the BNB an ERC-20 I should add by contract?
faqs.answer: No. Native BNB uses the placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE and appears as the gas balance once the wallet is on chain id 56. Importing that string as a token creates a junk row. Confirm the increase on BscScan's native balance. The ERC-20 you approve is WBTC, on Etherscan.

faqs.question: What is WBTC if it is not bitcoin?
faqs.answer: An ERC-20 at 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599, 8 decimals, on Ethereum. This route can spend that contract. It cannot move coins on the Bitcoin network. If your goal is a Bitcoin wallet balance, stop. If your goal is BNB gas funded from that ERC-20, this is the pair.

faqs.question: Why do I still need ETH?
faqs.answer: Because the spend starts on chain id 1. WBTC cannot pay Ethereum gas, and the BNB you will receive does not exist on Ethereum yet. Hold ETH for the approval and the send. Blocks are about 12 seconds. After arrival, BNB covers chain id 56.

intro:
Swap USDC from Ethereum to USDT on Polygon. Traders who need Tether on Polygon spend Circle USDC on Ethereum and receive the PoS USDT.

This page is for a chain 137 wallet that must hold Tether. A mainnet pool is the right tool when you only want to rotate Circle dollars into Tether on Ethereum. You approve 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan, Circle USDC, 6 decimals. You receive 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F on Polygonscan, also 6 decimals. That is not Circle's native USDC on Polygon. Gas to send is ETH on chain id 1, about 12 seconds a block. Polygon then charges POL. Switch the wallet to chain id 137 before you look for the Tether on Polygonscan.
description: Swap USDC from Ethereum to USDT on Polygon when a Polygon wallet needs Tether and you already hold Circle USDC on Ethereum mainnet before you approve.

sections.heading: Stay on Ethereum to flip the stable
sections.body: Circle USDC and Tether already trade on chain id 1. This route is the wrong tool for that rotation. Open it when the Tether has to be the Polygon contract. A same-chain swap never creates 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F, and it never moves the wallet onto chain 137.

sections.heading: Polygonscan is where the USDT lives
sections.body: Match 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F before you forward the funds. The source approval is only 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan. Polygon native USDC, 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359, is a different dollar and is not the output of this pair.

sections.heading: ETH first, POL second
sections.body: Chain id 1 takes ETH. Chain id 137 takes POL, and blocks there are about 2 seconds. The USDT you receive cannot pay that fee. [Polygon](/chains/polygon) is the network where the gas coin is POL. Keep a little of it on the receiving wallet or the Tether sits still.

sections.heading: Who the PoS USDT is for
sections.body: Use it when a Polygon app, invoice, or pool quotes pairs in this Tether. Both legs are 6 decimals, which makes the unit look familiar and does not make the contracts the same. Circle does not custody the destination token. You hold Tether on Polygon.

faqs.question: Is Polygon USDT the same contract as Ethereum USDT?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum Tether is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan. This route pays 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F on Polygonscan. Both use 6 decimals, so the amount can look familiar while the chain is different. Switch the wallet to chain id 137 and match the full address before you spend it.

faqs.question: Will the received USDT pay Polygon gas?
faqs.answer: No. Gas on chain id 137 is POL. USDT is an ERC-20, so a wallet with only that token cannot move it. Keep POL on the destination address. The send itself still needs ETH on Ethereum, chain id 1, because Circle USDC cannot pay mainnet gas either. Blocks on Polygon are about 2 seconds once POL is available.

faqs.question: What if I only wanted USDT on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: Sell Circle USDC for Tether on Ethereum and stop. The output there is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. This bridge is the wrong tool for that balance. Use it when a Polygon address is expecting the PoS USDT contract and the dollars you hold today are still Circle USDC on mainnet.

intro:
Swap USDC from Ethereum to WETH on Polygon. A chain 137 wallet that wants wrapped ETH spends Circle USDC on Ethereum to receive it.

The WETH that arrives is 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 on Polygonscan. It is not Ethereum WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, and it is not native ETH. You spend Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan. Ethereum gas is ETH, chain id 1, about 12 seconds a block. Polygon gas is POL, chain id 137, about 2 seconds a block. The received WETH cannot pay either fee. Switch to chain id 137 and import the Polygonscan contract before you decide the WETH is missing. The Ethereum wallet keeps showing the old mainnet WETH balance until you change networks.
description: Swap USDC from Ethereum to WETH on Polygon when you want Polygon WETH on chain 137 and you will spend Circle USDC held on Ethereum before you approve.

sections.heading: Two WETH contracts, two explorers
sections.body: Approve only 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan. Watch 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 on Polygonscan. If your wallet is still on chain id 1, the Polygon WETH will not show in the mainnet WETH line. Switch networks before you decide the funds are missing.

sections.heading: Buying WETH on Ethereum is a different job
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when you want 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 or native ETH on mainnet. Those trades stay on chain id 1. Use this page when a Polygon pool lists WETH and means the Polygonscan contract. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the split between the two balances.

sections.heading: POL has to be there already
sections.body: Wrapped ETH on Polygon does not pay gas. A fresh chain 137 wallet can receive 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 and then be unable to swap it. Hold POL first, or pick a route whose output is native POL, before you plan the next signature.

sections.heading: What Polygon WETH is used for
sections.body: Chain 137 books that say WETH usually mean this bridged contract, 18 decimals. Landing it from Circle USDC lets you enter those books without first holding WETH on Ethereum. You still pay ETH to leave mainnet. The quote you sign is the amount you accept.

faqs.question: Is Polygon WETH the same token as mainnet WETH?
faqs.answer: No. Mainnet WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Etherscan. This route pays 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 on Polygonscan. Both are ERC-20s that track ETH, and a pool on one chain will not take the other contract. Check the network badge in the wallet before you deposit.

faqs.question: Which token do I approve?
faqs.answer: Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan. You do not approve Polygon WETH before it arrives. You do need ETH on chain id 1 for gas, because USDC cannot pay it. Blocks there are about 12 seconds. The approval and the send can be two transactions.

faqs.question: What if the Polygon app wants native POL instead?
faqs.answer: Then this output is the wrong asset. POL is the gas coin, marked with the 0xEeee placeholder, and this route delivers WETH. Pick the USDC to POL pair when the gap is gas. Pick this pair when the pool or transfer asks for 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619.

intro:
Swap USDC from Ethereum to POL on Polygon. People who need POL for gas on chain 137 spend Circle USDC on Ethereum and receive it.

Native POL is marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. On this route that placeholder is the gas coin Polygonscan shows for chain id 137, not native ETH. You send Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan. Some wallets still label the Polygon gas coin with the older MATIC name. The balance this route delivers is POL. Keep ETH on Ethereum for the send. Mainnet blocks are about 12 seconds. Switch to chain id 137 and read the native balance on Polygonscan.
description: Swap USDC from Ethereum to POL on Polygon when a Polygon wallet needs POL for gas and you will spend Circle USDC from Ethereum mainnet before you approve.

sections.heading: POL is the fee the next click needs
sections.body: A Polygon wallet full of USDT or WETH still cannot move them without POL. This pair turns Circle dollars you already hold on Ethereum into that gas coin. It is a poor fit when you wanted a stablecoin to remain a stablecoin on chain 137. The output is the native balance, not an ERC-20 payout.

sections.heading: Do not import the placeholder
sections.body: Leave 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE out of the custom token list. On Ethereum the same string means ETH. On Polygon it means POL. Chain id is the difference. Read the native line on Polygonscan after you switch the wallet to chain id 137.

sections.heading: The USDC approval stays on Etherscan
sections.body: Spend 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, Circle USDC, 6 decimals. Polygon native USDC at 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 is already on chain 137 and is not the input. If your dollars are already on Polygon, swap them for POL there. This bridge is the wrong tool for that wallet.

sections.heading: ETH pays for the departure
sections.body: Chain id 1 charges ETH even though the coin you want is POL. [Polygon](/chains/polygon) collects POL only after you arrive. Blocks there are about 2 seconds. Leave some of the received POL unspent so the next approval on chain 137 can be mined.

faqs.question: Why does my wallet say MATIC when this page says POL?
faqs.answer: Some wallets still print the older ticker for Polygon gas. The coin this route delivers is POL, the native gas token of chain id 137, represented by 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Check the native balance on Polygonscan rather than a custom token row. You do not import that placeholder as an ERC-20.

faqs.question: Can I pay the Ethereum fee with USDC?
faqs.answer: No. Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 is the asset you sell. ETH is the fee on chain id 1. Blocks are about 12 seconds. If the wallet holds USDC and no ETH, add a little ETH before you approve. POL arrives later and cannot pay that mainnet fee.

faqs.question: When should I skip this and swap on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: When you want USDT, WETH, or more USDC on mainnet. Those books are already on chain id 1 and will not credit native POL. This route is for a chain 137 wallet that needs gas. If you already hold a Polygon token, buy POL on Polygon instead of bridging from Ethereum.

intro:
Swap USDT from Ethereum to USDC on Polygon. Wallets that need Circle's native USDC on chain 137 spend Ethereum Tether to receive it.

You send Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan, 6 decimals. You receive 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 on Polygonscan, Circle's native USDC on Polygon, also 6 decimals. The older bridged USDC.e at 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174 is a different contract and is not this output. Gas to leave is ETH on chain id 1. Polygon gas is POL on chain id 137. If an app printed the USDC.e address, stop, because this route will not credit that bridged contract. The native dollar and the bridged dollar do not share a Polygonscan balance. Deposit only where the allowlist matches the native contract.
description: Swap USDT from Ethereum to USDC on Polygon for Circle's native USDC on Polygon, spent from Tether you already hold on Ethereum mainnet before you approve.

sections.heading: Native USDC is not USDC.e
sections.body: Apps on Polygon split the dollar. Circle's native token is 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. Bridged USDC.e is 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174. This route pays the native contract. If the app's allowlist prints the USDC.e address, these dollars will not credit. Read the allowlist on Polygonscan before you deposit.

sections.heading: Tether is what leaves Ethereum
