sections.body: Approve 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 only. Ethereum USDT often needs its own approval transaction, and that transaction burns ETH. Circle USDC on Ethereum, 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, is not the token you send and not the token you receive.

sections.heading: A mainnet stable swap stays on mainnet
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when both dollars should remain on Ethereum. USDT and Circle USDC already have a chain id 1 book. Bridging is justified when the receiving contract is the Polygon native USDC. [Polygon](/chains/polygon) is where that contract is spent, and where POL pays the fee.

sections.heading: POL after a 6 decimal dollar
sections.body: The received USDC uses 6 decimals, like the Tether you spent, and it still cannot pay gas. Chain id 137 blocks about every 2 seconds and charges POL. Keep POL on the destination wallet. Chain id 1 blocks about every 12 seconds and charges ETH.

faqs.question: Which USDC address should I watch on Polygon?
faqs.answer: 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 on Polygonscan. That is Circle's native USDC. USDC.e at 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174 is the bridged token and will not increase because of this route. If your wallet shows two USDC rows, import the native contract and hide the one the app did not ask for.

faqs.question: What do I approve on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan. Keep ETH in the same wallet for gas on chain id 1. USDT cannot pay that fee, and the approval may be a separate transaction from the swap. Blocks are about 12 seconds. The USDC you receive shows up only after you switch to chain id 137.

faqs.question: Is this the same as swapping USDT for USDC on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: The tickers match and the contracts do not. On Ethereum the USDC would be 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. This route delivers Polygon native USDC. Use the mainnet pool when the dollars should stay on chain id 1. Use this page when chain 137 is where the USDC has to sit.

intro:
Swap USDT from Ethereum to WETH on Polygon. Traders who want wrapped ETH on chain 137 spend Tether from Ethereum and receive Polygon WETH.

The output is 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 on Polygonscan, an 18 decimal ERC-20. It is not native ETH and it will not pay POL gas. You spend Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan. Ethereum WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is a different contract on a different explorer. Chain id 1 gas is ETH, about 12 seconds a block. Chain id 137 gas is POL, about 2 seconds a block. A wallet that stays on Ethereum and watches Etherscan will not see this WETH. The credit exists only on chain id 137, under the Polygonscan contract, after you switch networks. Check Polygonscan before you trade it.
description: Swap USDT from Ethereum to WETH on Polygon when you want Polygon WETH on chain 137 and you will spend Tether held on Ethereum mainnet before you approve.

sections.heading: Sell Tether for WETH on mainnet if you are staying
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when the WETH you want is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. That pool is already on Ethereum. Bridge when the book you need uses Polygon WETH. A chain id 1 swap never mints 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619.

sections.heading: Match Tether in and WETH out
sections.body: Etherscan should show a spend of 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. Polygonscan should show a credit of 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. Tether is 6 decimals. Polygon WETH is 18. A wallet that uses one decimal field for both will misread one of the balances.

sections.heading: Two gas coins, neither is the output
sections.body: USDT cannot pay Ethereum gas, so hold ETH. Polygon WETH cannot pay chain 137 gas, so hold POL. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is only where you sign first. If the missing piece is POL itself, this pair delivers the wrong asset.

sections.heading: Where this WETH gets deposited
sections.body: Polygon pools that list WETH mean the Polygonscan contract. Receiving it from Ethereum Tether lets you join those pools. You do not receive a claim on mainnet WETH, and you do not receive native ETH on either chain. The quote on the screen is the number you judge.

faqs.question: Will my Ethereum WETH balance increase?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum WETH stays at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Etherscan. This route pays 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 on Polygonscan. Switch the wallet to chain id 137 before you look. If the wallet network is still Ethereum, the new WETH is invisible and the old WETH is unchanged.

faqs.question: Why does the send ask for ETH when I am spending USDT?
faqs.answer: Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is an ERC-20. Moving it on chain id 1 costs ETH. The approval can be its own transaction. A wallet that holds only USDT cannot finish the route. Add ETH for gas. Blocks are about 12 seconds. POL is a later requirement, on Polygon.

faqs.question: Does Polygon WETH pay the next swap?
faqs.answer: It pays the trade only in the sense that it is the asset you can sell. The network fee is POL. If the destination wallet has no POL, the WETH can be visible on Polygonscan and still be stuck. Fund POL first, or choose a route that outputs native POL.

intro:
Swap USDT from Ethereum to POL on Polygon. A Polygon wallet short of gas spends Ethereum Tether and receives native POL.

Native POL uses 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. That placeholder is the gas coin on chain id 137, shown on Polygonscan as a native balance. The token you approve is Tether, 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, on Etherscan. If your Tether is already the Polygon contract at 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F, you do not need this bridge. You need ETH beside the mainnet USDT so chain id 1 can mine the send. Switch the wallet to chain id 137 and read the native line on Polygonscan, including wallets that still print the older MATIC label for this gas coin.
description: Swap USDT from Ethereum to POL on Polygon when a Polygon wallet needs POL for gas and you will spend Tether held on Ethereum mainnet before you approve.

sections.heading: Already on Polygon? Swap there
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when the USDT is already at 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. Trade that token for POL on chain 137. Bridging from Ethereum moves 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, which is a mainnet balance. Check which explorer holds the Tether before you sign.

sections.heading: The placeholder means POL here
sections.body: Do not import 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. On this path it means POL. On an Ethereum path it means ETH. After the route, switch to chain id 137 and read the native line on Polygonscan. A wallet that still says MATIC is often showing this same gas coin under the old label.

sections.heading: ETH for the Tether approval
sections.body: Chain id 1 charges ETH and blocks about every 12 seconds. Tether cannot substitute. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) covers the source signature. The POL you receive can pay the next chain 137 transaction, where blocks are about 2 seconds.

sections.heading: Leave POL for the follow-up
sections.body: If you spend the entire native balance on the next transfer, later token moves stall. Keep a remainder sized for an approval and a swap. This pair exists to fund that remainder from Ethereum Tether, not to replace a dollar balance you still need.

faqs.question: I hold USDT on Polygon already. Should I open this page?
faqs.answer: No. This page starts from Ethereum Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan. Polygon USDT at 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F can be swapped for POL on chain 137. Using this bridge would move a mainnet balance you may be leaving in place on purpose. Use a same-chain swap instead.

faqs.question: Is 0xEeee a POL contract on Polygonscan?
faqs.answer: It is a placeholder for the native gas coin, not a contract to import. On chain id 137 that coin is POL. Polygonscan shows it as the native balance of the address. Importing the placeholder creates a useless token row. Switch the wallet network and read the gas line.

faqs.question: What else belongs in the Ethereum wallet?
faqs.answer: Tether plus ETH. The USDT contract cannot pay gas on chain id 1, and blocks there are about 12 seconds. POL does not exist on Ethereum yet, so it cannot pay the fee either. Add a small ETH balance before you approve 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7.

intro:
Swap DAI from Ethereum to USDC on Polygon. Holders leaving Maker DAI for Circle's dollar on chain 137 spend DAI and receive native USDC.

DAI is Maker's collateral dollar at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Etherscan, 18 decimals. The USDC you receive is 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 on Polygonscan, Circle's native USDC, 6 decimals. Bridged USDC.e at 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174 is not the receipt. You pay ETH on chain id 1. You later pay POL on chain id 137. Import the native contract from Polygonscan before you deposit. A wallet showing only USDC.e will look empty even after the route completes and the chain id is already 137. The 6 decimal display is another reason to read the token page before you size a transfer.
description: Swap DAI from Ethereum to USDC on Polygon when you are leaving Maker DAI for Circle's native USDC that has to sit on Polygon chain 137 before you approve.

sections.heading: Watch the native USDC, not USDC.e
sections.body: Polygonscan should show 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. If you imported only 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174, the wallet will look empty. The decimals also change, from 18 on Maker DAI to 6 on Circle's native USDC. Read both token pages before you size the next transfer.

sections.heading: Maker DAI is the approval
sections.body: The contract that decreases is 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. Confirm it on Etherscan. Circle USDC on Ethereum, 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, is what you would receive from a mainnet DAI to USDC swap, and this route does not pay that contract.

sections.heading: Keep the Maker dollar on Ethereum when that is the job
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool if you want Circle USDC on chain id 1, or if you want to remain in DAI. Both of those are mainnet actions. Bridge when a Polygon app has whitelisted the native USDC. [Polygon](/chains/polygon) is where POL then pays for using it.

sections.heading: Gas on both sides of the decimal change
sections.body: ETH pays the Ethereum approval. Blocks there are about 12 seconds. POL pays any later move of the USDC. Blocks on chain 137 are about 2 seconds. The USDC cannot sponsor that second fee. Hold POL before you try to deposit the new dollars.

faqs.question: Does this give me Circle USDC on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. It spends Maker DAI and pays Circle's native USDC on Polygon, 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 on Polygonscan. Ethereum Circle USDC remains 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan. If that mainnet contract is the balance you wanted, trade DAI for it on chain id 1 and skip this bridge.

faqs.question: Why might the USDC amount look different from the DAI amount?
faqs.answer: DAI uses 18 decimals and Polygon native USDC uses 6. A wallet with the wrong decimal field will shift the display by many zeros even when the quote was a dollar-for-dollar shape. Check the decimals on Polygonscan for 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. The quote you sign is the figure to trust, and this page does not set it.

faqs.question: What if the app listed USDC.e?
faqs.answer: Stop and do not deposit this output there. USDC.e is 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174. This route pays the native contract. Sending native USDC into a pool that wants the bridged token will not credit your position. Match the allowlist address, not the USDC ticker.

intro:
Swap DAI from Ethereum to USDT on Polygon. Someone paying Tether on chain 137 can spend Maker DAI from Ethereum and receive the PoS USDT.

You approve Maker DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Etherscan, 18 decimals. You receive Tether at 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F on Polygonscan, 6 decimals. Ethereum Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is not the balance that increases. The issuers differ: Maker on the way out, Tether on the way in. Gas to leave is ETH on chain id 1. Tell the payee to watch Polygonscan on chain id 137. An Etherscan tab open to Ethereum Tether will stay flat for the whole transfer. Confirm the contract there.
description: Swap DAI from Ethereum to USDT on Polygon when a Polygon wallet needs Tether and the source balance is Maker DAI on Ethereum mainnet before you approve.

sections.heading: Polygonscan USDT is the payment asset
sections.body: Expect 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. A payee who printed the Ethereum USDT address will not see this transfer on Etherscan. Tell them the network is Polygon, chain id 137, and the contract is the Polygonscan one. The decimal change from 18 to 6 is a display detail, not a second payment.

sections.heading: DAI for Ethereum Tether is a local swap
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when the invoice is on mainnet. Sell Maker DAI for 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 and stop. Bridge only when the Tether contract is the Polygon one. A chain id 1 pool already exists for the local job.

sections.heading: ETH out, POL in
sections.body: Chain id 1 blocks about every 12 seconds and charges ETH. DAI cannot pay it. Chain id 137 blocks about every 2 seconds and charges POL. The received USDT cannot pay that either. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is why each chain keeps its own fee.

sections.heading: Approve the Maker contract only
sections.body: 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F is the DAI this route can spend. A token with the DAI ticker and a different address is a different market. Confirm the string on Etherscan before the approval, then confirm the USDT string on Polygonscan after the wallet is on chain 137.

faqs.question: Will Ethereum USDT increase if I run this route?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum Tether stays at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan. The new tokens are 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F on Polygonscan. Look there after you switch to chain id 137. Both can be labeled USDT. The address and the explorer are how you tell the payment landed.

faqs.question: Why do the decimals change?
faqs.answer: Maker DAI uses 18 decimals. Polygon USDT uses 6, the same as Ethereum Tether. If the wallet was pointed at DAI's decimals, the USDT row will look wrong by many zeros. Re-import 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F from Polygonscan. Judge the trade by the quote you sign, which this page does not set.

faqs.question: What gas do I need on each side?
faqs.answer: ETH on Ethereum to approve and spend the DAI, because chain id 1 charges ETH. POL on Polygon to move the USDT afterward, because chain id 137 charges POL. The route delivers neither gas coin. Blocks are about 12 seconds on the way out and about 2 seconds on Polygon.

intro:
Swap DAI from Ethereum to WETH on Polygon. A trader moving Maker DAI into wrapped ETH on chain 137 receives Polygon WETH.

DAI is not a wrapper around ETH. You spend 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Etherscan. You receive 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 on Polygonscan. That WETH is not the mainnet contract 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, and withdrawing from the mainnet contract is not this route. Chain id 1 gas is ETH. Chain id 137 gas is POL. Switch to chain id 137 before you search for the wrapped ETH. The mainnet WETH row on Etherscan does not move when this pair completes, so the network badge matters as much as the ticker.
description: Swap DAI from Ethereum to WETH on Polygon when you want Polygon WETH on chain 137 and you will spend Maker DAI held on Ethereum mainnet before you approve.

sections.heading: Polygon WETH is an ERC-20 on Polygonscan
sections.body: Search 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 and confirm the contract before you treat the balance as spendable ETH. It will not pay POL fees. It will not show as native ETH on Ethereum. The wallet has to be on chain id 137, where blocks are about 2 seconds.

sections.heading: Buying WETH with DAI on mainnet stays home
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool if you want 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 or native ETH on chain id 1. Those markets are already on Ethereum. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is only the network that holds the DAI at the start. Bridge when the WETH address you were given is the Polygon one.

sections.heading: The DAI you approve
sections.body: Only 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. Maker DAI uses 18 decimals, and so does Polygon WETH, which can make the unit count look familiar while the asset changes from a dollar to wrapped ETH. You still need ETH in the Ethereum account so the approval can be mined.

sections.heading: POL has to be waiting
sections.body: Plan a small POL balance on the receiving address. Polygon WETH cannot sponsor its own first transfer. Until POL is present, the token can be visible on Polygonscan and still be stuck. Mainnet blocks, about 12 seconds, only cover the send.

faqs.question: Is this how I unwrap DAI into ETH?
faqs.answer: DAI is not wrapped ETH, so there is nothing to unwrap. Selling DAI for WETH on Ethereum credits 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. This route credits 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 on Polygon. Use it when chain 137 WETH is the position. Skip it when you want ETH exposure to stay on mainnet.

faqs.question: Which explorers do I check?
faqs.answer: Etherscan for the DAI spend at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. Polygonscan for the WETH credit at 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. Native ETH would use the 0xEeee placeholder and is not the output. If your native ETH line on Ethereum grew, you did a different trade. Then switch networks before you search.

faqs.question: What blocks the WETH after it arrives?
faqs.answer: No POL. Chain id 137 charges POL for every transfer, and Polygon WETH is an ERC-20. Add POL before the next signature. You also needed ETH on chain id 1 to spend the DAI. The route delivers neither of those gas coins.

intro:
Swap DAI from Ethereum to POL on Polygon. Wallets that need POL for gas on chain 137 can spend Maker DAI held on Ethereum.

The output is native POL, written as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Polygonscan shows that as the gas balance of chain id 137. The input is Maker DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Etherscan. You still need ETH on chain id 1 to pay for the send. A local sale of DAI for ETH would leave you on Ethereum, and that ETH cannot pay Polygon fees. Switch to chain id 137 and read the native gas line on Polygonscan.
description: Swap DAI from Ethereum to POL on Polygon when a Polygon wallet needs POL for gas and the source balance is Maker DAI on Ethereum mainnet before you approve.

sections.heading: Gas on chain 137 is the point
sections.body: Maker DAI on Ethereum cannot pay a Polygon fee. If the next signature is on chain id 137, the wallet needs POL. This pair converts DAI you already hold into that gas coin. It is the wrong shape if you wanted USDC or USDT to arrive instead. The quote on the screen is what you judge.

sections.heading: The placeholder is not a token row
sections.body: Leave 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE out of the import list. On this route it means POL. On Ethereum it means ETH. Chain id 137 versus chain id 1 is the whole difference. Some wallets still print MATIC for this native balance.

sections.heading: Approve DAI, pay ETH
sections.body: The contract that decreases is 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. Confirm it on Etherscan. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) explains the source-chain signature. Blocks on Ethereum are about 12 seconds. Blocks on Polygon are about 2 seconds once POL can pay.

sections.heading: Skip the bridge when the pool is local
sections.body: If you want ETH, USDC, or USDT on Ethereum, swap DAI on mainnet. This route is the wrong tool for those balances. If you already hold a Polygon stable and only need gas, swap that stable for POL on chain 137. Bridge from Ethereum when the DAI is still on mainnet.

faqs.question: Does the POL show up as an ERC-20?
faqs.answer: It shows up as the native balance on chain id 137. The address 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is a stand-in, not a contract you import from Polygonscan. Switch the wallet to Polygon and read the gas line. A custom token with that address will not be the real POL balance.

faqs.question: Can I start with only DAI in the wallet?
faqs.answer: You need Maker DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F and you also need ETH. Chain id 1 charges ETH for the approval and the send. DAI is the asset being sold. ETH is the fee. POL is what you receive later, and it cannot pay the Ethereum transaction.

faqs.question: Is this a way to turn DAI into ETH?
faqs.answer: No. Selling DAI for native ETH is a mainnet swap, and the ETH stays on chain id 1. This route sells DAI for native POL on Polygon. Use it when chain 137 gas is the gap. Skip it when the next trade is still on Ethereum.

intro:
Swap ETH from Ethereum to USDC on Polygon. You spend native ETH on Ethereum and a chain 137 wallet receives Circle's native USDC.

Native ETH is marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, the gas coin Etherscan shows on chain id 1. You do not approve it. The dollar that arrives is 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 on Polygonscan, 6 decimals. Bridged USDC.e at 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174 is not the receipt. Leave ETH behind for the mainnet fee. Blocks there are about 12 seconds. Import 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 from Polygonscan. A wallet that only tracks USDC.e will hide the dollars this route delivers. Leave POL on that same chain 137 address or the new USDC cannot move after it shows up. Confirm the contract before you deposit.
description: Swap ETH from Ethereum to USDC on Polygon when you want Circle's native USDC on Polygon and you will spend native ETH from Ethereum mainnet before you approve.

sections.heading: Leave ETH for the chain id 1 fee
sections.body: The coin you sell and the coin that pays gas are the same balance. A max send can fail because nothing remains for the fee. Lower the amount until the wallet still shows ETH. The USDC lands on Polygon and cannot refund that mainnet cost.

sections.heading: Native USDC, not the bridged dollar
sections.body: Watch 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 on Polygonscan. USDC.e is a second contract, 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174, and this route does not mint it. Circle USDC on Ethereum, 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, is also not the credit. [Polygon](/chains/polygon) is where the native dollar is spent.

sections.heading: A mainnet ETH to USDC sale stays home
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when you want Circle USDC on Ethereum. That pool already exists on chain id 1. Use the bridge when a Polygon app has whitelisted the native contract. Selling ETH for dollars on mainnet never creates the Polygonscan balance.

sections.heading: POL after the dollars land
sections.body: Native USDC does not pay gas on chain id 137. Blocks there are about 2 seconds, and each transfer still needs POL. If the destination wallet has never held POL, the new dollars can show on Polygonscan and still be unable to move.

faqs.question: Do I approve a contract for the ETH?
faqs.answer: No. Native ETH uses 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE as a placeholder, not a token you import. You sign a send on chain id 1. Keep enough ETH unspent to cover gas, because the amount you bridge and the fee come from the same balance. Etherscan shows that native balance, not an ERC-20 approval.

faqs.question: Which USDC row should increase?
faqs.answer: The native one, 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 on Polygonscan, 6 decimals. USDC.e at 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174 stays put. If the app you are funding lists the bridged address, this route delivers the wrong contract. Match the allowlist before you deposit. Match the allowlist before you deposit the dollars.

faqs.question: When is an Ethereum swap enough?
faqs.answer: When the dollars should remain on chain id 1 as Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. This bridge is the wrong tool for that balance. Open it only if the next use of the money is on Polygon and the accepted contract is the native USDC.

intro:
Swap ETH from Ethereum to USDT on Polygon. A chain 137 wallet that needs Tether spends native ETH from Ethereum and receives the PoS USDT.

You send native ETH, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, the gas coin on Etherscan for chain id 1. You receive 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F on Polygonscan, 6 decimals. Ethereum Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is not the output. Leave ETH in the wallet for the mainnet fee. Blocks on Ethereum are about 12 seconds. Polygon then charges POL. Switch to chain id 137 before looking for the Tether. Etherscan will not show a new USDT balance from this pair, even though the ticker on both networks can read USDT. Confirm it on Polygonscan.
description: Swap ETH from Ethereum to USDT on Polygon when a Polygon wallet needs Tether and you will spend native ETH from Ethereum mainnet for the send in your wallet.

sections.heading: Ethereum already pairs ETH with Tether
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool if the Tether you want is the mainnet contract. Sell ETH for 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on chain id 1 and stop. Bridge only when the payee or the pool wants 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. A same-chain swap cannot mint that Polygonscan token.

sections.heading: Six decimals on the way in
sections.body: Import the Polygon USDT from Polygonscan so the wallet reads 6 decimals. There is no ERC-20 approval on the source, because native ETH is the 0xEeee placeholder. The amount you sell and the ETH you keep for gas have to be split from one balance.

sections.heading: POL is still required
sections.body: Chain id 137 takes POL and produces a block about every 2 seconds. The output is an ERC-20, so it does not cover that fee. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the general picture. Hold POL on the destination wallet before the next signature.

sections.heading: Who wants this Tether
sections.body: Use the pair to fund a Polygon book quoted in USDT, or to pay a chain 137 address that named this contract. You are selling mainnet ETH. The quote has to leave a fee behind. This page does not set that quote.

faqs.question: Does my Ethereum USDT balance change?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum Tether remains 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan. This route delivers 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F on Polygonscan. Switch to chain id 137 and match the full address. The ticker can read USDT on both networks while the contracts stay different. The contracts stay different even when the ticker matches.

faqs.question: Why can a full ETH balance fail?
faqs.answer: The ETH you sell and the ETH that pays gas are one coin. Setting the amount to the entire native balance leaves nothing for chain id 1. Lower it until ETH remains. Native ETH uses 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE and does not need a token approval. Blocks are about 12 seconds.

faqs.question: Will Polygon USDT pay the next fee?
faqs.answer: No. It is an ERC-20. Gas on chain id 137 is POL, and blocks there are about 2 seconds only after that fee can be paid. If the receiving wallet has no POL, add some before you move the Tether. The route's job ends when the USDT arrives.

intro:
Swap ETH from Ethereum to WETH on Polygon. Someone who needs wrapped ETH on chain 137 spends native ETH on Ethereum and receives Polygon WETH.

Wrapping on Ethereum is a deposit into 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, and the WETH stays on mainnet. This route spends native ETH, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and delivers 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 on Polygonscan. Those are different contracts. Leave ETH for gas on chain id 1. The received token cannot pay POL on chain id 137. Depositing ETH into the mainnet WETH contract is a separate action and leaves you on chain id 1. This pair's receipt is only visible on Polygonscan after you switch to chain id 137. Hold POL there or the wrapped token cannot be transferred.
description: Swap ETH from Ethereum to WETH on Polygon when you want Polygon WETH on chain 137 and you will spend native ETH you already hold on Ethereum in your wallet.

sections.heading: A local wrap does not reach Polygon
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool if you want WETH on Ethereum. Deposit ETH into 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 and stop. That contract never becomes 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. Open this page when a Polygon pool asks for the Polygonscan WETH. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is only the chain you sign on.

sections.heading: Native in, ERC-20 out
sections.body: You do not approve the ETH. The placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means the gas coin on chain id 1. You do import, on chain 137, the WETH at 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. If the native ETH line on Ethereum is what you wanted to keep, this pair spends it.

sections.heading: Keep a fee on both chains
sections.body: Chain id 1 charges ETH and blocks about every 12 seconds, from the same balance you are selling. Chain id 137 charges POL and blocks about every 2 seconds. Polygon WETH pays neither. Budget POL on the destination before you try to use the wrapped token.

sections.heading: Pools that name WETH on Polygon
sections.body: They mean 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619, 18 decimals. Landing that contract from native ETH lets you join those books. You do not receive mainnet WETH, native POL, or a stablecoin. The amount is whatever quote you sign.

faqs.question: How is this different from wrapping ETH?
faqs.answer: Wrapping deposits native ETH into 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 and stays on Ethereum. This route delivers Polygon WETH at 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 on Polygonscan. The ticker matches. The chain and the contract do not. Use the wrap when the next signature is on chain id 1.

faqs.question: Do I approve ETH before sending?
faqs.answer: No approval is required for native ETH. It is recorded as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. You still must leave enough ETH to pay chain id 1 gas, or the send fails. Etherscan shows the native balance falling. Polygonscan shows the WETH balance rising after you switch networks.

faqs.question: Can Polygon WETH pay gas?
faqs.answer: No. Gas on chain id 137 is POL. The WETH can arrive and sit until POL is added. Blocks are about 2 seconds once a transaction can pay that fee. If you needed the gas coin itself, choose a route whose output is native POL.

intro:
Swap ETH from Ethereum to POL on Polygon. Someone who needs POL gas on chain 137 spends native ETH on Ethereum to receive it.

Both sides use 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. On Ethereum that string means native ETH, the gas coin on Etherscan for chain id 1. On Polygon the same string means native POL, the gas coin on Polygonscan for chain id 137. You are selling ETH to receive POL. Leave extra ETH so the send can pay its own fee. Mainnet blocks are about 12 seconds. Switch to chain id 137 and read the native line on Polygonscan.
description: Swap ETH from Ethereum to POL on Polygon when a Polygon wallet needs POL for gas and you will spend native ETH from Ethereum mainnet today in your wallet.

sections.heading: Same placeholder, different gas coin
sections.body: Do not import 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on either chain. The wallet shows ETH on chain id 1 and POL on chain id 137. A wallet that still prints MATIC is often labeling this POL balance with the old name. If both lines look unchanged, you are still on the source network.

sections.heading: Why sell ETH for POL
sections.body: A new Polygon wallet cannot move tokens until it holds POL. This pair turns mainnet ETH into that gas coin. It is a poor way to keep a dollar balance. If you wanted USDC or USDT on chain 137, pick the route whose output is that contract. [Polygon](/chains/polygon) is the network the POL pays for.

sections.heading: Wrong tool for a mainnet trade
sections.body: Buying WETH, USDC, or USDT on Ethereum never credits native POL. Wrapping ETH into 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is also local. This route is the wrong tool for all of those. Use it when the next signature has to be on chain id 137.

sections.heading: After the native balance moves
sections.body: Switch to chain id 137 and read Polygonscan. Blocks there are about 2 seconds. The POL you received can pay the next approval or swap. Spend less than the full amount if you still need gas for that follow-up.

faqs.question: Why are the two addresses identical?
faqs.answer: Both are 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE because each chain uses that placeholder for its own gas coin. Etherscan reads it as ETH on chain id 1. Polygonscan reads it as POL on chain id 137. You are not moving one native balance from one explorer onto the other.

faqs.question: How much ETH should stay behind?
faqs.answer: Enough to pay the chain id 1 fee after the amount you sell. Native ETH funds both the trade and the gas, so a max send can fail. The POL you receive does not pay that mainnet fee. It exists on chain id 137 only. Ethereum blocks are about 12 seconds.

faqs.question: Is a MATIC token on Ethereum the same result?
faqs.answer: An ERC-20 with an old MATIC ticker on Ethereum stays on chain id 1 and will not pay Polygon gas. This route delivers native POL. Use it when chain 137 fees are the gap. Skip it when you are still trading on Ethereum and only wanted a mainnet token.

intro:
Swap WETH from Ethereum to USDC on Polygon. Holders of wrapped ETH who need Circle's native USDC on chain 137 spend WETH and receive that dollar.

You approve WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Etherscan. Withdrawing from that contract unwraps to native ETH and stays on Ethereum. This route spends the WETH and delivers 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 on Polygonscan, Circle's native USDC, 6 decimals. Bridged USDC.e at 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174 is not the receipt. Gas to start is still ETH on chain id 1. Import the native USDC from Polygonscan after you switch to chain id 137. USDC.e will not reflect this route, and Etherscan will not show the new dollars either. Hold POL on the destination wallet before you try to deposit those dollars. Confirm it on Polygonscan.
description: Swap WETH from Ethereum to USDC on Polygon when you want Circle native USDC on Polygon and the source token is wrapped ETH on Ethereum mainnet in your wallet.

sections.heading: Unwrapping is the wrong tool
sections.body: If you want native ETH on Ethereum, withdraw from 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 and stop. If you want Circle USDC on Ethereum, swap WETH there. This page is for a wallet that must hold Polygon native USDC. A mainnet trade never creates 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359.

sections.heading: Native USDC versus USDC.e
sections.body: The credit to expect is 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 on Polygonscan. The bridged dollar is 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174. Depositing into the wrong row will not credit an app that listed the other address. WETH in is 18 decimals. This USDC is 6.

sections.heading: ETH gas beside the WETH
sections.body: WETH cannot pay the Ethereum fee. Hold native ETH for the approval. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) walks through that signature. On chain 137 the fee is POL, and native USDC does not cover it. Blocks there are about 2 seconds.

sections.heading: After the 6 decimal dollar arrives
sections.body: Switch to chain id 137 and read Polygonscan before you deposit. Apps that want USDT at 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F will ignore this USDC. Apps that want Ethereum USDC are on the wrong network. Mainnet blocks are about 12 seconds on the way out.

faqs.question: Can I unwrap WETH and then bridge the ETH?
faqs.answer: You can, and that is a different route. Withdrawing 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 returns native ETH on chain id 1. This page spends the WETH contract and pays Polygon native USDC at 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. Choose the output the destination wallet is supposed to hold.

faqs.question: What do I approve on Etherscan?
faqs.answer: Approve 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Do not approve Circle's Ethereum USDC for this pair. You still need native ETH for gas on chain id 1. Blocks are about 12 seconds. WETH is the asset being sold. ETH is only the fee. ETH is only the fee on chain id 1.

faqs.question: Which USDC will the wallet show?
faqs.answer: Circle's native USDC at 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359, 6 decimals, on Polygonscan. USDC.e will not move. If the balance looks enormous or tiny, the decimal field is wrong. Re-import the contract from Polygonscan before you send it to a pool. Then switch the wallet to chain id 137.

intro:
Swap WETH from Ethereum to USDT on Polygon. A chain 137 wallet that needs Tether spends wrapped ETH from Ethereum and receives the PoS USDT.

Approve WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Etherscan. That contract is not native ETH. The Tether you receive is 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F on Polygonscan, 6 decimals. Ethereum USDT at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is a different contract on Etherscan. Gas to start is ETH on chain id 1. Gas after arrival is POL on chain id 137. Switch to chain id 137 and match the Polygonscan USDT before you tell a payee the transfer finished. An Ethereum address will not display this balance.
description: Swap WETH from Ethereum to USDT on Polygon when a Polygon wallet needs Tether and the source token is wrapped ETH held on Ethereum mainnet before you approve.

sections.heading: WETH on Etherscan, USDT on Polygonscan
sections.body: The spend is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. The receipt is 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. A wallet that labels both with familiar tickers can still be pointed at a copy. Etherscan and Polygonscan are the two checks. They are not two views of one token.

sections.heading: Sell WETH for USDT on mainnet if you are staying
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool if you want Ethereum Tether or native ETH. Mainnet pools already pair WETH with USDT, and unwrapping WETH is a local withdraw. Use the bridge when the Tether contract you were given is the Polygon one. Staying on chain id 1 is simpler when the pool is already there.

sections.heading: POL comes second
sections.body: Ethereum blocks are about 12 seconds and the fee is ETH, even though the token moving is WETH. Polygon blocks are about 2 seconds and the fee is POL. [Polygon](/chains/polygon) will not treat USDT as gas. Keep POL on the destination address or the Tether waits.

sections.heading: Payments that name this USDT
sections.body: Send the output only to a chain 137 address that expects 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F. An Ethereum address controlled by the same person will not show the tokens on Etherscan. Tell the payee the network as well as the amount on the quote.

faqs.question: Is spending WETH the same as spending ETH?
faqs.answer: No. WETH is the ERC-20 at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Native ETH is the gas coin, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE when a route needs it. This pair approves WETH. You still need a separate ETH balance for the chain id 1 fee. Unwrapping first stays on Ethereum.

faqs.question: Which USDT contract arrives on Polygon?
faqs.answer: 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F on Polygonscan, 6 decimals. Ethereum Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is not credited. If your payee uses the Ethereum contract, this route is the wrong tool. Match the address the invoice printed, then switch the wallet to chain id 137. Then switch the wallet to chain id 137.

faqs.question: What stops the USDT from moving later?
faqs.answer: An empty POL balance. Chain id 137 charges POL for every token transfer. The USDT cannot sponsor itself. Put POL on the receiving wallet before a second transaction. Blocks are about 2 seconds after that fee can be paid. Blocks there are about 2 seconds after POL is in the wallet.

intro:
Swap WETH from Ethereum to POL on Polygon. Wallets that need native POL spend wrapped ETH on Ethereum and receive the chain 137 gas coin.

You approve WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Etherscan. You receive native POL, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which Polygonscan shows as the gas balance of chain id 137. Unwrapping WETH would have given you native ETH on Ethereum instead, and that ETH does not pay Polygon fees. Mainnet blocks are about 12 seconds. Polygon blocks are about 2 seconds. Switch to chain id 137 and read the native gas line on Polygonscan after the route.
description: Swap WETH from Ethereum to POL on Polygon when a Polygon wallet needs POL for gas and the source token is wrapped ETH held on Ethereum mainnet in your wallet.

sections.heading: The output is gas, not another wrapper
sections.body: 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on this route means POL. Once the wallet is on chain id 137, the native line should increase. If you imported the placeholder as a custom token, delete that row and read Polygonscan. The WETH you spent will not appear there. Some wallets still label this balance MATIC.

sections.heading: Approve wrapped ETH, pay native ETH
sections.body: The contract that decreases is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. The fee on chain id 1 is ETH. A wallet with WETH and no ETH cannot start. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is why the source chain collects a fee in its own coin first.

sections.heading: Unwrap does not produce POL
sections.body: Withdrawing WETH returns ETH on Ethereum. Swapping WETH for USDC or USDT on Ethereum keeps you on chain id 1. This route is the wrong tool for both outcomes. Use it when the missing piece is POL for a chain 137 signature. If you already hold a Polygon token, swap that token for POL locally.

sections.heading: Keep some POL unspent
sections.body: The POL you receive pays the next transaction. Sending the entire balance onward can leave other tokens stuck. Chain id 137 is inexpensive next to mainnet and still charges a fee. Leave a remainder sized for an approval plus a swap.

faqs.question: Does this unwrap WETH into ETH first?
faqs.answer: The result you hold is native POL on chain id 137, not native ETH on Ethereum. WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is what you approve on Etherscan. A local unwrap credits ETH on chain id 1 and stops. If ETH on Ethereum is the goal, do not open this pair.

faqs.question: How do I confirm the POL arrived?
faqs.answer: Set the wallet to chain id 137 and check the native balance on Polygonscan. The marker 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is not a contract page you need to open. Blocks are about 2 seconds. If the wallet is still on Ethereum, you will keep seeing ETH and miss the POL.

faqs.question: What if I hold WETH and no ETH?
faqs.answer: Unwrap a small slice of WETH to native ETH on Ethereum so the approval can pay gas. Then spend the remaining WETH on this route. Chain id 1 will not accept WETH as a fee. The POL you receive later cannot pay that first transaction.

intro:
Swap WBTC from Ethereum to USDC on Polygon. Holders of wrapped bitcoin who need Circle's native USDC on chain 137 spend WBTC and receive that dollar.

WBTC is an ERC-20, not bitcoin on the Bitcoin chain. You approve 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 on Etherscan. It uses 8 decimals. A Bitcoin address cannot receive it. The dollars you receive are 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 on Polygonscan, Circle's native USDC, 6 decimals. USDC.e at 0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174 is not the output. Gas to leave is ETH on chain id 1. Import the native USDC from Polygonscan once the wallet is on chain id 137. The bridged USDC.e row will stay unchanged, which is easy to misread as a failed route.
description: Swap WBTC from Ethereum to USDC on Polygon when you want Circle native USDC on Polygon and the source is wrapped bitcoin, an ERC-20, on Ethereum in your wallet.

sections.heading: Not a Bitcoin withdrawal
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool if the destination is a Bitcoin address. WBTC stays an Ethereum token until the route spends it, and the output is a dollar on Polygon. Redeeming WBTC for bitcoin, where a custodian allows it, does not use Polygonscan and does not pay 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359.

sections.heading: Eight decimals in, six out, and not USDC.e
sections.body: Check 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 on Etherscan for the WBTC you spend. Check 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359 on Polygonscan for the native USDC you receive. The bridged USDC.e contract will not move. A mixed-up decimal field will invent the size of the balance.

sections.heading: ETH to start, POL to finish
sections.body: WBTC does not pay Ethereum gas. Keep ETH on chain id 1. Native USDC does not pay Polygon gas. Keep POL on chain id 137, where blocks are about 2 seconds. [Polygon](/chains/polygon) is the network the dollars land on. Mainnet blocks are about 12 seconds.

sections.heading: A mainnet WBTC sale is enough for mainnet dollars
sections.body: WBTC already trades against Circle USDC on Ethereum. Use that pool when the dollars should stay on chain id 1 as 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. This bridge is for a wallet that needs the Polygon native contract. Selling on mainnet never creates it.

faqs.question: Can the receiver be a Bitcoin address?
faqs.answer: No. The output is Circle's native USDC on Polygon, 0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359. The input is WBTC at 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 on Etherscan, an ERC-20 with 8 decimals. Neither side is the Bitcoin network. Use an EVM address that can switch to chain id 137.

faqs.question: Why does a small WBTC figure represent a large dollar value?
faqs.answer: WBTC uses 8 decimals, so a fraction of one token is a meaningful amount of wrapped bitcoin. The USDC you receive is set by the quote you sign, which this page does not fix. Read the minimum on that quote. The native USDC then displays with 6 decimals on Polygonscan.

faqs.question: What do I hold besides WBTC?
faqs.answer: ETH on Ethereum, because chain id 1 will not take WBTC as a fee. POL on Polygon after arrival, because native USDC will not pay chain id 137. Blocks are about 12 seconds on the way out and about 2 seconds on Polygon. Both gas coins sit apart from the two token contracts.

intro:
Swap WBTC from Ethereum to USDT on Polygon. A chain 137 payment in Tether can start from wrapped bitcoin held as an ERC-20 on Ethereum.

Approve WBTC at 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 on Etherscan, 8 decimals. It is not a Bitcoin-network coin. Receive 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F on Polygonscan, Tether on Polygon, 6 decimals. Ethereum USDT at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is not the balance that increases. You pay ETH gas on chain id 1, where a block takes about 12 seconds. The recipient has to be on chain id 137, watching Polygonscan, or the Tether payment is invisible to them. An Etherscan watch on Ethereum USDT will not update. Send the network name with the amount. Confirm it on Polygonscan.
description: Swap WBTC from Ethereum to USDT on Polygon when a Polygon wallet needs Tether and the source is the wrapped bitcoin ERC-20 on Ethereum mainnet in your wallet.

sections.heading: Two contracts name the whole pair
sections.body: Spend 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 on Etherscan. Receive 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F on Polygonscan. WBTC in, Polygon USDT out. If either explorer shows a different contract under a similar name, stop. Copies reuse the first and last characters of a popular address.

sections.heading: An Ethereum invoice wants different Tether
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when the invoice prints 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. Sell WBTC for that Tether on mainnet. Bridge when the invoice says Polygon and prints the Polygonscan address. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is the signing order.

sections.heading: Bitcoin chain is the wrong destination
sections.body: Sending WBTC to a Bitcoin address will not redeem it, and this route will not either. You finish holding Tether on chain id 137. If the goal is bitcoin in a Bitcoin wallet, use the redemption path your custodian documents. Polygonscan will not show a bitcoin UTXO.

sections.heading: Fees around an 8 decimal token
sections.body: Keep ETH for the Ethereum approval. Keep POL for the chain 137 transfer that follows, because the USDT cannot pay it. Blocks on Polygon are about 2 seconds. Size the trade from the quote, and remember that 8 decimal units are easy to mistype by a factor of ten.

faqs.question: Is WBTC bitcoin for this payment?
faqs.answer: No. WBTC at 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 is an ERC-20 on Ethereum, 8 decimals, checked on Etherscan. This route spends it and pays Polygon USDT. A Bitcoin wallet cannot hold either token. Treat the position as an Ethereum asset until you redeem it through a separate process.

faqs.question: Which Tether should the recipient watch?
faqs.answer: Polygonscan for 0xc2132D05D31c914a87C6611C10748AEb04B58e8F, on chain id 137. Watching Etherscan for 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 will show no change from this route. Ask them to switch networks. The token uses 6 decimals, like Ethereum USDT, and it is still a different contract. Ask them to switch networks before they check.

faqs.question: What if I am still trading on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: Stay there. WBTC and Tether already have a mainnet market, and the output is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. This bridge is the wrong tool for that market. Use it when the Tether has to be the Polygon contract because the next wallet or pool is on chain 137.

intro:
Swap WBTC from Ethereum to WETH on Polygon. Traders moving wrapped bitcoin into wrapped ETH on chain 137 receive Polygon WETH.

You spend WBTC at 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 on Etherscan, an 8 decimal ERC-20. You receive 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 on Polygonscan. That is not mainnet WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, and it is not bitcoin. Chain id 1 gas is ETH, about 12 seconds a block. Chain id 137 gas is POL, about 2 seconds a block. The Polygon WETH shows up only after the wallet leaves Ethereum. Etherscan's WETH balance does not record this route, so a mainnet watch will look unchanged.
description: Swap WBTC from Ethereum to WETH on Polygon when you want Polygon WETH on chain 137 and the source is the wrapped bitcoin ERC-20 on Ethereum before you approve.

sections.heading: Two wrappers on two chains
sections.body: Selling WBTC for WETH on Ethereum would leave you in 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. This route leaves you in Polygon WETH. It is the wrong tool for a Bitcoin-network withdrawal and the wrong tool for a mainnet WETH balance. Use it when the ETH book you want is on chain 137.

sections.heading: Check Polygon WETH, not the native line
sections.body: Polygonscan must show 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619. The WBTC that decreases is 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 on Etherscan. Native ETH would have been the 0xEeee placeholder, and it is not the output. If your Ethereum ETH balance is what you wanted to grow, you opened the wrong pair.

sections.heading: Gas that neither wrapper can pay
sections.body: WBTC will not pay the Ethereum approval. Hold ETH on chain id 1. Polygon WETH will not pay the chain 137 transfer. Hold POL. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is only the starting side. The quote you sign is the amount you accept. This article does not publish a price.

sections.heading: When the source-chain pool is the better book
sections.body: Someone who wants to rotate WBTC into WETH without leaving Ethereum should stay on chain id 1, where both contracts already trade. The pool being on the source chain is the reason to skip the bridge. This pair is for a desk that needs the Polygonscan WETH specifically.

faqs.question: Is the WETH I receive the Ethereum WETH contract?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Etherscan. This route pays 0x7ceB23fD6bC0adD59E62ac25578270cFf1b9f619 on Polygonscan. Native ETH is the gas coin on chain id 1. Three different things use the ETH name. The contract you can spend on Polygon is the Polygon one.

faqs.question: Can this WBTC go to a Bitcoin address instead?
faqs.answer: Not on this route. WBTC at 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 is an ERC-20 on Ethereum. The output is an ERC-20 on Polygon. Neither explorer is a Bitcoin explorer. If you need bitcoin on the Bitcoin chain, this pair is the wrong tool. This pair cannot do that job.

faqs.question: What fails if the wallet holds only WBTC?
faqs.answer: The Ethereum transaction. Chain id 1 charges ETH, and WBTC cannot substitute. Add ETH before you approve 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599. On the far side, add POL or the Polygon WETH will be unable to move. Blocks are about 12 seconds on Ethereum and about 2 seconds on Polygon.

intro:
Swap WBTC from Ethereum to POL on Polygon. A chain 137 wallet that needs gas can spend wrapped bitcoin on Ethereum and receive native POL.

WBTC at 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 is an 8 decimal ERC-20 on Etherscan, not a coin on the Bitcoin chain. Native POL is marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE and shows up as the gas balance on Polygonscan for chain id 137. You approve the WBTC contract and pay that approval in ETH. Ethereum blocks are about 12 seconds. You do not import the POL placeholder. Switch to chain id 137 and read the native balance on Polygonscan.
description: Swap WBTC from Ethereum to POL on Polygon when a Polygon wallet needs POL for gas and the source is the wrapped bitcoin ERC-20 on Ethereum before you approve.

sections.heading: Chain 137 gas is the reason
sections.body: Wrapped bitcoin cannot pay a Polygon fee. If the next signature has to happen on chain id 137, the wallet needs native POL. This pair turns WBTC you already hold on Ethereum into that gas coin. It is the wrong shape if you wanted USDC or USDT to arrive instead.

sections.heading: This never becomes a bitcoin send
sections.body: A Bitcoin address will not accept WBTC, and it will not accept POL. Etherscan is where 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 decreases. Polygonscan is where the native POL balance increases. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) describes that split. It is not a Bitcoin bridge.

sections.heading: Use the Ethereum pool when you are staying
sections.body: If you want ETH, WETH, USDC, or USDT on mainnet, sell WBTC there. This route is the wrong tool for those balances. If you already hold Polygon assets and only need a little POL, swap those assets on chain 137. Bridge from Ethereum when the wrapped bitcoin is still on mainnet.

sections.heading: Leave POL for the next click
sections.body: Chain id 137 blocks about every 2 seconds and charges POL. The coin you just received is that fee token, so it can pay a follow-up trade. Spending all of it strands any other token in the same wallet. Some wallets still label the balance MATIC.

faqs.question: Should I import POL by contract address?
faqs.answer: No. Native POL uses 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE and appears as the gas balance once the wallet is on chain id 137. Importing that string creates a junk row. Confirm the increase on Polygonscan's native balance. The ERC-20 you approve is WBTC, on Etherscan.

faqs.question: What is WBTC if it is not bitcoin?
faqs.answer: An ERC-20 at 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599, 8 decimals, on Ethereum. This route can spend that contract. It cannot move coins on the Bitcoin network. If your goal is a Bitcoin wallet, stop. If your goal is POL gas funded from that ERC-20, this is the pair.

faqs.question: Why is ETH still required?
faqs.answer: Because the spend starts on chain id 1. WBTC cannot pay Ethereum gas, and the POL you will receive does not exist on Ethereum yet. Hold ETH for the approval and the send. Blocks are about 12 seconds. After arrival, POL covers chain id 137.

intro:
Swap USDC from Ethereum to USDT on Arbitrum One. Traders who need Tether on Arbitrum One spend Circle USDC on Ethereum and receive that USDT.

This page is for a wallet on chain id 42161, Arbitrum One, not Arbitrum Nova. You approve Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan, 6 decimals. You receive Tether at 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 on Arbiscan, also 6 decimals. Ethereum Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is not the credit. A mainnet pool already swaps these stables if both should stay on chain id 1. Gas to leave is ETH, and blocks there are about 12 seconds. Gas on Arbitrum One is also ETH, and it is a separate balance from the ETH you spend on Ethereum.
description: Swap USDC from Ethereum to USDT on Arbitrum One when an Arbitrum One wallet needs Tether and you already hold Circle USDC on Ethereum before you approve.

sections.heading: A mainnet stable swap stays on mainnet
sections.body: Circle USDC and Tether already trade on Ethereum. This route is the wrong tool for that rotation. Open it when the Tether has to be the Arbitrum One contract. A same-chain swap never creates 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 and never switches the wallet to chain id 42161.

sections.heading: Arbiscan is where this USDT lives
sections.body: Match 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 before you forward the funds. The approval on Etherscan is only 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. Circle's native USDC on Arbitrum One, 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831, is a different dollar and is not this output.

sections.heading: ETH on Ethereum, then ETH on Arbitrum One
sections.body: Both networks charge ETH, and the balances do not merge. Chain id 1 needs ETH to move the USDC. Chain id 42161 needs its own ETH to move the USDT after it arrives. [Arbitrum One](/chains/arbitrum) is not Nova. The received Tether cannot pay either fee.

sections.heading: Who wants this Tether
sections.body: Use it when an Arbitrum One app, invoice, or pool quotes this USDT contract. Both legs are 6 decimals, which makes the unit look familiar and does not make the contracts the same. You hold Tether on Arbitrum One, not a claim on the Ethereum USDC you spent.

faqs.question: Is Arbitrum USDT the same contract as Ethereum USDT?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum Tether is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan. This route pays 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 on Arbiscan. Both use 6 decimals. Switch the wallet to Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, and match the full address. Arbitrum Nova is a different network and will not show this balance.

faqs.question: Does the USDT pay gas on Arbitrum One?
faqs.answer: No. Gas on chain id 42161 is ETH, and that ETH is not the same balance as ETH on Ethereum. USDT is an ERC-20. If the Arbitrum wallet has no ETH, the Tether can sit on Arbiscan until you add gas. The send on Ethereum also needs ETH, because Circle USDC cannot pay chain id 1.

faqs.question: What if I only wanted USDT on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: Sell Circle USDC for Tether on Ethereum and stop at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. This bridge is the wrong tool for that balance. Use it when an Arbitrum One address expects 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 and the dollars you hold are still Circle USDC on mainnet.

intro:
Swap USDC from Ethereum to ETH on Arbitrum One. A wallet that needs ETH for gas on chain 42161 spends Circle USDC on Ethereum and receives native ETH there.

The output is native ETH, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. On this route that placeholder means ETH on Arbitrum One, the gas coin Arbiscan shows for chain id 42161, not Arbitrum Nova. It is a different balance from native ETH on Ethereum. You spend Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan. You still need a little ETH on chain id 1 to pay for that send. Mainnet blocks are about 12 seconds. The ETH you receive can pay later transactions on Arbitrum One.
description: Swap USDC from Ethereum to ETH on Arbitrum One when you need ETH for gas on Arbitrum One and you will spend Circle USDC held on Ethereum before you approve.

sections.heading: This ETH is the gas coin on Arbitrum One
sections.body: People open this pair because an Arbitrum One wallet full of tokens still cannot move them without ETH. Receiving native ETH fixes that. Receiving USDT or ARB would not. The marker 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE names the gas coin. Do not import it as a custom ERC-20.

sections.heading: The USDC you approve on Etherscan
sections.body: Spend 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, Circle USDC, 6 decimals. Circle's native USDC on Arbitrum One is 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 and is not the input. If your dollars are already on chain 42161, swap them for ETH there. This bridge is the wrong tool for that wallet.

sections.heading: L1 ETH and L2 ETH are separate
sections.body: Selling USDC for ETH on Ethereum leaves you with mainnet gas. It does not fund Arbitrum One. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is why the source chain collects its own fee first. Keep ETH on chain id 1 for the USDC send, then use the received ETH on chain id 42161.

sections.heading: Nova is the wrong network
sections.body: Arbitrum One is chain id 42161. Nova is a different chain. A wallet pointed at Nova will not show this ETH in the gas line you care about. Switch to Arbitrum One and read the native balance on Arbiscan. Leave some ETH unspent for the next signature.

faqs.question: Will this ETH show up on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. The ETH you receive is the native gas balance on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161. Etherscan's native ETH line is the coin you may have spent as gas, not the receipt. Switch the wallet off Ethereum and off Arbitrum Nova. Arbiscan shows the gas balance for the address on Arbitrum One.

faqs.question: Do I approve an ETH contract?
faqs.answer: You approve Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. Native ETH on the destination is the placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, not a token to import. You also need ETH on chain id 1 so the USDC transfer can pay gas. The USDC itself cannot cover that fee.

faqs.question: Is buying ETH on Ethereum enough?
faqs.answer: Only if the next signature is on chain id 1. Mainnet ETH does not pay Arbitrum One gas. This route is the one that delivers native ETH on chain id 42161 from Circle USDC. Skip it when you wanted a stablecoin to remain a stablecoin on Arbitrum One.

intro:
Swap USDC from Ethereum to WETH on Arbitrum One. A chain 42161 wallet that wants wrapped ETH spends Circle USDC on Ethereum and receives Arbitrum WETH.

The WETH that arrives is 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on Arbiscan. It is not Ethereum WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, and it is not the native ETH that pays gas on Arbitrum One. You spend Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan. Chain id 1 gas is ETH, with blocks about every 12 seconds. Chain id 42161 gas is also ETH, a separate balance. This route does not deliver that gas coin. Arbitrum Nova is not the destination. Switch to chain id 42161 before you look for the wrapped token on Arbiscan.
description: Swap USDC from Ethereum to WETH on Arbitrum One when you want Arbitrum WETH on chain 42161 and you will spend Circle USDC held on Ethereum before you approve.

sections.heading: Two WETH contracts
sections.body: Approve only 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan. Watch 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on Arbiscan. If the wallet is still on chain id 1, Arbitrum WETH will not appear in the mainnet WETH line. Switch to Arbitrum One, not Nova, before you decide the funds are missing.

sections.heading: Wrapped ETH does not pay the L2 fee
sections.body: A fresh Arbitrum One wallet can receive this WETH and then be unable to swap it. Hold native ETH on chain id 42161 first, or pick the route whose output is native ETH. This pair is the wrong tool when the gap is gas rather than a WETH position.

sections.heading: Buying WETH on Ethereum stays home
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when you want 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. That wrap and those pools stay on chain id 1. Use this page when an Arbitrum One pool lists WETH and means the Arbiscan contract. [Arbitrum One](/chains/arbitrum) is the network that contract belongs to.

sections.heading: What this WETH is for
sections.body: Books on chain 42161 that say WETH usually mean 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1, 18 decimals. Landing it from Circle USDC lets you enter those books. You still pay ETH to leave Ethereum. The quote you sign is the amount you accept.

faqs.question: Is Arbitrum WETH the same as mainnet WETH?
faqs.answer: No. Mainnet WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Etherscan. This route pays 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on Arbiscan. Both track ETH as ERC-20s, and a pool on one chain will not take the other contract. Check that the wallet is on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, not Nova.

faqs.question: Which token do I approve?
faqs.answer: Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan. You do not approve Arbitrum WETH before it arrives. You do need ETH on chain id 1 for gas. Blocks there are about 12 seconds. USDC cannot pay that fee. The approval and the send can be two transactions.

faqs.question: What if I needed ETH for gas instead of WETH?
faqs.answer: Choose the route that outputs native ETH, the 0xEeee placeholder, on Arbitrum One. This pair delivers an ERC-20. WETH cannot pay chain id 42161 fees. If the pool you care about asks for 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1, then this is the contract to receive.

intro:
Swap USDC from Ethereum to ARB on Arbitrum One. Someone who wants the ARB token on chain 42161 spends Circle USDC on Ethereum and receives that token.

ARB is 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 on Arbiscan. It is the governance token. It does not pay gas on Arbitrum One. Gas there is ETH, a separate balance from ETH on Ethereum. You spend Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan. The destination is Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, not Arbitrum Nova. Mainnet blocks are about 12 seconds, and the send still needs ETH on chain id 1.
description: Swap USDC from Ethereum to ARB on Arbitrum One when you want the ARB token on chain 42161 and you will spend Circle USDC from Ethereum mainnet in your wallet.

sections.heading: ARB does not pay the network fee
sections.body: After this route you hold 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. Transfers of that token still cost ETH on chain id 42161. If the wallet has never held ETH on Arbitrum One, the ARB can arrive and sit. Native ETH on Ethereum is what pays the USDC send, and this route does not leave that balance in place of the dollars.

sections.heading: Match USDC on Etherscan first
sections.body: Approve only 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. That is Circle USDC, 6 decimals. ARB is an 18 decimal token on Arbiscan. A copy that shares the ARB ticker and a different address is a different market. Confirm the full string before you trade it onward.

sections.heading: Skip this if you wanted gas or a dollar
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when you want native ETH on Arbitrum One, or Circle USDC to stay a dollar. Selling USDC for ETH or USDT on Ethereum never mints 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. Use it when an Arbitrum One app asks for the ARB token. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the general mechanic.

sections.heading: Where the ARB token is spent
sections.body: Governance, pools, and transfers on Arbitrum One that name ARB mean this contract. You still need ETH on chain id 42161 to move it. Nova will not show the same balance. Switch the wallet to Arbitrum One and read Arbiscan before you vote or deposit.

faqs.question: Can I pay Arbitrum gas with ARB?
faqs.answer: No. ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 is an ERC-20 on Arbiscan. Gas on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, is ETH. If the destination wallet has no ETH, the ARB sits until you add some. ETH on Ethereum is a third balance and does not cover chain 42161 fees.

faqs.question: Which USDC do I approve?
faqs.answer: Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan. Native USDC on Arbitrum One is a different address and is not the token you send. Keep ETH on chain id 1 for gas. Blocks there are about 12 seconds. The ARB you receive is only visible on Arbitrum One, not on Nova.

faqs.question: Is this the right route for ETH gas?
faqs.answer: No. This pair delivers the ARB token, not native ETH. If the wallet cannot pay fees on chain id 42161, choose a route whose output is the 0xEeee gas placeholder. Use this page when you specifically want 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548. Use this page only for that ARB contract.

intro:
Swap USDT from Ethereum to USDC on Arbitrum One. Wallets that need Circle's native USDC on chain 42161 spend Ethereum Tether and receive that dollar.

You send Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan, 6 decimals. You receive 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on Arbiscan, Circle's native USDC on Arbitrum One, also 6 decimals. The older bridged USDC.e at 0xFF970A61A04b1cA14834A43f5dE4533eBDDB5CC8 is a different contract and is not this output. The chain is Arbitrum One, id 42161, not Nova. Gas to leave is ETH on Ethereum. Gas after arrival is ETH on Arbitrum One, a separate balance. If an app printed the USDC.e address, stop. This route credits only the native contract on Arbiscan, and the bridged dollar will not move.
description: Swap USDT from Ethereum to USDC on Arbitrum One for Circle native USDC on Arbitrum One, starting from Tether you already hold on Ethereum mainnet today.

sections.heading: Native USDC is not USDC.e
sections.body: Apps on Arbitrum One split the dollar. Circle's native token is 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831. Bridged USDC.e is 0xFF970A61A04b1cA14834A43f5dE4533eBDDB5CC8. This route pays the native contract. If an allowlist prints the USDC.e address, these dollars will not credit. Read it on Arbiscan before you deposit.

sections.heading: Tether is what leaves Ethereum
sections.body: Approve 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 only. That approval burns ETH on chain id 1. Circle USDC on Ethereum, 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, is not the token you send and not the token you receive. Blocks on Ethereum are about 12 seconds.

sections.heading: Stay on Ethereum to flip the stable
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when both dollars should remain on mainnet. USDT and Circle USDC already have a chain id 1 book. Bridge when the receiving contract is native USDC on Arbitrum One. [Arbitrum One](/chains/arbitrum) is where that contract is spent, and where a separate ETH balance pays the fee.

sections.heading: ETH on the L2 after a 6 decimal dollar
sections.body: The received USDC cannot pay gas. Chain id 42161 charges ETH. That ETH is not the ETH sitting on Ethereum. Keep some on the Arbitrum One wallet or the new dollars wait. Nova is the wrong place to look for them.

faqs.question: Which USDC address should I watch on Arbitrum?
faqs.answer: 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on Arbiscan. That is Circle's native USDC on Arbitrum One. USDC.e at 0xFF970A61A04b1cA14834A43f5dE4533eBDDB5CC8 will not increase because of this route. If the wallet shows two USDC rows, import the native contract. Chain id 42161 is the network, not Nova.

faqs.question: What do I approve on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan. Keep ETH in that wallet for gas on chain id 1. USDT cannot pay the fee, and the approval may be its own transaction. Blocks are about 12 seconds. The USDC appears only after you switch the wallet to Arbitrum One.

faqs.question: Is this the same as USDT to USDC on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: The tickers match and the contracts do not. On Ethereum the USDC would be 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. This route delivers 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831. Use the mainnet pool when the dollars should stay on chain id 1. Use this page when Arbitrum One is where the USDC has to sit.

intro:
Swap USDT from Ethereum to ETH on Arbitrum One. A chain 42161 wallet that needs gas spends Ethereum Tether and receives native ETH on Arbitrum One.

Native ETH on the destination is 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, the gas coin Arbiscan shows for Arbitrum One. It is not WETH, and it is not the ETH balance on Ethereum. You approve Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan. If your Tether is already on Arbitrum One at 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9, swap it for ETH there instead. Chain id 1 still needs ETH to move the mainnet USDT. The destination is not Arbitrum Nova. Switch to Arbitrum One and read the native gas line on Arbiscan. Nova will not show this ETH.  Confirm it on Arbiscan.
description: Swap USDT from Ethereum to ETH on Arbitrum One when you need ETH for gas on Arbitrum One and you will spend Tether held on Ethereum mainnet before you approve.

sections.heading: Already on Arbitrum One? Swap there
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when the USDT is already at 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9. Trade that token for ETH on chain 42161. Bridging from Ethereum moves 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. Check which explorer holds the Tether before you sign.

sections.heading: The placeholder means L2 ETH here
sections.body: Do not import 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. On this path it means ETH on Arbitrum One. On an Ethereum path it means ETH on chain id 1. After the route, switch to chain id 42161 and read the native line on Arbiscan. Nova will show a different gas balance.

sections.heading: ETH for the Tether approval
sections.body: Chain id 1 charges ETH and blocks about every 12 seconds. Tether cannot substitute. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is where that signature happens. The ETH you receive on Arbitrum One can pay the next transaction there. It cannot refund the mainnet fee.

sections.heading: Leave L2 ETH for the follow-up
sections.body: If you spend the entire Arbitrum ETH balance on the next transfer, later token moves stall. Keep a remainder sized for an approval and a swap. This pair funds that remainder from Ethereum Tether. It does not replace a dollar you still need on chain 42161.

faqs.question: I already hold USDT on Arbitrum One. Should I use this page?
faqs.answer: No. This page starts from Ethereum Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan. USDT at 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 can be swapped for ETH on Arbitrum One. Using this bridge would move a mainnet balance you may be leaving in place on purpose. Use a same-chain swap on Arbitrum One instead.

faqs.question: Is 0xEeee an ETH contract I should import?
faqs.answer: It is a placeholder for the native gas coin, not a contract to import. On chain id 42161 that coin is ETH. Arbiscan shows it as the native balance. Importing the placeholder creates a useless row. Switch the wallet to Arbitrum One, not Nova, and read the gas line.

faqs.question: What else belongs in the Ethereum wallet?
faqs.answer: Tether plus ETH. The USDT contract cannot pay gas on chain id 1, and blocks there are about 12 seconds. ETH you will receive on Arbitrum One does not exist on Ethereum yet, so it cannot pay the fee either. Add a small ETH balance before you approve.

intro:
Swap USDT from Ethereum to WETH on Arbitrum One. Traders who want wrapped ETH on chain 42161 spend Tether from Ethereum and receive Arbitrum WETH.

The output is 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on Arbiscan, an 18 decimal ERC-20. It will not pay gas on Arbitrum One. You spend Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan, 6 decimals. Ethereum WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is a different contract. Chain id 1 gas is ETH, about 12 seconds a block. Chain id 42161 gas is a separate ETH balance. The network is Arbitrum One, not Nova. Switch to chain id 42161 and import the Arbiscan WETH before you assume the transfer missed. The mainnet WETH row does not move.  Confirm the WETH on Arbiscan.
description: Swap USDT from Ethereum to WETH on Arbitrum One when you want Arbitrum WETH on chain 42161 and you will spend Tether held on Ethereum before you approve.

sections.heading: Sell Tether for WETH on mainnet if you are staying
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when the WETH you want is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. That pool is already on Ethereum. Bridge when the book uses Arbitrum WETH. A chain id 1 swap never mints 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1.

sections.heading: Tether in, Arbitrum WETH out
sections.body: Etherscan should show a spend of 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. Arbiscan should show a credit of 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Tether is 6 decimals. This WETH is 18. One decimal field for both will misread a balance. Switch to chain id 42161 before you look.

sections.heading: Neither output nor input pays both fees
sections.body: USDT cannot pay Ethereum gas, so hold ETH on chain id 1. Arbitrum WETH cannot pay chain 42161 gas, so hold ETH on Arbitrum One. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is the signing order. If the missing piece is L2 gas, this pair delivers the wrong asset.

sections.heading: Pools that list WETH on Arbitrum One
