sections.body: They mean the Arbiscan contract. Receiving it from Ethereum Tether lets you join those pools. You do not receive mainnet WETH, native ETH on either chain, or the ARB token. The quote on the screen is the number you judge. This page does not set it.

faqs.question: Will my Ethereum WETH balance increase?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum WETH stays at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Etherscan. This route pays 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on Arbiscan. Switch the wallet to Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, before you look. Nova will not show it. If the wallet is still on Ethereum, the new WETH is invisible.

faqs.question: Why does the send ask for ETH when I am spending USDT?
faqs.answer: Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is an ERC-20. Moving it on chain id 1 costs ETH. The approval can be its own transaction. A wallet that holds only USDT cannot finish. Add ETH for gas. Blocks are about 12 seconds. ETH on Arbitrum One is a later, separate requirement.

faqs.question: Does this WETH pay the next swap's fee?
faqs.answer: It can be the asset you sell. The network fee is ETH on chain id 42161. If that gas balance is empty, the WETH can be visible on Arbiscan and still be stuck. Fund ETH on Arbitrum One, or choose a route that outputs native ETH.

intro:
Swap USDT from Ethereum to ARB on Arbitrum One. Someone who wants the ARB token on chain 42161 spends Ethereum Tether and receives that governance token.

ARB is 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 on Arbiscan. It does not pay gas. Gas on Arbitrum One is ETH, separate from ETH on Ethereum. You approve Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan, 6 decimals. The destination is chain id 42161, not Arbitrum Nova. If your Tether is already the Arbitrum contract 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9, buy ARB there. This page starts from mainnet Tether and still needs ETH on chain id 1. Blocks there are about 12 seconds. Switch to Arbitrum One and import the ARB contract from Arbiscan before you try to move it.
description: Swap USDT from Ethereum to ARB on Arbitrum One when you want the ARB token on chain 42161 and you will spend Tether held on Ethereum mainnet in your wallet.

sections.heading: ARB arrives, ETH still has to be there
sections.body: 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 cannot pay a chain 42161 fee. Hold ETH on Arbitrum One or the token sits on Arbiscan. The Tether you spent cannot pay the Ethereum fee either. Budget both ETH balances before you treat the ARB as spendable.

sections.heading: Mainnet Tether is the approval
sections.body: The contract that decreases is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan. Arbitrum USDT is a different address and is not the input. A same-chain buy of ARB on Ethereum, if a pool exists there, would not be this Arbiscan token. Check the explorer that matches the chain you will trade on.

sections.heading: Wrong tool for gas or for a dollar
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when you need native ETH on Arbitrum One or when you want USDC. Those are different outputs. [Arbitrum One](/chains/arbitrum) is where ARB is the governance asset and ETH is the fee. Nova will not display this balance.

sections.heading: After the token shows on Arbiscan
sections.body: Switch the wallet to chain id 42161 before you vote, transfer, or deposit. ARB uses 18 decimals, unlike the 6 decimal Tether you sold. A wallet with the wrong decimal field will misstate the size. Read the token page on Arbiscan.

faqs.question: Does ARB pay gas on Arbitrum One?
faqs.answer: No. The token at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 is an ERC-20. Gas is ETH on chain id 42161. ETH on Ethereum is a different balance and does not cover those fees. If you needed gas, pick a route that outputs native ETH. Use this pair when the ARB token itself is the position.

faqs.question: Which USDT do I approve?
faqs.answer: Ethereum Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan. Keep ETH beside it for chain id 1 gas. Blocks are about 12 seconds. USDT already at 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 belongs on Arbitrum One and should be swapped there, not bridged again from mainnet. Keep the wallet on chain id 1 for that approval.

faqs.question: Will I see ARB if my wallet is on Nova?
faqs.answer: No. This route delivers ARB on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161. Nova is a different network. Set the wallet to Arbitrum One and read 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 on Arbiscan. The Ethereum wallet will not show that token in its mainnet list. Set the network before you search for the token.

intro:
Swap DAI from Ethereum to USDC on Arbitrum One. Holders leaving Maker DAI for Circle's dollar on chain 42161 spend DAI and receive native USDC.

DAI is Maker's collateral dollar at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Etherscan, 18 decimals. The USDC you receive is 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on Arbiscan, Circle's native USDC, 6 decimals. Bridged USDC.e at 0xFF970A61A04b1cA14834A43f5dE4533eBDDB5CC8 is not the receipt. The chain is Arbitrum One, not Nova. You pay ETH on chain id 1, about 12 seconds a block. You later need a separate ETH balance on chain id 42161, because the USDC cannot pay gas. Import the native USDC from Arbiscan after you switch to chain id 42161. A wallet that only tracks USDC.e will look empty, and Nova will not show the dollars either.  Confirm the contract on Arbiscan.
description: Swap DAI from Ethereum to USDC on Arbitrum One when you are leaving Maker DAI for Circle's native USDC that has to sit on Arbitrum One before you approve.

sections.heading: Watch native USDC, not USDC.e
sections.body: Arbiscan should show 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831. If you imported only 0xFF970A61A04b1cA14834A43f5dE4533eBDDB5CC8, the wallet will look empty. Decimals also change, from 18 on Maker DAI to 6 on Circle's native USDC. Read both token pages before the next transfer.

sections.heading: The Maker contract is the approval
sections.body: 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F is the DAI that decreases. Circle USDC on Ethereum, 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, is what a mainnet DAI to USDC swap would pay. This route does not pay that contract.

sections.heading: Stay in DAI on Ethereum when that is the job
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool if you want Circle USDC on chain id 1 or if you want to remain in DAI. Both are mainnet actions. Bridge when an Arbitrum One app whitelisted the native USDC. [Arbitrum One](/chains/arbitrum) is where the separate ETH balance then pays for using it.

sections.heading: Two ETH balances around the decimal change
sections.body: ETH pays the Ethereum approval. ETH on chain id 42161 pays any later move of the USDC. The USDC cannot sponsor that second fee. Hold L2 ETH before you deposit the new dollars. Looking on Nova will not reveal them.

faqs.question: Does this give me Circle USDC on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. It spends Maker DAI and pays Circle's native USDC on Arbitrum One, 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on Arbiscan. Ethereum Circle USDC remains 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan. If that mainnet contract is what you wanted, trade DAI for it on chain id 1. Trade on Ethereum if that is the dollar you want.

faqs.question: Why can the USDC display look nothing like the DAI amount?
faqs.answer: DAI uses 18 decimals and Arbitrum native USDC uses 6. A wrong decimal field shifts the display by many zeros. Check decimals on Arbiscan for 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831. Judge the trade by the quote you sign. This page does not set that quote.

faqs.question: What if the app listed USDC.e?
faqs.answer: Do not deposit this output there. USDC.e is 0xFF970A61A04b1cA14834A43f5dE4533eBDDB5CC8. This route pays the native contract on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161. Sending native USDC into a pool that wants the bridged token will not credit you. Match the allowlist, not the USDC ticker.

intro:
Swap DAI from Ethereum to USDT on Arbitrum One. Someone paying Tether on chain 42161 can spend Maker DAI from Ethereum and receive that USDT.

You approve Maker DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Etherscan, 18 decimals. You receive Tether at 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 on Arbiscan, 6 decimals. Ethereum Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 does not increase. Issuers differ: Maker on the way out, Tether on the way in. The network is Arbitrum One, not Nova. Gas to leave is ETH on chain id 1. Gas afterward is ETH on chain id 42161, and the USDT cannot pay it. Tell the payee to watch Arbiscan on chain id 42161. An Etherscan tab open to Ethereum Tether will stay flat for the whole transfer.  Confirm the USDT contract on Arbiscan before you pay.
description: Swap DAI from Ethereum to USDT on Arbitrum One when an Arbitrum One wallet needs Tether and the source balance is Maker DAI on Ethereum before you approve.

sections.heading: Arbiscan USDT is the payment asset
sections.body: Expect 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9. A payee who printed the Ethereum USDT address will not see this transfer on Etherscan. Tell them the network is Arbitrum One, chain id 42161. The decimal change from 18 to 6 is a display detail, not a second payment.

sections.heading: DAI for Ethereum Tether is a local swap
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when the invoice is on mainnet. Sell Maker DAI for 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 and stop. Bridge only when the Tether contract is the Arbitrum one. A chain id 1 pool already covers the local job.

sections.heading: ETH on the way out and on the way in
sections.body: Chain id 1 blocks about every 12 seconds and charges ETH. DAI cannot pay it. Chain id 42161 charges its own ETH. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is why each chain keeps its own fee. The received USDT is an ERC-20 on Arbiscan.

sections.heading: Approve only the Maker contract
sections.body: 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F is the DAI this route can spend. Confirm it on Etherscan, then confirm the USDT string on Arbiscan after the wallet is on Arbitrum One. A Nova wallet will not show the credit.

faqs.question: Will Ethereum USDT increase?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum Tether stays at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan. The new tokens are 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 on Arbiscan. Look there after you switch to Arbitrum One, chain id 42161. Both can be labeled USDT. The address is how you tell the payment landed.

faqs.question: Why do the decimals change?
faqs.answer: Maker DAI uses 18 decimals. Arbitrum USDT uses 6, like Ethereum Tether. If the wallet still uses DAI's decimals, the USDT row looks wrong by many zeros. Re-import 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 from Arbiscan. Trust the quote you sign. This page does not set it.

faqs.question: What gas do I need?
faqs.answer: ETH on Ethereum to spend the DAI, because chain id 1 charges ETH. ETH on Arbitrum One to move the USDT afterward, because chain id 42161 charges ETH and the two balances are separate. The route delivers neither gas coin. Blocks on Ethereum are about 12 seconds.

intro:
Swap DAI from Ethereum to ETH on Arbitrum One. A wallet that needs ETH for gas on chain 42161 can spend Maker DAI held on Ethereum.

The output is native ETH on Arbitrum One, written as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Arbiscan shows that as the gas balance of chain id 42161, not Nova. The input is Maker DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Etherscan. You still need ETH on chain id 1 to pay for the send. A local sale of DAI for ETH would leave the ETH on Ethereum, and that balance cannot pay Arbitrum One fees. Mainnet blocks are about 12 seconds. Switch to Arbitrum One and read the native line on Arbiscan.
description: Swap DAI from Ethereum to ETH on Arbitrum One when you need ETH for gas on Arbitrum One and you will spend Maker DAI held on Ethereum before you approve.

sections.heading: L2 gas is the reason to open it
sections.body: Maker DAI on Ethereum cannot pay an Arbitrum One fee. If the next signature is on chain id 42161, the wallet needs ETH there. This pair converts DAI you already hold into that gas coin. It is the wrong shape if you wanted USDC, USDT, or ARB to arrive instead.

sections.heading: The placeholder is the gas line
sections.body: Leave 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE out of the import list. On this route it means ETH on Arbitrum One. On Ethereum the same string means ETH on chain id 1. They are not one balance. Read the native line on Arbiscan after you switch networks.

sections.heading: Approve DAI, pay mainnet ETH
sections.body: The contract that decreases is 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. Confirm it on Etherscan. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is where that fee is charged. The ETH you receive on Arbitrum One cannot pay the transaction that creates it.

sections.heading: Skip the bridge when the pool is local
sections.body: If you want ETH, USDC, or USDT on Ethereum, swap DAI on mainnet. This route is the wrong tool for those balances. If you already hold an Arbitrum One stable and only need gas, swap that stable for ETH on chain 42161. Bridge when the DAI is still on mainnet.

faqs.question: Does the ETH show up as an ERC-20?
faqs.answer: It shows up as the native gas balance on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161. The address 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is a stand-in, not a contract you import from Arbiscan. Switch the wallet to Arbitrum One, not Nova, and read the gas line.

faqs.question: Can I start with only DAI?
faqs.answer: You need Maker DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F and you also need ETH on Ethereum. Chain id 1 charges ETH for the approval and the send. DAI is the asset. ETH on mainnet is the fee. ETH on Arbitrum One is what you receive later and cannot pay the first transaction.

faqs.question: Is this how I turn DAI into mainnet ETH?
faqs.answer: No. Selling DAI for native ETH on Ethereum keeps the ETH on chain id 1. This route sells DAI for native ETH on Arbitrum One. Use it when chain 42161 gas is the gap. Skip it when the next trade is still on Ethereum.

intro:
Swap DAI from Ethereum to WETH on Arbitrum One. A trader moving Maker DAI into wrapped ETH on chain 42161 receives Arbitrum WETH.

DAI is not a wrapper around ETH. You spend 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Etherscan. You receive 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on Arbiscan. That WETH is not 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, and withdrawing from the mainnet contract is not this route. The chain is Arbitrum One, not Nova. Chain id 1 gas is ETH. Chain id 42161 gas is a separate ETH balance, and the received WETH cannot pay it. Switch to chain id 42161 before you search. The mainnet WETH row on Etherscan does not move when this pair completes, so the network badge matters.  Confirm the WETH contract on Arbiscan before you deposit.
description: Swap DAI from Ethereum to WETH on Arbitrum One when you want Arbitrum WETH on chain 42161 and you will spend Maker DAI held on Ethereum before you approve.

sections.heading: Arbitrum WETH is an ERC-20 on Arbiscan
sections.body: Search 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 before you treat the balance as spendable ETH. It will not pay fees on chain id 42161. It will not show as native ETH on Ethereum. The wallet has to be on Arbitrum One.

sections.heading: Buying WETH with DAI on mainnet stays home
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool if you want 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 or native ETH on chain id 1. Those markets are on Ethereum. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the split. Bridge when the WETH address you were given is the Arbiscan one.

sections.heading: The DAI approval
sections.body: Only 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. Maker DAI and Arbitrum WETH both use 18 decimals, so the unit count can look familiar while the asset changes from a dollar to wrapped ETH. You still need ETH on Ethereum so the approval can be mined. Blocks there are about 12 seconds.

sections.heading: L2 ETH has to be waiting
sections.body: Plan ETH on the receiving address on chain id 42161. Arbitrum WETH cannot sponsor its own first transfer. Until that gas is present, the token can be visible on Arbiscan and still be stuck. Nova is the wrong network to search.

faqs.question: Is this an unwrap of DAI into ETH?
faqs.answer: DAI is not wrapped ETH, so there is nothing to unwrap. Selling DAI for WETH on Ethereum credits 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. This route credits 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on Arbitrum One. Use it when that Arbiscan contract is the position. Skip it when ETH exposure should stay on mainnet.

faqs.question: Which explorers do I check?
faqs.answer: Etherscan for the DAI spend at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. Arbiscan for the WETH credit at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Native ETH would use the 0xEeee placeholder and is not the output. Chain id 42161 is Arbitrum One, not Nova. Confirm both strings before you sign.

faqs.question: What blocks the WETH after it arrives?
faqs.answer: No ETH on Arbitrum One. Chain id 42161 charges ETH for every transfer, and this WETH is an ERC-20. Add gas on that chain before the next signature. You also needed ETH on chain id 1 to spend the DAI. The route delivers neither gas balance.

intro:
Swap DAI from Ethereum to ARB on Arbitrum One. A wallet that wants the ARB token on chain 42161 can spend Maker DAI from Ethereum to get it.

You approve DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Etherscan. You receive ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 on Arbiscan. ARB does not pay gas. ETH does, and the ETH on Arbitrum One is not the ETH on Ethereum. The destination is chain id 42161, not Nova. DAI is Maker's collateral dollar, 18 decimals, and it cannot pay the mainnet fee. Blocks on Ethereum are about 12 seconds. Switch to Arbitrum One and read the ARB contract on Arbiscan before you deposit it.  Confirm it on Arbiscan.
description: Swap DAI from Ethereum to ARB on Arbitrum One when you want the ARB token on Arbitrum One and the source balance is Maker DAI on Ethereum before you approve.

sections.heading: Governance token, not gas
sections.body: 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 is what Arbitrum One apps mean by ARB. It will not move itself. Hold ETH on chain id 42161 or the token waits on Arbiscan. If you needed gas, this output is the wrong asset. If you needed a dollar, it is also the wrong asset.

sections.heading: DAI stays on Etherscan until you sign
sections.body: The spend is 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. A mainnet swap of DAI into ETH, USDC, or USDT never creates the Arbiscan ARB balance. This route is the wrong tool for those mainnet balances. Use it when the token you were asked for is the ARB contract on Arbitrum One.

sections.heading: Two ETH fees around one approval
sections.body: Chain id 1 takes ETH to move the DAI. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) covers that signature. Chain id 42161 takes ETH again to move the ARB. Neither fee is paid in DAI or in ARB. Nova is not a shortcut between them.

sections.heading: Read ARB on Arbiscan before you deposit
sections.body: Import 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 from Arbiscan while the wallet is on Arbitrum One. A ticker match is not an address match. The quote you sign is the amount you accept. This page does not publish a price for ARB.

faqs.question: Can ARB pay the next Arbitrum transaction?
faqs.answer: No. ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 is an ERC-20. Gas on chain id 42161 is ETH. Add ETH on Arbitrum One before you try to transfer or vote. ETH on Ethereum paid the DAI send and does not remain as spendable gas on Arbitrum One.

faqs.question: What do I approve?
faqs.answer: Maker DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Etherscan. Keep ETH in that wallet for chain id 1. Blocks are about 12 seconds. You do not approve ARB before it arrives. Afterward, switch to Arbitrum One, not Nova, and read the contract on Arbiscan.

faqs.question: When should I sell DAI on Ethereum instead?
faqs.answer: When you want ETH, USDC, or USDT to stay on chain id 1. Those pools already exist. This bridge is the wrong tool for them. Open it when the position you want is ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 on Arbitrum One and the DAI is still on mainnet.

intro:
Swap ETH from Ethereum to USDC on Arbitrum One. You spend native ETH on Ethereum and an Arbitrum One wallet receives Circle's native USDC.

Native ETH is marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, the gas coin Etherscan shows on chain id 1. You do not approve it. The dollar that arrives is 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on Arbiscan, 6 decimals. Bridged USDC.e at 0xFF970A61A04b1cA14834A43f5dE4533eBDDB5CC8 is not the receipt. Leave ETH behind for the mainnet fee, because the coin you sell and the fee are the same balance. Blocks on Ethereum are about 12 seconds. The destination is Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, not Nova, and the USDC there still needs a separate ETH balance to move. Import the native USDC from Arbiscan once the wallet is on chain id 42161.
description: Swap ETH from Ethereum to USDC on Arbitrum One when you want Circle native USDC on Arbitrum One and you will spend native ETH from Ethereum mainnet today.

sections.heading: Leave ETH for the chain id 1 fee
sections.body: A max send can fail because nothing remains for gas. Lower the amount until the wallet still shows ETH on Ethereum. The USDC lands on Arbitrum One and cannot refund that mainnet cost. Canonical bridging of ETH to Arbitrum One would have left you in ETH, not in this dollar.

sections.heading: Native USDC, not the bridged dollar
sections.body: Watch 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on Arbiscan. USDC.e at 0xFF970A61A04b1cA14834A43f5dE4533eBDDB5CC8 does not move. Circle USDC on Ethereum, 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, is also not the credit. [Arbitrum One](/chains/arbitrum) is where the native dollar is spent.

sections.heading: A mainnet ETH sale stays home
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when you want Circle USDC on Ethereum. That pool already exists on chain id 1. Use the bridge when an Arbitrum One app whitelisted the native contract. Selling ETH for dollars on mainnet never creates the Arbiscan balance.

sections.heading: ETH on Arbitrum One after the dollars land
sections.body: Native USDC does not pay gas on chain id 42161. If the destination wallet has never held ETH there, the new dollars can show on Arbiscan and still be unable to move. Nova will not display them either.

faqs.question: Do I approve a contract for the ETH?
faqs.answer: No. Native ETH uses 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE as a placeholder, not a token you import. You sign a send on chain id 1. Keep enough ETH unspent to cover gas, because the amount and the fee come from the same balance. Etherscan shows that native balance falling.

faqs.question: Which USDC row should increase?
faqs.answer: The native one, 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on Arbiscan, 6 decimals, on Arbitrum One. USDC.e at 0xFF970A61A04b1cA14834A43f5dE4533eBDDB5CC8 stays put. If the app lists the bridged address, this route delivers the wrong contract. Chain id 42161 is the network to select, not Nova. Match the allowlist before you deposit.

faqs.question: When is an Ethereum swap enough?
faqs.answer: When the dollars should remain on chain id 1 as Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. This bridge is the wrong tool for that balance. Open it only if the next use of the money is on Arbitrum One and the accepted contract is the native USDC.

intro:
Swap ETH from Ethereum to USDT on Arbitrum One. A chain 42161 wallet that needs Tether spends native ETH from Ethereum and receives Arbitrum USDT.

You send native ETH, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, the gas coin on Etherscan for chain id 1. You receive 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 on Arbiscan, 6 decimals. Ethereum Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is not the output. Leave ETH for the mainnet fee. Blocks on Ethereum are about 12 seconds. The destination is Arbitrum One, not Nova. The USDT cannot pay gas there, so the receiving wallet needs its own ETH. Switch to chain id 42161 before looking for the Tether. Etherscan will not show a new USDT balance from this pair, even when the ticker matches.  Confirm the USDT contract on Arbiscan before you pay.
description: Swap ETH from Ethereum to USDT on Arbitrum One when an Arbitrum One wallet needs Tether and you will spend native ETH from Ethereum mainnet before you approve.

sections.heading: Ethereum already pairs ETH with Tether
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool if the Tether you want is the mainnet contract. Sell ETH for 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on chain id 1 and stop. Bridge only when the payee wants 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9. A same-chain swap cannot mint that Arbiscan token.

sections.heading: No approval on the ETH you sell
sections.body: Native ETH is the 0xEeee placeholder. The amount you sell and the ETH you keep for gas come from one balance. Import the Arbitrum USDT from Arbiscan so the wallet reads 6 decimals. Chain id 42161 is where that token lives.

sections.heading: L2 ETH is still required
sections.body: Chain id 42161 takes ETH, and that balance is not the ETH you just sold on Ethereum. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the general picture. Hold ETH on Arbitrum One before the next signature. The output is an ERC-20.

sections.heading: Who wants this Tether
sections.body: Use the pair to fund an Arbitrum One book quoted in USDT, or to pay a chain 42161 address that named this contract. The quote has to leave a mainnet fee behind. This page does not set that quote.

faqs.question: Does my Ethereum USDT balance change?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum Tether remains 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan. This route delivers 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 on Arbiscan. Switch to Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, not Nova. The ticker can read USDT on both networks while the contracts stay different. The contracts stay different even when the ticker matches.

faqs.question: Why can a full ETH balance fail?
faqs.answer: The ETH you sell and the ETH that pays gas on chain id 1 are one coin. Setting the amount to the entire native balance leaves nothing for the fee. Lower it until ETH remains. Native ETH uses 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE and does not need a token approval. Blocks are about 12 seconds.

faqs.question: Will Arbitrum USDT pay the next fee?
faqs.answer: No. It is an ERC-20. Gas on chain id 42161 is ETH, separate from Ethereum ETH. If the receiving wallet has no ETH on Arbitrum One, add some before you move the Tether. The route ends when the USDT arrives on Arbiscan.

intro:
Swap ETH from Ethereum to WETH on Arbitrum One. Someone who needs wrapped ETH on chain 42161 spends native ETH on Ethereum and receives Arbitrum WETH.

Wrapping on Ethereum is a deposit into 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, and that WETH stays on mainnet. This route spends native ETH, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and delivers 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on Arbiscan. Those are different contracts. Leave ETH for gas on chain id 1. The received token cannot pay ETH gas on Arbitrum One. The chain is 42161, not Nova. Blocks on Ethereum are about 12 seconds. Depositing into the mainnet WETH contract is a separate action and stays on chain id 1. This receipt is visible only on Arbiscan after you switch to Arbitrum One.  Confirm it on Arbiscan.
description: Swap ETH from Ethereum to WETH on Arbitrum One when you want Arbitrum WETH on chain 42161 and you will spend native ETH from Ethereum mainnet right now.

sections.heading: A local wrap does not reach Arbitrum One
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool if you want WETH on Ethereum. Deposit ETH into 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 and stop. That contract never becomes 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. Open this page when an Arbitrum One pool asks for the Arbiscan WETH. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is only the chain you sign on.

sections.heading: Native in, ERC-20 out
sections.body: You do not approve the ETH. The placeholder means the gas coin on chain id 1. You do import, on chain 42161, the WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1. If the native ETH line on Ethereum is what you wanted to keep, this pair spends it.

sections.heading: Keep a fee on both chains
sections.body: Chain id 1 charges ETH from the same balance you are selling. Chain id 42161 charges a different ETH balance. Arbitrum WETH pays neither. Budget ETH on Arbitrum One before you use the wrapped token. Nova will not show the credit.

sections.heading: Pools that name WETH on Arbitrum One
sections.body: They mean 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1, 18 decimals. Landing that contract from native ETH lets you join those books. You do not receive mainnet WETH, the ARB token, or a stablecoin. The amount is the quote you sign.

faqs.question: How is this different from wrapping ETH?
faqs.answer: Wrapping deposits native ETH into 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 and stays on Ethereum. This route delivers Arbitrum WETH at 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1 on Arbiscan. The ticker matches. The chain and the contract do not. Use the wrap when the next signature is on chain id 1.

faqs.question: Do I approve ETH before sending?
faqs.answer: No. It is recorded as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. You still must leave enough ETH to pay chain id 1 gas, or the send fails. Etherscan shows the native balance falling. Arbiscan shows the WETH rising after you switch to Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, not Nova.

faqs.question: Can this WETH pay gas?
faqs.answer: No. Gas on chain id 42161 is ETH. The WETH can arrive and sit until ETH is added on Arbitrum One. If you needed the gas coin itself, choose a route whose output is native ETH, the 0xEeee placeholder, on that chain.

intro:
Swap ETH from Ethereum to ARB on Arbitrum One. Someone who wants the ARB token on chain 42161 spends native ETH on Ethereum and receives that governance token.

You send native ETH, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE on chain id 1. You receive ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 on Arbiscan. ARB does not pay gas. You must leave ETH on Ethereum for the send, and you still need ETH on Arbitrum One afterward, because the token you receive is not the fee token. The chain is 42161, not Nova. Blocks on Ethereum are about 12 seconds. A local wrap of ETH into WETH would not create this ARB balance. Switch to chain id 42161 and import ARB from Arbiscan.
description: Swap ETH from Ethereum to ARB on Arbitrum One when you want the ARB token on chain 42161 and you will spend native ETH from Ethereum mainnet in your wallet.

sections.heading: You spend gas to buy a non-gas token
sections.body: Native ETH on Ethereum funds both the trade and the chain id 1 fee, so a max send can fail. The ARB that arrives cannot pay chain id 42161 either. Hold ETH on Arbitrum One before you try to move 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548.

sections.heading: Not a wrap, and not a canonical ETH bridge
sections.body: Depositing ETH into 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 stays on Ethereum as WETH. Bridging ETH as ETH would leave native ETH on Arbitrum One. This route is the wrong tool for both. Use it when the position is the ARB token. [Arbitrum One](/chains/arbitrum) is where that token lives.

sections.heading: The placeholder is only the input
sections.body: 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means the ETH you sell on chain id 1. The output is an ERC-20 with its own address on Arbiscan. Do not look for ARB in the native gas line. Switch to Arbitrum One and import the contract.

sections.heading: Leave L2 ETH beside the ARB
sections.body: Once ARB is visible on Arbiscan, the next vote or transfer still costs ETH on chain id 42161. Spending every bit of that gas balance strands the token. Nova will not show this ARB. The quote you sign is the amount you accept.

faqs.question: Does the ARB replace my need for ETH on Arbitrum One?
faqs.answer: No. ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 cannot pay gas. Chain id 42161 charges ETH. The ETH you sold was on Ethereum, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and the fee there came from the same balance. Add ETH on Arbitrum One before you move the token.

faqs.question: How much ETH should I keep on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: Enough to pay the chain id 1 fee after the amount you sell. A send of the entire native balance fails. Blocks are about 12 seconds. You do not approve an ERC-20 for the ETH. Etherscan shows the native balance. Arbiscan shows the ARB after you switch to chain id 42161.

faqs.question: Is this how I move ETH to Arbitrum One?
faqs.answer: Only if you want the value to arrive as ARB. Native ETH on Arbitrum One is a different output. Wrapping on Ethereum is a third action and stays on chain id 1. This pair is the wrong tool unless 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 is the token you mean to hold.

intro:
Swap WETH from Ethereum to USDC on Arbitrum One. Holders of wrapped ETH who need Circle's native USDC on chain 42161 spend WETH and receive that dollar.

You approve WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Etherscan. Withdrawing from that contract unwraps to native ETH and stays on Ethereum. This route spends the WETH and delivers 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on Arbiscan, Circle's native USDC, 6 decimals. Bridged USDC.e at 0xFF970A61A04b1cA14834A43f5dE4533eBDDB5CC8 is not the receipt. Gas to start is still ETH on chain id 1. The destination is Arbitrum One, not Nova, and the USDC there needs a separate ETH balance to move. Blocks on Ethereum are about 12 seconds. Import the native USDC from Arbiscan after you switch to chain id 42161. USDC.e will not reflect this route, and Etherscan will not show the new dollars.
description: Swap WETH from Ethereum to USDC on Arbitrum One when you want Circle native USDC on Arbitrum One and the source is wrapped ETH on Ethereum before you approve.

sections.heading: Unwrapping WETH stays on Ethereum
sections.body: If you want native ETH on Ethereum, withdraw from 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 and stop. If you want Circle USDC on Ethereum, swap WETH there. This page is for a wallet that must hold Arbitrum native USDC. A mainnet trade never creates 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831.

sections.heading: Arbitrum native USDC, not USDC.e
sections.body: The credit to expect is 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on Arbiscan. The bridged dollar is 0xFF970A61A04b1cA14834A43f5dE4533eBDDB5CC8. WETH in is 18 decimals. This USDC is 6. Deposit only where the allowlist matches the native contract on chain id 42161.

sections.heading: ETH on mainnet, then ETH on Arbitrum One
sections.body: WETH cannot pay the Ethereum fee. Hold native ETH for the approval. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) walks through that signature. On Arbitrum One the fee is ETH again, a different balance, and native USDC does not cover it.

sections.heading: Spending the 6 decimal USDC on Arbitrum One
sections.body: Switch to Arbitrum One and read Arbiscan before you deposit. Apps that want USDT at 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 will ignore this USDC. Apps that want Ethereum USDC are on the wrong network. Nova will not show the dollars.

faqs.question: Can I unwrap WETH and then bridge the ETH?
faqs.answer: You can, and that is a different route. Withdrawing 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 returns native ETH on chain id 1. This page spends the WETH contract and pays Arbitrum native USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831. Choose the output the destination wallet is supposed to hold.

faqs.question: What do I approve on Etherscan?
faqs.answer: Approve 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Do not approve Circle's Ethereum USDC for this pair. You still need native ETH for gas on chain id 1. Blocks are about 12 seconds. WETH is the asset being sold. ETH is only the fee. ETH on chain id 1 is only the fee.

faqs.question: Which USDC will the wallet show?
faqs.answer: Circle's native USDC at 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831, 6 decimals, on Arbiscan. USDC.e will not move. Set the wallet to Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, not Nova. If the balance looks enormous or tiny, re-import the contract and read its decimals. Then switch the wallet to chain id 42161.

intro:
Swap WETH from Ethereum to USDT on Arbitrum One. A chain 42161 wallet that needs Tether spends wrapped ETH from Ethereum and receives Arbitrum USDT.

Approve WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Etherscan. That contract is not native ETH. The Tether you receive is 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 on Arbiscan, 6 decimals. Ethereum USDT at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is a different contract. Gas to start is ETH on chain id 1, about 12 seconds a block. Gas after arrival is ETH on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, not Nova. The USDT cannot pay that second fee. Switch to chain id 42161 and match the Arbiscan USDT before you tell a payee the transfer finished. An Ethereum address will not display this balance.  Confirm the USDT on Arbiscan before you tell the payee.
description: Swap WETH from Ethereum to USDT on Arbitrum One when an Arbitrum wallet needs Tether and the source token is wrapped ETH on Ethereum mainnet right now.

sections.heading: WETH on Etherscan, USDT on Arbiscan
sections.body: The spend is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. The receipt is 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9. Etherscan and Arbiscan are the two checks. They are not two views of one token. Switch to Arbitrum One before you tell a payee the transfer finished.

sections.heading: Sell WETH for USDT on mainnet if you are staying
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool if you want Ethereum Tether or native ETH. Mainnet pools already pair WETH with USDT, and unwrapping WETH is a local withdraw. Use the bridge when the Tether contract you were given is the Arbitrum one.

sections.heading: ETH on Arbitrum One comes second
sections.body: The fee on chain id 1 is ETH even though the token moving is WETH. The fee on chain id 42161 is ETH again, from a different balance. [Arbitrum One](/chains/arbitrum) will not treat USDT as gas. Keep ETH on the destination or the Tether waits.

sections.heading: Payments that name this USDT
sections.body: Send the output only to an Arbitrum One address that expects 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9. An Ethereum address will not show the tokens on Etherscan. Tell the payee the network as well as the amount on the quote.

faqs.question: Is spending WETH the same as spending ETH?
faqs.answer: No. WETH is the ERC-20 at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Native ETH is the gas coin, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE when a route needs it. This pair approves WETH. You still need a separate ETH balance for the chain id 1 fee. Unwrapping first stays on Ethereum.

faqs.question: Which USDT arrives?
faqs.answer: 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 on Arbiscan, 6 decimals, on Arbitrum One. Ethereum Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is not credited. If your payee uses the Ethereum contract, this route is the wrong tool. Chain id 42161 is the network, not Nova. Match the invoice address before you send.

faqs.question: What stops the USDT from moving later?
faqs.answer: An empty ETH balance on Arbitrum One. Chain id 42161 charges ETH for every token transfer. The USDT cannot sponsor itself. Put ETH on the receiving wallet before a second transaction. The ETH on Ethereum was only enough to start the route.

intro:
Swap WETH from Ethereum to ETH on Arbitrum One. Wrapped ETH on Ethereum is the input, and native ETH on chain 42161 is what arrives.

This is not an unwrap. Unwrapping spends 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 and returns native ETH on Ethereum, which Etherscan shows as a gas balance. This route spends that same WETH contract and delivers native ETH on Arbitrum One, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which Arbiscan shows as the gas coin of chain id 42161. You still need ETH on chain id 1 to start. The ETH you receive can pay later fees on Arbitrum One. It cannot pay the mainnet transaction. The chain is not Nova. Blocks on Ethereum are about 12 seconds.
description: Swap WETH from Ethereum to ETH on Arbitrum One when you need ETH for gas on Arbitrum One and the source is wrapped ETH on Ethereum mainnet before you approve.

sections.heading: Unwrap locally if you want mainnet ETH
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool for getting native ETH back on Ethereum. The WETH contract already has a withdraw function, and the ETH it returns stays on chain id 1. Open this page when an Arbitrum One wallet needs its own ETH for gas. Those are different receipts, on different explorers.

sections.heading: WETH in, native ETH out
sections.body: You approve 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Etherscan. You watch the native line on Arbiscan, not an ERC-20. The placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means ETH on chain id 42161 here. On Ethereum that same string would have meant the gas coin you are not receiving.

sections.heading: Gas to leave Ethereum
sections.body: Chain id 1 charges ETH and blocks about every 12 seconds. WETH cannot pay that. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is where the approval is signed. After arrival, the received ETH is the fee token on Arbitrum One. Leave a remainder if you still need to move other tokens.

sections.heading: Not Arbitrum WETH, and not Nova
sections.body: If a pool asks for 0x82aF49447D8a07e3bd95BD0d56f35241523fBab1, this route delivered the gas coin instead. Switch outputs. A wallet on Nova will not show the ETH this pair sends to chain id 42161.

faqs.question: If I want ETH, why not just unwrap?
faqs.answer: Unwrap when the ETH should be mainnet gas. Withdrawing from 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 stays on Ethereum. This route delivers native ETH on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. The ticker matches and the chain does not. Pick unwrap for chain id 1.

faqs.question: Will the received ETH pay Arbitrum fees?
faqs.answer: Yes. Native ETH is the gas token on chain id 42161. That is the reason to pick this output instead of WETH or ARB. It will not pay the Ethereum fee that spent the WETH. Keep a little of the received ETH unspent for the next signature. Look on Arbiscan, not on Nova.

faqs.question: What should I approve?
faqs.answer: Only the WETH contract at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Etherscan. Keep native ETH for the mainnet gas. There is no destination token to import, because the output is the native balance. Switch the wallet to Arbitrum One to see it. There is no ERC-20 import for that gas balance.

intro:
Swap WETH from Ethereum to ARB on Arbitrum One. Wallets that want the ARB token on chain 42161 spend wrapped ETH on Ethereum and receive that governance token.

You approve WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Etherscan. You receive ARB at 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 on Arbiscan. ARB does not pay gas on Arbitrum One. Unwrapping WETH would have given you native ETH on Ethereum instead, and that ETH does not pay chain id 42161 fees and is not the ARB token. Mainnet blocks are about 12 seconds. The destination is Arbitrum One, not Nova. You need ETH on chain id 1 to start and ETH on chain id 42161 after the ARB arrives. Read the ARB token on Arbiscan after you switch.
description: Swap WETH from Ethereum to ARB on Arbitrum One when you want the ARB token on Arbitrum One and the source token is wrapped ETH on Ethereum before you approve.

sections.heading: The output is not gas and not WETH
sections.body: 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 is an ERC-20. Once the wallet is on chain id 42161, import it from Arbiscan. The native ETH line will not increase because of this pair. If you needed gas, choose the route that outputs the 0xEeee placeholder on Arbitrum One.

sections.heading: Approve wrapped ETH, pay native ETH
sections.body: The contract that decreases is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. The fee on chain id 1 is ETH. A wallet with WETH and no ETH cannot start. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is why the source chain collects a fee in its own coin first.

sections.heading: Unwrap does not produce ARB
sections.body: Withdrawing WETH returns ETH on Ethereum. Swapping WETH for USDC or USDT on Ethereum keeps you on chain id 1. This route is the wrong tool for both. Use it when the missing token is ARB on Arbitrum One. If you already hold an Arbitrum asset, buy ARB there.

sections.heading: ETH on Arbitrum One still matters
sections.body: The ARB you receive cannot pay the next transaction. Keep ETH on chain id 42161. Nova will not list this token. Read the full address on Arbiscan before you deposit it into a governance or pool contract.

faqs.question: Does this unwrap WETH into ETH first?
faqs.answer: The result you hold is ARB on chain id 42161, not native ETH on Ethereum. WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 is what you approve on Etherscan. A local unwrap credits ETH on chain id 1 and stops. If ETH on Ethereum is the goal, do not open this pair.

faqs.question: How do I confirm the ARB arrived?
faqs.answer: Set the wallet to Arbitrum One, chain id 42161, and open 0x912CE59144191C1204E64559FE8253a0e49E6548 on Arbiscan. Nova will not show it. The native gas line is ETH, not ARB. If the wallet is still on Ethereum, you will keep seeing WETH and miss the token.

faqs.question: What if I hold WETH and no ETH?
faqs.answer: Unwrap a small slice of WETH to native ETH on Ethereum so the approval can pay gas. Then spend the remaining WETH on this route. Chain id 1 will not accept WETH as a fee. The ARB you receive later cannot pay that first transaction, and it cannot pay chain 42161 fees either.

intro:
Swap WBTC from Ethereum to USDC on Arbitrum One. Holders of wrapped bitcoin who need Circle's native USDC on chain 42161 spend WBTC and receive that dollar.

WBTC is an ERC-20, not bitcoin on the Bitcoin chain. You approve 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 on Etherscan. It uses 8 decimals. A Bitcoin address cannot receive it. The dollars you receive are 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on Arbiscan, Circle's native USDC, 6 decimals. USDC.e at 0xFF970A61A04b1cA14834A43f5dE4533eBDDB5CC8 is not the output. Gas to leave is ETH on chain id 1, about 12 seconds a block. The destination is Arbitrum One, not Nova, and the USDC needs ETH there to move. Import the native USDC from Arbiscan once the wallet is on chain id 42161. The USDC.e row stays unchanged.
description: Swap WBTC from Ethereum to USDC on Arbitrum One when you want Circle native USDC on Arbitrum One and the source is wrapped bitcoin on Ethereum right now.

sections.heading: Not a Bitcoin withdrawal
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool if the destination is a Bitcoin address. WBTC stays an Ethereum token until the route spends it, and the output is a dollar on Arbitrum One. Redeeming WBTC for bitcoin, where a custodian allows it, does not use Arbiscan and does not pay 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831.

sections.heading: Eight decimals in, six out, and not USDC.e
sections.body: Check 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 on Etherscan for the WBTC you spend. Check 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831 on Arbiscan for the native USDC. The bridged USDC.e contract will not move. A mixed-up decimal field will invent the size of the balance.

sections.heading: ETH on both chains, for different reasons
sections.body: WBTC does not pay Ethereum gas. Keep ETH on chain id 1. Native USDC does not pay Arbitrum One gas. Keep ETH on chain id 42161. [Arbitrum One](/chains/arbitrum) is the network the dollars land on. Nova is a different chain id.

sections.heading: A mainnet WBTC sale is enough for mainnet dollars
sections.body: WBTC already trades against Circle USDC on Ethereum. Use that pool when the dollars should stay on chain id 1 as 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. This bridge is for a wallet that needs the Arbitrum native contract. Selling on mainnet never creates it.

faqs.question: Can the receiver be a Bitcoin address?
faqs.answer: No. The output is Circle's native USDC on Arbitrum One, 0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831. The input is WBTC at 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 on Etherscan, an ERC-20 with 8 decimals. Neither side is the Bitcoin network. Use an EVM address that can switch to chain id 42161.

faqs.question: Why does a small WBTC figure represent a large value?
faqs.answer: WBTC uses 8 decimals, so a fraction of one token is a meaningful amount of wrapped bitcoin. The USDC you receive is set by the quote you sign, which this page does not fix. Read the minimum on that quote. The native USDC then displays with 6 decimals on Arbiscan.

faqs.question: What do I hold besides WBTC?
faqs.answer: ETH on Ethereum, because chain id 1 will not take WBTC as a fee. ETH on Arbitrum One after arrival, because native USDC will not pay chain id 42161. Blocks are about 12 seconds on the way out. Both ETH balances sit apart from the two token contracts. Nova will not show the USDC.

intro:
Swap WBTC from Ethereum to USDT on Arbitrum One. A chain 42161 payment in Tether can start from wrapped bitcoin held as an ERC-20 on Ethereum.

Approve WBTC at 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 on Etherscan, 8 decimals. It is not a Bitcoin-network coin. Receive 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 on Arbiscan, Tether on Arbitrum One, 6 decimals. Ethereum USDT at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is not the balance that increases. You pay ETH gas on chain id 1, where a block takes about 12 seconds. The recipient must be on Arbitrum One, not Nova, and needs ETH there because the USDT cannot pay gas. The recipient has to be on chain id 42161, watching Arbiscan, or the Tether payment is invisible. An Etherscan watch will not update.
description: Swap WBTC from Ethereum to USDT on Arbitrum One when an Arbitrum One wallet needs Tether and the source is wrapped bitcoin on Ethereum mainnet right now.

sections.heading: Two contracts name the pair
sections.body: Spend 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 on Etherscan. Receive 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9 on Arbiscan. If either explorer shows a different contract under a similar name, stop. Copies reuse the first and last characters of a popular address.

sections.heading: An Ethereum invoice wants different Tether
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when the invoice prints 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. Sell WBTC for that Tether on mainnet. Bridge when the invoice says Arbitrum One and prints the Arbiscan address. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) is the signing order.

sections.heading: The Bitcoin chain is the wrong destination
sections.body: Sending WBTC to a Bitcoin address will not redeem it, and this route will not either. You finish holding Tether on chain id 42161. If the goal is bitcoin in a Bitcoin wallet, use the redemption path your custodian documents. Arbiscan will not show a bitcoin UTXO.

sections.heading: Fees around an 8 decimal token
sections.body: Keep ETH for the Ethereum approval. Keep ETH on Arbitrum One for the transfer that follows, because the USDT cannot pay it. Size the trade from the quote, and remember that 8 decimal units are easy to mistype. This page does not set the quote.

faqs.question: Is WBTC bitcoin for this payment?
faqs.answer: No. WBTC at 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 is an ERC-20 on Ethereum, 8 decimals, checked on Etherscan. This route spends it and pays Arbitrum USDT. A Bitcoin wallet cannot hold either token. Treat the position as an Ethereum asset until you redeem it through a separate process.

faqs.question: Which Tether should the recipient watch?
faqs.answer: Arbiscan for 0xFd086bC7CD5C481DCC9C85ebE478A1C0b69FCbb9, on Arbitrum One, chain id 42161. Watching Etherscan for 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 will show no change. Ask them to switch networks, and not to Nova. The token uses 6 decimals and is still a different contract from Ethereum USDT.

faqs.question: What if I am still trading on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: Stay there. WBTC and Tether already have a mainnet market, and the output is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. This bridge is the wrong tool for that market. Use it when the Tether has to be the Arbitrum contract because the next wallet or pool is on chain 42161.

intro:
Swap WBTC from Ethereum to ETH on Arbitrum One. A chain 42161 wallet that needs gas can spend wrapped bitcoin on Ethereum and receive native ETH there.

WBTC at 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 is an 8 decimal ERC-20 on Etherscan, not a coin on the Bitcoin chain. Native ETH on Arbitrum One is marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE and shows up as the gas balance on Arbiscan for chain id 42161, not Nova. You approve the WBTC contract and pay that approval in ETH on Ethereum. Blocks there are about 12 seconds. You do not import the destination placeholder. sections.body: 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F is the DAI that decreases. Circle USDC on Ethereum, 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, is what a mainnet DAI to USDC swap would pay. This route does not pay that contract.

sections.heading: Stay in DAI on Ethereum when that is the job
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool if you want Circle USDC on chain id 1 or if you want to remain in DAI. Both are mainnet actions. Bridge when a Base app whitelisted the native USDC. [Base](/chains/base) is where the separate ETH balance then pays for using it.

sections.heading: Two ETH balances around the decimal change
sections.body: ETH pays the Ethereum approval. ETH on chain id 8453 pays any later move of the USDC. The USDC cannot sponsor that second fee. Hold Base ETH before you deposit the new dollars.

faqs.question: Does this give me Circle USDC on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. It spends Maker DAI and pays Circle's native USDC on Base, 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 on Basescan. Ethereum Circle USDC remains 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan. If that mainnet contract is what you wanted, trade DAI for it on chain id 1 and skip the bridge.

faqs.question: Why can the USDC display look nothing like the DAI amount?
faqs.answer: DAI uses 18 decimals and Base native USDC uses 6. A wrong decimal field shifts the display by many zeros. Check decimals on Basescan for 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913. Judge the trade by the quote you sign. This page does not set that quote.

faqs.question: What if the app listed USDbC?
faqs.answer: Do not deposit this output there. USDbC is 0xd9aAEc86B65D86f6A7B5B1b0c42FFA531710b6CA. This route pays the native contract on Base, chain id 8453. Sending native USDC into a pool that wants the bridged token will not credit you. Match the allowlist, not the USDC ticker.

intro:
Swap DAI from Ethereum to ETH on Base. A wallet that needs ETH for gas on chain 8453 can spend Maker DAI held on Ethereum.

The output is native ETH on Base, written as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Basescan shows that as the gas balance of chain id 8453. The input is Maker DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Etherscan. You still need ETH on chain id 1 to pay for the send. A local sale of DAI for ETH would leave the ETH on Ethereum, and that balance cannot pay Base fees. Mainnet blocks are about 12 seconds. Switch to Base and read the native line on Basescan. Base WETH at the 0x4200 predeploy is a different asset and is not this output.
description: Swap DAI from Ethereum to ETH on Base when a chain 8453 wallet needs ETH for gas and the source balance is Maker DAI on Ethereum mainnet in your wallet.

sections.heading: Base gas is the reason to open it
sections.body: Maker DAI on Ethereum cannot pay a Base fee. If the next signature is on chain id 8453, the wallet needs ETH there. This pair converts DAI you already hold into that gas coin. It is the wrong shape if you wanted USDC or WETH to arrive instead.

sections.heading: The placeholder is the gas line
sections.body: Leave 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE out of the import list. On this route it means ETH on Base. On Ethereum the same string means ETH on chain id 1. They are not one balance. Read the native line on Basescan after you switch networks.

sections.heading: Approve DAI, pay mainnet ETH
sections.body: The contract that decreases is 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. Confirm it on Etherscan. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is where that fee is charged. The ETH you receive on Base cannot pay the transaction that creates it.

sections.heading: Skip the bridge when the pool is local
sections.body: If you want ETH, USDC, or USDT on Ethereum, swap DAI on mainnet. This route is the wrong tool for those balances. If you already hold a Base stable and only need gas, swap that stable for ETH on chain 8453. Bridge when the DAI is still on mainnet.

faqs.question: Does the ETH show up as the WETH predeploy?
faqs.answer: No. It shows up as the native gas balance on Base, chain id 8453. The address 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is a stand-in, not a contract you import. Base WETH is 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. Switch the wallet to Base and read the gas line on Basescan.

faqs.question: Can I start with only DAI?
faqs.answer: You need Maker DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F and you also need ETH on Ethereum. Chain id 1 charges ETH for the approval and the send. DAI is the asset. ETH on mainnet is the fee. ETH on Base is what you receive later and cannot pay the first transaction.

faqs.question: Is this how I turn DAI into mainnet ETH?
faqs.answer: No. Selling DAI for native ETH on Ethereum keeps the ETH on chain id 1. This route sells DAI for native ETH on Base. Use it when chain 8453 gas is the gap. Skip it when the next trade is still on Ethereum.

intro:
Swap DAI from Ethereum to WETH on Base. A trader moving Maker DAI into wrapped ETH on chain 8453 receives the Base WETH predeploy.

DAI is not a wrapper around ETH. You spend 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Etherscan. You receive 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on Basescan. That WETH is not 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, and withdrawing from the mainnet contract is not this route. Chain id 1 gas is ETH, about 12 seconds a block. Chain id 8453 gas is a separate ETH balance, and the received WETH cannot pay it. Switch to Base before you search, because the mainnet WETH row does not move. Switch to chain id 8453 and read the predeploy on Basescan. The Ethereum WETH balance does not record this route. Confirm the predeploy on Basescan before you deposit the wrapped ETH into a pool.
description: Swap DAI from Ethereum to WETH on Base when you want the Base WETH predeploy on chain 8453 and you will spend Maker DAI held on Ethereum in your wallet.

sections.heading: Base WETH is the predeploy on Basescan
sections.body: Search 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 before you treat the balance as spendable ETH. It will not pay fees on chain id 8453. It will not show as native ETH on Ethereum. The wallet has to be on Base.

sections.heading: Buying WETH with DAI on mainnet stays home
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool if you want 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 or native ETH on chain id 1. Those markets are on Ethereum. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is the split. Bridge when the WETH address you were given is the Basescan predeploy.

sections.heading: The DAI approval
sections.body: Only 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. Maker DAI and Base WETH both use 18 decimals, so the unit count can look familiar while the asset changes from a dollar to wrapped ETH. You still need ETH on Ethereum so the approval can be mined.

sections.heading: Base ETH has to be waiting
sections.body: Plan ETH on the receiving address on chain id 8453. Base WETH cannot sponsor its own first transfer. Until that gas is present, the token can be visible on Basescan and still be stuck.

faqs.question: Is this an unwrap of DAI into ETH?
faqs.answer: DAI is not wrapped ETH, so there is nothing to unwrap. Selling DAI for WETH on Ethereum credits 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. This route credits 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on Base. Use it when that predeploy is the position. Skip it when ETH exposure should stay on mainnet.

faqs.question: Which explorers do I check?
faqs.answer: Etherscan for the DAI spend at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. Basescan for the WETH credit at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. Native ETH would use the 0xEeee placeholder and is not the output. Chain id 8453 is Base. Confirm the full address on the explorer before you send it onward.

faqs.question: What blocks the WETH after it arrives?
faqs.answer: No ETH on Base. Chain id 8453 charges ETH for every transfer, and this WETH is an ERC-20. Add gas on that chain before the next signature. You also needed ETH on chain id 1 to spend the DAI. The route delivers neither gas balance.

intro:
Swap ETH from Ethereum to USDC on Base. You spend native ETH on Ethereum and a Base wallet receives Circle's native USDC.

Native ETH is marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, the gas coin Etherscan shows on chain id 1. You do not approve it. The dollar that arrives is 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 on Basescan, 6 decimals. Bridged USDbC at 0xd9aAEc86B65D86f6A7B5B1b0c42FFA531710b6CA is not the receipt. Leave ETH behind for the mainnet fee, because the coin you sell and the fee are the same balance. Blocks on Ethereum are about 12 seconds. Base, chain id 8453, still charges ETH, a separate balance, and the USDC cannot pay it. Import the native contract from Basescan after you switch networks. Import the native USDC from Basescan after the wallet is on chain id 8453. USDbC will stay flat.
description: Swap ETH from Ethereum to USDC on Base when you want Circle's native USDC on chain 8453 and you will spend native ETH from Ethereum mainnet today on this route.

sections.heading: Leave ETH for the chain id 1 fee
sections.body: A max send can fail because nothing remains for gas. Lower the amount until the wallet still shows ETH on Ethereum. The USDC lands on Base and cannot refund that mainnet cost. A canonical bridge of ETH to Base would have left you in ETH, not in this dollar.

sections.heading: Native USDC, not USDbC
sections.body: Watch 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 on Basescan. USDbC at 0xd9aAEc86B65D86f6A7B5B1b0c42FFA531710b6CA does not move. Circle USDC on Ethereum, 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, is also not the credit. [Base](/chains/base) is where the native dollar is spent.

sections.heading: A mainnet ETH sale stays home
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when you want Circle USDC on Ethereum. That pool already exists on chain id 1. Use the bridge when a Base app whitelisted the native contract. Selling ETH for dollars on mainnet never creates the Basescan balance.

sections.heading: ETH on Base after the dollars land
sections.body: Native USDC does not pay gas on chain id 8453. If the destination wallet has never held ETH there, the new dollars can show on Basescan and still be unable to move.

faqs.question: Do I approve a contract for the ETH?
faqs.answer: No. Native ETH uses 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE as a placeholder, not a token you import. You sign a send on chain id 1. Keep enough ETH unspent to cover gas, because the amount and the fee come from the same balance. Etherscan shows that native balance falling.

faqs.question: Which USDC row should increase?
faqs.answer: The native one, 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 on Basescan, 6 decimals, on Base. USDbC at 0xd9aAEc86B65D86f6A7B5B1b0c42FFA531710b6CA stays put. If the app lists the bridged address, this route delivers the wrong contract. Chain id 8453 is the network to select. Confirm the full address on the explorer before you send it onward.

faqs.question: When is an Ethereum swap enough?
faqs.answer: When the dollars should remain on chain id 1 as Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. This bridge is the wrong tool for that balance. Open it only if the next use of the money is on Base and the accepted contract is the native USDC.

intro:
Swap ETH from Ethereum to WETH on Base. Someone who needs wrapped ETH on chain 8453 spends native ETH on Ethereum and receives the Base WETH predeploy.

Wrapping on Ethereum is a deposit into 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, and that WETH stays on mainnet. This route spends native ETH, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, and delivers 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on Basescan. Those are different contracts. Leave ETH for gas on chain id 1. The received token cannot pay ETH gas on Base. Blocks on Ethereum are about 12 seconds. Switch to chain id 8453 and read the predeploy on Basescan. A local wrap never creates that balance. A local wrap into mainnet WETH stays on chain id 1. This receipt is only the Basescan predeploy after you switch to Base. Confirm the predeploy on Basescan before you use it.
description: Swap ETH from Ethereum to WETH on Base when you want the Base WETH predeploy on chain 8453 and you will spend native ETH from Ethereum mainnet right now.

sections.heading: A local wrap does not reach Base
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool if you want WETH on Ethereum. Deposit ETH into 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 and stop. That contract never becomes 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. Open this page when a Base pool asks for the Basescan predeploy. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is only the chain you sign on.

sections.heading: Native in, predeploy out
sections.body: You do not approve the ETH. The placeholder means the gas coin on chain id 1. You do import, on chain 8453, the WETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. If the native ETH line on Ethereum is what you wanted to keep, this pair spends it.

sections.heading: Keep a fee on both chains
sections.body: Chain id 1 charges ETH from the same balance you are selling. Chain id 8453 charges a different ETH balance. Base WETH pays neither. Budget ETH on Base before you use the wrapped token.

sections.heading: Pools that name WETH on Base
sections.body: They mean 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006, 18 decimals. Landing that contract from native ETH lets you join those books. You do not receive mainnet WETH or a stablecoin. The amount is the quote you sign.

faqs.question: How is this different from wrapping ETH?
faqs.answer: Wrapping deposits native ETH into 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 and stays on Ethereum. This route delivers Base WETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on Basescan. The ticker matches. The chain and the contract do not. Use the wrap when the next signature is on chain id 1.

faqs.question: Do I approve ETH before sending?
faqs.answer: No. It is recorded as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. You still must leave enough ETH to pay chain id 1 gas, or the send fails. Etherscan shows the native balance falling. Basescan shows the predeploy rising after you switch to Base, chain id 8453.

faqs.question: Can this WETH pay gas on Base?
faqs.answer: No. Gas on chain id 8453 is ETH. The WETH can arrive and sit until ETH is added on Base. If you needed the gas coin itself, choose a route whose output is native ETH, the 0xEeee placeholder, on that chain.

intro:
Swap WETH from Ethereum to USDC on Base. Holders of wrapped ETH who need Circle's native USDC on chain 8453 spend WETH and receive that dollar.

You approve WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Etherscan. Withdrawing from that contract unwraps to native ETH and stays on Ethereum. This route spends the WETH and delivers 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 on Basescan, Circle's native USDC, 6 decimals. Bridged USDbC at 0xd9aAEc86B65D86f6A7B5B1b0c42FFA531710b6CA is not the receipt. Gas to start is still ETH on chain id 1, about 12 seconds a block. Base, chain id 8453, needs its own ETH before the USDC can move. Import the native contract from Basescan. USDbC will not reflect this route. Import native USDC from Basescan on chain id 8453. USDbC will not reflect this route, and Etherscan will not show the new dollars. Confirm the native USDC on Basescan before you deposit.
description: Swap WETH from Ethereum to USDC on Base when you want Circle native USDC on chain 8453 and the source token is wrapped ETH held on Ethereum mainnet today.

sections.heading: Unwrapping is the wrong tool
sections.body: If you want native ETH on Ethereum, withdraw from 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 and stop. If you want Circle USDC on Ethereum, swap WETH there. This page is for a wallet that must hold Base native USDC. A mainnet trade never creates 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913.

sections.heading: Native USDC versus USDbC
sections.body: The credit to expect is 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 on Basescan. The bridged dollar is 0xd9aAEc86B65D86f6A7B5B1b0c42FFA531710b6CA. WETH in is 18 decimals. This USDC is 6. Deposit only where the allowlist matches the native contract on chain id 8453.

sections.heading: ETH gas beside the WETH
sections.body: WETH cannot pay the Ethereum fee. Hold native ETH for the approval. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) walks through that signature. On Base the fee is ETH again, a different balance, and native USDC does not cover it.

sections.heading: After the 6 decimal dollar arrives
sections.body: Switch to Base and read Basescan before you deposit. Apps that want Ethereum USDC are on the wrong network. Apps that want USDbC will ignore this native contract.

faqs.question: Can I unwrap WETH and then bridge the ETH?
faqs.answer: You can, and that is a different route. Withdrawing 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 returns native ETH on chain id 1. This page spends the WETH contract and pays Base native USDC at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913. Choose the output the destination wallet is supposed to hold.

faqs.question: What do I approve on Etherscan?
faqs.answer: Approve 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. Do not approve Circle's Ethereum USDC for this pair. You still need native ETH for gas on chain id 1. Blocks are about 12 seconds. WETH is the asset being sold. ETH is only the fee. Confirm the full address on the explorer before you send it onward.

faqs.question: Which USDC will the wallet show?
faqs.answer: Circle's native USDC at 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913, 6 decimals, on Basescan. USDbC will not move. Set the wallet to Base, chain id 8453. If the balance looks enormous or tiny, re-import the contract and read its decimals before you deposit. Confirm the full address on the explorer before you send it onward.

intro:
Swap WETH from Ethereum to ETH on Base. Wrapped ETH on Ethereum is the input, and native ETH on chain 8453 is what arrives.

This is not an unwrap. Unwrapping spends 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 and returns native ETH on Ethereum, which Etherscan shows as a gas balance. This route spends that same WETH contract and delivers native ETH on Base, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, which Basescan shows as the gas coin of chain id 8453. You still need ETH on chain id 1 to start. The ETH you receive can pay later fees on Base. It cannot pay the mainnet transaction. Blocks on Ethereum are about 12 seconds. The 0x4200 WETH predeploy is not the output. Read the native line on Basescan.
description: Swap WETH from Ethereum to ETH on Base when you need ETH for gas on chain 8453 and the source is wrapped ETH held on Ethereum mainnet today in your wallet.

sections.heading: Unwrap locally if you want mainnet ETH
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool for getting native ETH back on Ethereum. The WETH contract already has a withdraw function, and the ETH it returns stays on chain id 1. Open this page when a Base wallet needs its own ETH for gas. Those are different receipts, on different explorers.

sections.heading: WETH in, native ETH out
sections.body: You approve 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Etherscan. You watch the native line on Basescan, not an ERC-20. The placeholder 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE means ETH on chain id 8453 here. On Ethereum that same string would have meant the gas coin you are not receiving.

sections.heading: Gas to leave Ethereum
sections.body: Chain id 1 charges ETH and blocks about every 12 seconds. WETH cannot pay that. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is where the approval is signed. After arrival, the received ETH is the fee token on Base. Leave a remainder if you still need to move other tokens.

sections.heading: Not the WETH predeploy
sections.body: If a pool asks for 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006, this route delivered the gas coin instead. Switch outputs. A wallet still set to Ethereum will not show the Base ETH this pair sends.

faqs.question: If I want ETH, why not just unwrap?
faqs.answer: Unwrap when the ETH should be mainnet gas. Withdrawing from 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 stays on Ethereum. This route delivers native ETH on Base, chain id 8453, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. The ticker matches and the chain does not. Pick unwrap for chain id 1.

faqs.question: Will the received ETH pay Base fees?
faqs.answer: Yes. Native ETH is the gas token on chain id 8453. That is the reason to pick this output instead of the WETH predeploy. It will not pay the Ethereum fee that spent the WETH. Keep a little of the received ETH unspent for the next signature. Look on Basescan.

faqs.question: What should I approve?
faqs.answer: Only the WETH contract at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Etherscan. Keep native ETH for the mainnet gas. There is no destination token to import, because the output is the native balance. Switch the wallet to Base, chain id 8453, to see it.

Swap WBTC from Ethereum to USDC on Base. Holders of wrapped bitcoin who need Circle's native USDC on chain 8453 spend WBTC and receive that dollar.

WBTC is an ERC-20, not bitcoin on the Bitcoin chain. You approve 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 on Etherscan. It uses 8 decimals. A Bitcoin address cannot receive it. description: Swap WBTC from Ethereum to USDC on Base when you want Circle native USDC on chain 8453 and the source is wrapped bitcoin, an ERC-20, on Ethereum today.

sections.heading: Not a Bitcoin withdrawal
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool if the destination is a Bitcoin address. WBTC stays an Ethereum token until the route spends it, and the output is a dollar on Base. Redeeming WBTC for bitcoin, where a custodian allows it, does not use Basescan and does not pay 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913.

sections.heading: Eight decimals in, six out, and not USDbC
sections.body: Check 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 on Etherscan for the WBTC you spend. Check 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913 on Basescan for the native USDC. The bridged USDbC contract will not move. A mixed-up decimal field will invent the size of the balance.

sections.heading: ETH on both chains
sections.body: WBTC does not pay Ethereum gas. Keep ETH on chain id 1. Native USDC does not pay Base gas. Keep ETH on chain id 8453. [Base](/chains/base) is the network the dollars land on.

sections.heading: A mainnet sale is enough for mainnet dollars
sections.body: WBTC already trades against Circle USDC on Ethereum. Use that pool when the dollars should stay on chain id 1 as 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. This bridge is for a wallet that needs the Base native contract. Selling on mainnet never creates it.

faqs.question: Can the receiver be a Bitcoin address?
faqs.answer: No. The output is Circle's native USDC on Base, 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913. The input is WBTC at 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 on Etherscan, an ERC-20 with 8 decimals. Neither side is the Bitcoin network. Use an EVM address that can switch to chain id 8453.

faqs.question: Why does a small WBTC figure represent a large value?
faqs.answer: WBTC uses 8 decimals, so a fraction of one token is a meaningful amount of wrapped bitcoin. The USDC you receive is set by the quote you sign, which this page does not fix. Read the minimum on that quote. The native USDC then displays with 6 decimals on Basescan.

faqs.question: What do I hold besides WBTC?
faqs.answer: ETH on Ethereum, because chain id 1 will not take WBTC as a fee. ETH on Base after arrival, because native USDC will not pay chain id 8453. Blocks are about 12 seconds on the way out. Both ETH balances sit apart from the two token contracts.

intro:
Swap WBTC from Ethereum to ETH on Base. A chain 8453 wallet that needs gas can spend wrapped bitcoin on Ethereum and receive native ETH on Base.

WBTC at 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 is an 8 decimal ERC-20 on Etherscan, not a coin on the Bitcoin chain. Native ETH on Base is marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE and shows up as the gas balance on Basescan for chain id 8453. You approve the WBTC contract and pay that approval in ETH on Ethereum. Blocks there are about 12 seconds. You do not import the destination placeholder.
