description: Swap WBTC from Ethereum to ETH on Base when a chain 8453 wallet needs ETH for gas and the source is wrapped bitcoin, an ERC-20, on Ethereum mainnet today.

sections.heading: Base gas is the reason
sections.body: Wrapped bitcoin cannot pay a chain 8453 fee. If the next signature has to happen on Base, the wallet needs native ETH there. This pair turns WBTC you already hold on Ethereum into that gas coin. It is the wrong shape if you wanted USDC or WETH to arrive instead.

sections.heading: This never becomes a bitcoin send
sections.body: A Bitcoin address will not accept WBTC, and it will not accept Base ETH. Etherscan is where 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 decreases. Basescan is where the native ETH balance on chain id 8453 increases. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) describes that split.

sections.heading: Use the Ethereum pool when you are staying
sections.body: If you want ETH, WETH, USDC, or USDT on mainnet, sell WBTC there. This route is the wrong tool for those balances. If you already hold Base assets and only need a little ETH, swap those assets on chain 8453. Bridge from Ethereum when the wrapped bitcoin is still on mainnet.

sections.heading: Leave ETH for the next click
sections.body: The coin you receive is the fee token on Base, so it can pay a follow-up trade. Spending all of it strands any other token in the same wallet. The placeholder is not a contract to import.

faqs.question: Should I import the received ETH by contract?
faqs.answer: No. Native ETH on Base uses 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE and appears as the gas balance once the wallet is on chain id 8453. Importing that string creates a junk row. Confirm the increase on Basescan. The ERC-20 you approve is WBTC, on Etherscan.

faqs.question: What is WBTC if it is not bitcoin?
faqs.answer: An ERC-20 at 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599, 8 decimals, on Ethereum. This route can spend that contract. It cannot move coins on the Bitcoin network. If your goal is a Bitcoin wallet, stop. If your goal is ETH gas on Base funded from that ERC-20, this is the pair.

faqs.question: Why is ETH on Ethereum still required?
faqs.answer: Because the spend starts on chain id 1. WBTC cannot pay Ethereum gas, and the ETH you will receive on Base does not exist on Ethereum yet. Hold ETH for the approval and the send. Blocks are about 12 seconds. After arrival, that new ETH covers chain id 8453.

intro:
Swap WBTC from Ethereum to WETH on Base. Traders moving wrapped bitcoin into wrapped ETH on chain 8453 receive the Base WETH predeploy.

You spend WBTC at 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 on Etherscan, an 8 decimal ERC-20. You receive 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on Basescan. That is not mainnet WETH at 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2, and it is not bitcoin, and it is not native ETH. Chain id 1 gas is ETH, about 12 seconds a block. Chain id 8453 gas is a separate ETH balance, and this WETH cannot pay it. Switch to Base before you look. The predeploy will not appear in the Ethereum WETH row.
description: Swap WBTC from Ethereum to WETH on Base when you want the Base WETH predeploy and the source is the wrapped bitcoin ERC-20 on Ethereum mainnet in your wallet.

sections.heading: Two wrappers on two chains
sections.body: Selling WBTC for WETH on Ethereum would leave you in 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2. This route leaves you in the Base predeploy. It is the wrong tool for a Bitcoin-network withdrawal and the wrong tool for a mainnet WETH balance. Use it when the ETH book you want is on chain 8453.

sections.heading: Check the predeploy, not the native line
sections.body: Basescan must show 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006. The WBTC that decreases is 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 on Etherscan. Native ETH would have been the 0xEeee placeholder, and it is not the output. If your Ethereum ETH balance is what you wanted to grow, you opened the wrong pair.

sections.heading: Gas that neither wrapper can pay
sections.body: WBTC will not pay the Ethereum approval. Hold ETH on chain id 1. Base WETH will not pay the chain 8453 transfer. Hold ETH there too. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is only the starting side. The quote you sign is the amount you accept. This article does not publish a price.

sections.heading: When the source-chain pool is the better book
sections.body: Someone who wants to rotate WBTC into WETH without leaving Ethereum should stay on chain id 1, where both contracts already trade. The pool being on the source chain is the reason to skip the bridge. This pair is for a wallet that needs the Basescan predeploy specifically.

faqs.question: Is the WETH the Ethereum WETH contract?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum WETH is 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2 on Etherscan. This route pays 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 on Basescan. Native ETH is the gas coin on chain id 1 and, separately, on Base. The contract you can spend as WETH on chain 8453 is the predeploy.

faqs.question: Can this WBTC go to a Bitcoin address instead?
faqs.answer: Not on this route. WBTC at 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599 is an ERC-20 on Ethereum. The output is an ERC-20 on Base. Neither explorer is a Bitcoin explorer. If you need bitcoin on the Bitcoin chain, this pair is the wrong tool. Confirm the full address on the explorer before you send it onward.

faqs.question: What fails if the wallet holds only WBTC?
faqs.answer: The Ethereum transaction. Chain id 1 charges ETH, and WBTC cannot substitute. Add ETH before you approve 0x2260FAC5E5542a773Aa44fBCfeDf7C193bc2C599. On the far side, add ETH on Base or the WETH will be unable to move. Blocks on Ethereum are about 12 seconds.

intro:
Swap USDC from Ethereum to USDT on Avalanche C-Chain. Traders who need Tether on the C-Chain spend Circle USDC on Ethereum and receive that USDT.

This page is for a wallet on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114, not the X-Chain and not the P-Chain. You approve Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan, 6 decimals. You receive Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on Snowtrace. Ethereum Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 is not the credit. A mainnet pool already swaps these stables if both should stay on chain id 1. Gas to leave is ETH, and blocks there are about 12 seconds. Gas on the C-Chain is AVAX. The received USDT cannot pay it. Switch the wallet to the C-Chain and read Snowtrace. Switch to the C-Chain and match the Snowtrace USDT before you forward the payment.
description: Swap USDC from Ethereum to USDT on Avalanche C-Chain when a C-Chain wallet needs Tether and you already hold Circle USDC on Ethereum mainnet in your wallet.

sections.heading: A mainnet stable swap stays on mainnet
sections.body: Circle USDC and Tether already trade on Ethereum. This route is the wrong tool for that rotation. Open it when the Tether has to be the C-Chain contract. A same-chain swap never creates 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 and never moves the wallet onto chain id 43114.

sections.heading: Snowtrace is where this USDT lives
sections.body: Match 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 before you forward the funds. The approval on Etherscan is only 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. Circle's native USDC on the C-Chain, 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E, is a different dollar and is not this output.

sections.heading: ETH first, then AVAX
sections.body: Chain id 1 takes ETH. The C-Chain takes AVAX. An X-Chain or P-Chain address will not show this ERC-20. [Avalanche](/chains/avalanche) in this route means the C-Chain only. Keep AVAX on the receiving wallet or the Tether sits still.

sections.heading: Who wants this Tether
sections.body: Use it when a C-Chain app, invoice, or pool quotes this USDT contract. You hold Tether on chain id 43114, not a claim on the Ethereum USDC you spent. The quote you sign is the amount you accept.

faqs.question: Is C-Chain USDT the same contract as Ethereum USDT?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum Tether is 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan. This route pays 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on Snowtrace. Switch the wallet to Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114. The X-Chain and the P-Chain will not show this ERC-20. Match the full address before you spend it.

faqs.question: Does the USDT pay C-Chain gas?
faqs.answer: No. Gas on chain id 43114 is AVAX. USDT is an ERC-20. If the C-Chain wallet has no AVAX, the Tether can sit on Snowtrace until you add gas. The send on Ethereum also needs ETH, because Circle USDC cannot pay chain id 1. Blocks there are about 12 seconds.

faqs.question: What if I only wanted USDT on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: Sell Circle USDC for Tether on Ethereum and stop at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. This bridge is the wrong tool for that balance. Use it when a C-Chain address expects 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 and the dollars you hold are still Circle USDC on mainnet. Confirm the full address on the explorer before you send it onward.

intro:
Swap USDC from Ethereum to AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain. People who need AVAX for gas on the C-Chain spend Circle USDC on Ethereum and receive it.

Native AVAX is marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. On this route that placeholder is the gas coin Snowtrace shows for chain id 43114, not native ETH, and not an X-Chain or P-Chain balance. You send Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan. Keep ETH on Ethereum for the send. Mainnet blocks are about 12 seconds. The AVAX you receive can pay later transactions on the C-Chain. Do not import the placeholder as a custom token.
description: Swap USDC from Ethereum to AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain when a C-Chain wallet needs AVAX for gas and you will spend Circle USDC from Ethereum mainnet today.

sections.heading: C-Chain AVAX is the fee the next click needs
sections.body: A C-Chain wallet full of tokens still cannot move them without AVAX. This pair turns Circle dollars you already hold on Ethereum into that gas coin. It is a poor fit when you wanted a stablecoin to remain a stablecoin on chain 43114. The output is the native balance.

sections.heading: Not the X-Chain
sections.body: Leave 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE out of the custom token list. On Ethereum the same string means ETH. On this route it means AVAX on the C-Chain. An X-Chain or P-Chain address is a different system and will not show this balance. Read the native line on Snowtrace after you switch to chain id 43114.

sections.heading: The USDC approval stays on Etherscan
sections.body: Spend 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, Circle USDC, 6 decimals. Native USDC on the C-Chain at 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E is already there and is not the input. If your dollars are already on the C-Chain, swap them for AVAX there. This bridge is the wrong tool for that wallet.

sections.heading: ETH pays for the departure
sections.body: Chain id 1 charges ETH even though the coin you want is AVAX. [Avalanche](/chains/avalanche) here means the C-Chain, which collects AVAX only after you arrive. Leave some of the received AVAX unspent so the next approval can be mined.

faqs.question: Will this AVAX show up on the X-Chain?
faqs.answer: No. The output is native AVAX on the C-Chain, chain id 43114, marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Snowtrace shows that gas balance. The X-Chain and the P-Chain use different address styles and will not credit this route. Switch an EVM wallet to the C-Chain and read the native line.

faqs.question: Do I approve a contract for AVAX on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: You approve Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan. AVAX is not an Ethereum ERC-20 in this route. Keep ETH on chain id 1 for gas. Blocks are about 12 seconds. The USDC cannot pay that fee, and the AVAX you receive later cannot pay it either.

faqs.question: When should I skip this?
faqs.answer: When you want USDT or more USDC on Ethereum, or when you already hold a C-Chain token and only need AVAX. Buy AVAX on the C-Chain in that second case. This route is for Circle USDC that is still on Ethereum and a wallet that must hold C-Chain gas.

intro:
Swap USDT from Ethereum to USDC on Avalanche C-Chain. Wallets that need Circle's native USDC on the C-Chain spend Ethereum Tether and receive that dollar.

You send Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan, 6 decimals. You receive 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E on Snowtrace, Circle's native USDC on Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114. The older bridged USDC.e at 0xA7D7079b0FEaD91F3e65f86E8915Cb59c1a4C664 is a different contract and is not this output. The X-Chain and the P-Chain are the wrong networks. Gas to leave is ETH on Ethereum, about 12 seconds a block. Gas on the C-Chain is AVAX. The USDC cannot pay it. Import the native contract from Snowtrace before you deposit. Import native USDC from Snowtrace on chain id 43114. USDC.e will not move, and the X-Chain will not show the dollars at all. Confirm the native contract on Snowtrace before you deposit the dollars anywhere.
description: Swap USDT from Ethereum to USDC on Avalanche C-Chain for Circle's native USDC on the C-Chain, spent from Tether you already hold on Ethereum in your wallet.

sections.heading: Native USDC is not USDC.e
sections.body: C-Chain apps split the dollar. Circle's native token is 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E. Bridged USDC.e is 0xA7D7079b0FEaD91F3e65f86E8915Cb59c1a4C664. This route pays the native contract. If an allowlist prints the USDC.e address, these dollars will not credit. Read it on Snowtrace.

sections.heading: Tether is what leaves Ethereum
sections.body: Approve 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 only. That approval burns ETH on chain id 1. Circle USDC on Ethereum, 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, is not the token you send and not the token you receive.

sections.heading: Stay on Ethereum to flip the stable
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when both dollars should remain on mainnet. USDT and Circle USDC already have a chain id 1 book. Bridge when the receiving contract is native USDC on the C-Chain. [Avalanche](/chains/avalanche) in this pair means chain id 43114, where AVAX pays the fee.

sections.heading: AVAX after the dollar arrives
sections.body: The received USDC cannot pay gas. The C-Chain charges AVAX. Keep some on the destination wallet or the new dollars wait. An X-Chain address will not display this ERC-20.

faqs.question: Which USDC address should I watch on Avalanche?
faqs.answer: 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E on Snowtrace. That is Circle's native USDC on the C-Chain. USDC.e at 0xA7D7079b0FEaD91F3e65f86E8915Cb59c1a4C664 will not increase because of this route. Chain id 43114 is the network. The X-Chain will not show either contract. Confirm the full address on the explorer before you send it onward.

faqs.question: What do I approve on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan. Keep ETH in that wallet for gas on chain id 1. USDT cannot pay the fee, and the approval may be its own transaction. Blocks are about 12 seconds. The USDC appears only after you switch the wallet to the C-Chain.

faqs.question: Is this the same as USDT to USDC on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: The tickers match and the contracts do not. On Ethereum the USDC would be 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. This route delivers 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E. Use the mainnet pool when the dollars should stay on chain id 1. Use this page when the C-Chain is where the USDC has to sit.

intro:
Swap USDT from Ethereum to AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain. A C-Chain wallet short of gas spends Ethereum Tether and receives native AVAX.

Native AVAX uses 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. That placeholder is the gas coin on chain id 43114, shown on Snowtrace as a native balance, not an X-Chain balance. The token you approve is Tether, 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, on Etherscan. If your Tether is already the C-Chain contract at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7, swap it for AVAX there. This page starts from mainnet Tether and still needs ETH on chain id 1. Blocks there are about 12 seconds. Switch to the C-Chain to see the AVAX. Switch to the C-Chain and read the native AVAX line on Snowtrace. The X-Chain and the P-Chain will not show this balance. Confirm the native AVAX balance on Snowtrace after you switch the wallet to the C-Chain only.
description: Swap USDT from Ethereum to AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain when a C-Chain wallet needs AVAX for gas and you will spend Tether held on Ethereum mainnet today.

sections.heading: Already on the C-Chain? Swap there
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when the USDT is already at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. Trade that token for AVAX on chain 43114. Bridging from Ethereum moves 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. Check which explorer holds the Tether before you sign.

sections.heading: The placeholder means C-Chain AVAX
sections.body: Do not import 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. On this path it means AVAX. On an Ethereum path it means ETH. After the route, switch to chain id 43114 and read the native line on Snowtrace. The X-Chain and the P-Chain will not show it.

sections.heading: ETH for the Tether approval
sections.body: Chain id 1 charges ETH and blocks about every 12 seconds. Tether cannot substitute. [How to bridge assets between chains](/learn/guides/how-to-bridge-assets-between-chains) covers the source signature. The AVAX you receive can pay the next C-Chain transaction.

sections.heading: Leave AVAX for the follow-up
sections.body: If you spend the entire native balance on the next transfer, later token moves stall. Keep a remainder sized for an approval and a swap. This pair funds that remainder from Ethereum Tether.

faqs.question: I already hold USDT on the C-Chain. Should I use this page?
faqs.answer: No. This page starts from Ethereum Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan. USDT at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 can be swapped for AVAX on the C-Chain. Using this bridge would move a mainnet balance you may be leaving in place on purpose. Confirm the full address on the explorer before you send it onward.

faqs.question: Is 0xEeee an AVAX contract on Snowtrace?
faqs.answer: It is a placeholder for the native gas coin, not a contract to import. On chain id 43114 that coin is AVAX. Snowtrace shows it as the native balance. Importing the placeholder creates a useless row. The X-Chain is a different address system and is not this output.

faqs.question: What else belongs in the Ethereum wallet?
faqs.answer: Tether plus ETH. The USDT contract cannot pay gas on chain id 1, and blocks there are about 12 seconds. AVAX does not exist on Ethereum yet, so it cannot pay the fee either. Add a small ETH balance before you approve 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7.

intro:
Swap DAI from Ethereum to USDC on Avalanche C-Chain. Holders leaving Maker DAI for Circle's dollar on the C-Chain spend DAI and receive native USDC.

DAI is Maker's collateral dollar at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Etherscan, 18 decimals. The USDC you receive is 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E on Snowtrace, Circle's native USDC on chain id 43114, 6 decimals. Bridged USDC.e at 0xA7D7079b0FEaD91F3e65f86E8915Cb59c1a4C664 is not the receipt. You pay ETH on chain id 1, about 12 seconds a block. You later need AVAX on the C-Chain, because the USDC cannot pay gas. The X-Chain will not show this token. Import the native contract from Snowtrace or a wallet that only tracks USDC.e will look empty. Import the native USDC from Snowtrace after you switch to chain id 43114. USDC.e will look unchanged. Confirm it on Snowtrace.
description: Swap DAI from Ethereum to USDC on Avalanche C-Chain when you are leaving Maker DAI for Circle's native USDC that has to sit on the C-Chain in your wallet.

sections.heading: Watch native USDC, not USDC.e
sections.body: Snowtrace should show 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E. If you imported only 0xA7D7079b0FEaD91F3e65f86E8915Cb59c1a4C664, the wallet will look empty. Decimals also change, from 18 on Maker DAI to 6 on Circle's native USDC. Read both token pages before the next transfer.

sections.heading: The Maker contract is the approval
sections.body: 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F is the DAI that decreases. Circle USDC on Ethereum, 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, is what a mainnet DAI to USDC swap would pay. This route does not pay that contract.

sections.heading: Stay in DAI on Ethereum when that is the job
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool if you want Circle USDC on chain id 1 or if you want to remain in DAI. Both are mainnet actions. Bridge when a C-Chain app whitelisted the native USDC. [Avalanche](/chains/avalanche) here is chain id 43114, where AVAX then pays for using it.

sections.heading: AVAX after the decimal change
sections.body: ETH pays the Ethereum approval. AVAX pays any later move of the USDC. The USDC cannot sponsor that second fee. Hold AVAX on the C-Chain before you deposit the new dollars. Do not send them to an X-Chain address.

faqs.question: Does this give me Circle USDC on Ethereum?
faqs.answer: No. It spends Maker DAI and pays Circle's native USDC on the C-Chain, 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E on Snowtrace. Ethereum Circle USDC remains 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 on Etherscan. If that mainnet contract is what you wanted, trade DAI for it on chain id 1. Confirm the full address on the explorer before you send it onward.

faqs.question: Why can the USDC display look nothing like the DAI amount?
faqs.answer: DAI uses 18 decimals and C-Chain native USDC uses 6. A wrong decimal field shifts the display by many zeros. Check decimals on Snowtrace for 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E. Judge the trade by the quote you sign. This page does not set that quote.

faqs.question: What if the app listed USDC.e?
faqs.answer: Do not deposit this output there. USDC.e is 0xA7D7079b0FEaD91F3e65f86E8915Cb59c1a4C664. This route pays the native contract on the C-Chain, chain id 43114. Sending native USDC into a pool that wants the bridged token will not credit you. Match the allowlist, not the USDC ticker.

intro:
Swap DAI from Ethereum to USDT on Avalanche C-Chain. Someone paying Tether on the C-Chain can spend Maker DAI from Ethereum and receive that USDT.

You approve Maker DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Etherscan, 18 decimals. You receive Tether at 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on Snowtrace. Ethereum Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 does not increase. Issuers differ: Maker on the way out, Tether on the way in. The network is the C-Chain, chain id 43114, not the X-Chain. Gas to leave is ETH on chain id 1. Gas afterward is AVAX, and the USDT cannot pay it. Tell the payee to watch Snowtrace. An Etherscan tab will stay flat. The payee has to be on the C-Chain, watching Snowtrace, or the Tether is invisible. An Etherscan watch will not update, and an X-Chain address will not credit it. Confirm the USDT contract on Snowtrace before you pay.
description: Swap DAI from Ethereum to USDT on Avalanche C-Chain when a C-Chain wallet needs Tether and the source balance is Maker DAI on Ethereum mainnet in your wallet.

sections.heading: Snowtrace USDT is the payment asset
sections.body: Expect 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7. A payee who printed the Ethereum USDT address will not see this transfer on Etherscan. Tell them the network is Avalanche C-Chain, chain id 43114. An X-Chain address will not credit an ERC-20.

sections.heading: DAI for Ethereum Tether is a local swap
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when the invoice is on mainnet. Sell Maker DAI for 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 and stop. Bridge only when the Tether contract is the C-Chain one. A chain id 1 pool already covers the local job.

sections.heading: ETH out, AVAX in
sections.body: Chain id 1 blocks about every 12 seconds and charges ETH. DAI cannot pay it. The C-Chain charges AVAX. [How cross-chain bridges work](/learn/how-do-cross-chain-bridges-work) is why each chain keeps its own fee. The received USDT is an ERC-20 on Snowtrace.

sections.heading: Approve only the Maker contract
sections.body: 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F is the DAI this route can spend. Confirm it on Etherscan, then confirm the USDT string on Snowtrace after the wallet is on the C-Chain.

faqs.question: Will Ethereum USDT increase?
faqs.answer: No. Ethereum Tether stays at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 on Etherscan. The new tokens are 0x9702230a8ea53601f5cd2dc00fdbc13d4df4a8c7 on Snowtrace. Look there after you switch to the C-Chain, chain id 43114. The X-Chain will not list this contract. The address is how you tell the payment landed.

faqs.question: What gas do I need?
faqs.answer: ETH on Ethereum to spend the DAI, because chain id 1 charges ETH and blocks are about 12 seconds. AVAX on the C-Chain to move the USDT afterward. The route delivers neither gas coin. DAI is 18 decimals. Read the USDT decimals on Snowtrace before you forward the funds.

faqs.question: When should I sell DAI on Ethereum instead?
faqs.answer: When the recipient wants Tether at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7. That is a mainnet swap. This bridge is the wrong tool for that invoice. Open it when the invoice names the C-Chain contract and the DAI is still on Ethereum. Confirm the full address on the explorer before you send it onward.

intro:
Swap DAI from Ethereum to AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain. Wallets that need AVAX for gas on the C-Chain can spend Maker DAI held on Ethereum.

The output is native AVAX, written as 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE. Snowtrace shows that as the gas balance of chain id 43114, not an X-Chain balance. The input is Maker DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F on Etherscan. You still need ETH on chain id 1 to pay for the send. A local sale of DAI for ETH would leave the ETH on Ethereum, and that ETH cannot pay C-Chain fees. Mainnet blocks are about 12 seconds. Switch to the C-Chain and read the native line. Do not import the placeholder. Switch to the C-Chain and read the native line on Snowtrace. Confirm the native balance on Snowtrace.
description: Swap DAI from Ethereum to AVAX on Avalanche C-Chain when a C-Chain wallet needs AVAX for gas and the source balance is Maker DAI on Ethereum mainnet today.

sections.heading: C-Chain gas is the reason to open it
sections.body: Maker DAI on Ethereum cannot pay a C-Chain fee. If the next signature is on chain id 43114, the wallet needs AVAX. This pair converts DAI you already hold into that gas coin. It is the wrong shape if you wanted USDC or USDT to arrive instead.

sections.heading: The placeholder is the gas line
sections.body: Leave 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE out of the import list. On this route it means AVAX on the C-Chain. On Ethereum the same string means ETH. The X-Chain and the P-Chain are different systems. Read the native line on Snowtrace.

sections.heading: Approve DAI, pay mainnet ETH
sections.body: The contract that decreases is 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F. Confirm it on Etherscan. [Ethereum](/chains/ethereum) is where that fee is charged. The AVAX you receive cannot pay the transaction that creates it.

sections.heading: Skip the bridge when the pool is local
sections.body: If you want ETH, USDC, or USDT on Ethereum, swap DAI on mainnet. This route is the wrong tool for those balances. If you already hold a C-Chain stable and only need gas, swap that stable for AVAX on chain 43114.

faqs.question: Does the AVAX show up on the X-Chain?
faqs.answer: No. It shows up as the native gas balance on the C-Chain, chain id 43114. The address 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE is a stand-in, not a contract you import from Snowtrace. The X-Chain uses a different address format. Switch an EVM wallet to the C-Chain and read the gas line.

faqs.question: Can I start with only DAI?
faqs.answer: You need Maker DAI at 0x6B175474E89094C44Da98b954EedeAC495271d0F and you also need ETH on Ethereum. Chain id 1 charges ETH for the approval and the send. Blocks are about 12 seconds. DAI is the asset. ETH is the fee. AVAX is what you receive later and cannot pay the first transaction.

faqs.question: Is this how I turn DAI into mainnet ETH?
faqs.answer: No. Selling DAI for native ETH on Ethereum keeps the ETH on chain id 1. This route sells DAI for native AVAX on the C-Chain. Use it when chain 43114 gas is the gap. Skip it when the next trade is still on Ethereum.

intro:
Swap ETH from Ethereum to USDC on Avalanche C-Chain. You spend native ETH on Ethereum and a C-Chain wallet receives Circle's native USDC.

Native ETH is marked 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE, the gas coin Etherscan shows on chain id 1. You do not approve it. The dollar that arrives is 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E on Snowtrace. Bridged USDC.e at 0xA7D7079b0FEaD91F3e65f86E8915Cb59c1a4C664 is not the receipt. Leave ETH behind for the mainnet fee, because the coin you sell and the fee are the same balance. Blocks on Ethereum are about 12 seconds. The C-Chain, chain id 43114, charges AVAX, and the USDC cannot pay it. The X-Chain will not show the dollars. Import the native contract from Snowtrace after you switch. Import native USDC from Snowtrace on chain id 43114. USDC.e will not reflect this route. Confirm the native USDC on Snowtrace before you deposit.
description: Swap ETH from Ethereum to USDC on Avalanche C-Chain when you want Circle's native USDC on the C-Chain and you will spend native ETH from Ethereum today.

sections.heading: Leave ETH for the chain id 1 fee
sections.body: A max send can fail because nothing remains for gas. Lower the amount until the wallet still shows ETH on Ethereum. The USDC lands on the C-Chain and cannot refund that mainnet cost. This is not a transfer of ETH onto the X-Chain.

sections.heading: Native USDC, not USDC.e
sections.body: Watch 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E on Snowtrace. USDC.e at 0xA7D7079b0FEaD91F3e65f86E8915Cb59c1a4C664 does not move. Circle USDC on Ethereum, 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48, is also not the credit. [Avalanche](/chains/avalanche) here means chain id 43114.

sections.heading: A mainnet ETH sale stays home
sections.body: This route is the wrong tool when you want Circle USDC on Ethereum. That pool already exists on chain id 1. Use the bridge when a C-Chain app whitelisted the native contract. Selling ETH for dollars on mainnet never creates the Snowtrace balance.

sections.heading: AVAX after the dollars land
sections.body: Native USDC does not pay gas on the C-Chain. If the destination wallet has never held AVAX, the new dollars can show on Snowtrace and still be unable to move. Keep AVAX beside them.

faqs.question: Do I approve a contract for the ETH?
faqs.answer: No. Native ETH uses 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE as a placeholder, not a token you import. You sign a send on chain id 1. Keep enough ETH unspent to cover gas, because the amount and the fee come from the same balance. Etherscan shows that native balance falling.

faqs.question: Which USDC row should increase?
faqs.answer: The native one, 0xB97EF9Ef8734C71904D8002F8b6Bc66Dd9c48a6E on Snowtrace, on the C-Chain. USDC.e at 0xA7D7079b0FEaD91F3e65f86E8915Cb59c1a4C664 stays put. If the app lists the bridged address, this route delivers the wrong contract. Chain id 43114 is the network, not the X-Chain. Confirm the full address on the explorer before you send it onward.

faqs.question: When is an Ethereum swap enough?
faqs.answer: When the dollars should remain on chain id 1 as Circle USDC at 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48. This bridge is the wrong tool for that balance. Open it only if the next use of the money is on the C-Chain and the accepted contract is the native USDC.
